articles.title: The House Of Suntory’s Hibiki Puts Japanese Artistry At The Heart Of Bartender Creativity For 2026
articles.titleKo: The House Of Suntory’s Hibiki Puts Japanese Artistry At The Heart Of Bartender Creativity For 2026
articles.originalSummary: For two months only, 24 leading bars and restaurants will transform Japanese craftsmanship into original Hibiki Japanese Harmony cocktails This autumn, The House of Suntory’s Hibiki will put Japanese craftsmanship at the heart of bartender creativity with 24 Moments of Artistry: a limited-edition Hibiki Japanese Harmony cocktail programme bringing original Hibiki Japanese Harmony cocktails to 24 leading bars and restaurants across the UK. From 1 October to 30 November 2026, bartenders across the UK will transform four Japanese craft disciplines – Mokkō woodcraft, Yakimono ceramics, Senshoku textiles and Washi Japanese papermaking into original Hibiki Japanese Harmony cocktails. Hibiki’s iconic 24-faceted bottle represents the 24 traditional Japanese seasonal periods, or sekki, and the relationship between nature, time and craftsmanship. The ‘24 Moments of Artistry’ programme brings that philosophy to life through the creativity and interpretation of bartenders across the UK. Bartenders were challenged to interpret the precision, patience, balance and respect for materials associated with Japanese craftsmanship through flavour, texture, aroma, technique and presentation. The cocktails were developed following an immersive day at Japan House, London, exploring Japanese craftsmanship. Participating bartenders experienced vintage kimono and textile storytelling, traditional Japanese printmaking, ancient ceramics and a hands-on woodworking workshop. The experience was led by the House of Suntory UK Senior Brand Ambassador Raffaele Di Monaco, who also leads the House of Suntory DOJO Advocacy Programme, which introduces UK bartenders to the skills and philosophy behind Japanese bartending, hospitality and craftsmanship. Raffaele Di Monaco, House of Suntory UK Senior Brand Ambassador, said: “We wanted to challenge bartenders to think beyond ingredients and ask what craftsmanship actually means when translated into a drink. Whether that is the precision of woodworking, the layering of textiles, the relationship between vessel and liquid in ceramics, or the delicacy of washi paper, each discipline offers a different way to think about balance, technique and hospitality.” Cocktail Highlights include: Waltz, London — 翠白磁 Verdant Porcelain: Inspired by Japanese ceramics and the country’s ever-changing seasons, this elegant Hibiki serve is a celebration of nature and craftsmanship. Silky Shiro-An, ripe fig and floral, gently smoky tonka bean come together to evoke fine white porcelain, late-summer landscapes and the warmth of the potter’s kiln – all beautifully complementing Hibiki’s refined character. Speak In Code, Manchester — Hinoki 5: Inspired by Japanese woodworking, this innovative take on a Manhattan follows a craftsman’s day, from morning tea to evening drink. Spirit forward, it balances bright citrus with delicate herbal aromas, subtle roasted tea and a gentle warming spice. Smooth and elegant. The American Bar at Gleneagles Hotel, Edinburgh — Unetsubo: Inspired by Japanese ceramics and the beauty of imperfection, this Hibiki cocktail takes its cue from the unique scorch marks created by the intense heat of the kiln. In a playful Scottish twist, the idea is reimagined through the country’s well-fired rolls, with bread and Champagne transformed into a rich, toasted syrup – resulting in a soft, round and Hibiki forward cocktail with pear and toasted pastry notes. Served in a bespoke glass inspired by Unetsubo ceramics, it’s a distinctive meeting of Japanese artistry and Scottish character. Nathan Craig, Bar Manager at Dinings SW3, said: “When I learned about Japanese woodworking, what stood out wasn’t just the craftsmanship; it was the philosophy behind it. Every piece has a purpose, and the beauty comes from how they’re brought together. That’s exactly how I approached my cocktail, building layers of flavour that allow Hibiki Harmony to remain at the centre while revealing something new with every sip.” The focus on Japanese artist

articles.title: Urban abre loja temporária no JK Iguatemi e chega ao Mata Lab em dezembro
articles.titleKo: Urban abre loja temporária no JK Iguatemi e chega ao Mata Lab em dezembro
articles.originalSummary: A Urban, marca da Aramis., inaugura nesta quarta-feira, 25, uma loja temporária no JK Iguatemi, em São Paulo. Com 53,5 m², o espaço funcionará por seis meses e será a oitava unidade própria da marca. Em dezembro, a marca prevê iniciar uma operação no Mata Lab, ampliando sua presença na capital paulista. A abertura no JK Iguatemi faz parte da estratégia de aproximar a marca de consumidores do segmento premium e testar novos pontos de contato com o público. Durante o período de funcionamento, a empresa pretende acompanhar a aceitação dos produtos, os hábitos de compra e a entrada de novos clientes. Os resultados deverão orientar as próximas decisões de expansão. “A experimentação é central para a Urban. É ao vestir que o consumidor percebe, no toque, no caimento e na funcionalidade, a tecnologia incorporada às peças. O JK nos aproxima de um público com grande afinidade com a proposta da marca e nos permite transformar essa experiência em relacionamento”, afirma Juliana D’Auria, diretora de Marca e Marketing de Aramis Inc. O espaço foi projetado pela Vimer e segue o conceito arquitetônico e de visual merchandising apresentado na loja da Urban no Morumbi Shopping , inaugurada em 2025. Com uma área de vendas ocupa 44,27 m², a loja reúne 63 modelos em 136 combinações de cor em 12 categorias, dentre elas camisetas, polos, camisas, calças e calças de alfaiataria, bermudas, paletós, tricôs, jaquetas, calçados e acessórios. Os preços variam de R$ 199,90 a R$ 5.999,90. Entre os produtos estão peças com recursos de tecnologia têxtil. O portfólio também inclui jaquetas e peças de alfaiataria. “O JK Iguatemi é uma referência em moda, design e inovação, os mesmos territórios que orientam a construção da Urban. Levamos para lá a nossa nova linguagem de forma integrada à experiência, para que o cliente perceba no toque e no caimento o que significa built to elevate”, afirma Juliana. A Urban trabalha com o conceito de elevated smartwear, que combina tecidos tecnológicos e design em roupas para diferentes situações da rotina. A proposta é levar recursos como controle térmico, gestão de umidade e facilidade de manutenção para além do vestuário esportivo, incluindo o ambiente de trabalho e os deslocamentos urbanos. Novos canais Já a entrada no Mata Lab, prevista para dezembro, amplia a atuação da marca para além dos shopping centers e coloca a marca em contato com um público que circula por diferentes segmentos do mercado criativo. Localizado no Cidade Matarazzo, no bairro da Bela Vista, o espaço reúne mais de 200 marcas nacionais e internacionais de moda, beleza e design. Imagem: Divulgação O post Urban abre loja temporária no JK Iguatemi e chega ao Mata Lab em dezembro apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Preço de venda não é consequência: como o design-to-cost muda o jogo no varejo de moda
articles.titleKo: Preço de venda não é consequência: como o design-to-cost muda o jogo no varejo de moda
articles.originalSummary: Em setembro de 2026, a Hering surpreendeu o varejo de moda ao reduzir em quase 30% o preço de seu item mais emblemático, a camiseta básica, de R$ 69,90 para R$ 49,99, sem abrir mão da margem. Para chegar a esse resultado, a companhia conduziu um projeto de dez meses que envolveu mais de 50 profissionais e centenas de simulações e amostras. Na prática, reestruturou sua gestão em torno do custo-objetivo, tornando a peça atrativa para o consumidor sem comprometer a rentabilidade do negócio. Enquanto parte do mercado ainda tenta defender resultados pressionando fornecedores ou remarcando preços, esse movimento da Hering mostrou que a rentabilidade de uma coleção se decide muito antes de a peça chegar às lojas. Para quem lidera o desenvolvimento de produto e compras no varejo de moda, a questão central deixou de ser como negociar melhor o custo e passou a ser como projetar a peça para o preço que o cliente aceita pagar. Precificar multiplicando o custo por um markup objetivo se tornou uma armadilha. Quando uma marca desenvolve a peça primeiro e faz a conta depois, perde nos dois extremos: ou o produto chega à loja caro demais para a percepção do público ou chega barato demais e deixa margem na mesa. Na prática do varejo de moda, um bom gerente de produto olha para a peça e já sabe exatamente quanto o seu consumidor está disposto a pagar por ela. Esse princípio, que resume o conceito de Good Value for Money (Bom Custo-Benefício), exige entregar atributos tangíveis que façam o cliente sentir que o gasto valeu a pena, em vez de empurrar ineficiências para o preço de venda. Quando a conta não fecha no modelo tradicional, a solução mais comum é tentar salvar o resultado na negociação com o fornecedor ou esperar que o time comercial resolva o problema com promoções (markdown) lá na frente. O método design-to-cost inverte essa ordem. Em vez de descobrir o custo no final do processo, a equipe define três premissas antes de iniciar o desenvolvimento: o preço final aceito pelo mercado, a margem necessária para remunerar a operação e o custo-limite permitido para produzir aquela peça. Desta forma, o preço deixa de ser consequência e passa a ser o ponto de partida de todo o processo. Há muito espaço para ganhar margem no desenvolvimento sem empobrecer o produto aos olhos de quem compra. O segredo está em diferenciar o que o cliente realmente percebe do que é apenas custo oculto no processo: um ajuste fino na gramatura da malha pode reduzir o peso da matéria-prima mantendo exatamente o mesmo toque, qualidade e durabilidade; o desenvolvimento de tecidos com larguras específicas para melhorar o encaixe elimina desperdícios que custam caro na escala; até detalhes aparentemente pequenos, como substituir etiquetas internas tecidas por estampas diretas na peça ou enxugar o excesso de tags, cortam despesas sem tirar o valor percebido pelo consumidor. O movimento em direção à metodologia design-to-cost também muda a relação com a cadeia de fornecimento, trazendo o parceiro para desenvolver o produto em conjunto com a marca. Havendo previsibilidade de volume e metas claras de custo, o fornecedor ganha eficiência na compra de insumos e na ocupação da produção, construindo rentabilidade saudável para os dois lados. É importante ressaltar que nada disso funciona se estilo, compras, planejamento e engenharia têxtil continuarem trabalhando de forma isolada. Quando o estilista desenvolve sem meta de custo e o comprador negocia sem visão de produto, essa dinâmica pode gerar excesso de estoque e queima de margem nas liquidações de fim de estação. Integrar essas áreas sob indicadores comuns transforma o design, que deixa de ser uma etapa puramente estética para se tornar uma ferramenta estratégica. Como costumo dizer desde o início da minha carreira, margem no vestuário não se salva na negociação com o fornecedor nem na remarcação da loja; ela se constrói na inteligência técnica com que cada produto é concebido. articles.title: Black Friday: Shopee reúne cinco dicas para fazer compras online com mais segurança
articles.titleKo: Black Friday: Shopee reúne cinco dicas para fazer compras online com mais segurança
articles.originalSummary: A Shopee, marketplace que conecta consumidores, reúne cinco orientações para comprar com mais segurança na Black Friday, em 27 de novembro: conferir a reputação do vendedor, manter pagamentos e conversas dentro do aplicativo, entender a Garantia Shopee, verificar o anúncio e acompanhar o pedido pelos canais oficiais. Em 2026, a data deve movimentar R$ 13,3 bilhões no e-commerce brasileiro entre 26 e 29 de novembro, alta de 20,7%, segundo projeção da Confi Neotrust. Pesquisa interna da Shopee sobre intenção de compra para a Temporada de Compras 2026 indica que 86% dos consumidores entrevistados pretendem comprar na Black Friday, com intenção de gasto de R$ 764 na data, 20% acima da pesquisa de 2025. Em um período de maior movimentação, a Shopee também reforça as orientações de segurança aos consumidores. Entre os cuidados estão verificar a reputação dos vendedores, consultar as avaliações e realizar pagamentos exclusivamente pelos canais disponibilizados no aplicativo. “Recursos como a Garantia Shopee, o chat oficial e o selo de Loja Oficial fazem parte das ferramentas que a plataforma oferece. Separamos essas dicas para que o consumidor tenha uma experiência de compra ainda mais segura e agradável”, afirma Felipe Piringer, diretor de Marketing da Shopee. Para ajudar o consumidor a aproveitar esses recursos, a plataforma reúne a seguir cinco orientações para a Black Friday : 1. Confira a reputação do vendedor antes de comprar Antes de concluir uma compra, é importante consultar as informações disponíveis sobre o vendedor. Na Shopee, os consumidores podem verificar avaliações de outros compradores, comentários sobre os produtos, histórico de vendas e classificação das lojas. A plataforma conta ainda com identificações específicas para determinadas lojas. O selo de Loja Oficial permite reconhecer marcas e operações autorizadas que integram a seção de grandes marcas. Já a identificação de Vendedor Indicado destaca lojas que atendem a critérios estabelecidos pela plataforma. Essas informações podem ser consultadas antes da finalização do pedido e ajudam o consumidor a avaliar diferentes opções de compra. 2. Mantenha pagamentos e conversas dentro da plataforma Durante períodos promocionais, o consumidor deve prestar atenção aos canais utilizados para negociar e pagar suas compras. A orientação da Shopee é que todo o processo seja realizado dentro da plataforma. O pagamento deve ser concluído exclusivamente pelas opções apresentadas no checkout. Solicitações de transferência bancária, Pix ou qualquer outra forma de pagamento fora da plataforma devem ser desconsideradas e denunciadas. O mesmo cuidado vale para a comunicação com os vendedores. O chat oficial da Shopee permite esclarecer dúvidas sobre produtos, disponibilidade, características e andamento dos pedidos, mantendo o histórico das conversas registrado na plataforma. Caso um vendedor solicite que a negociação seja transferida para aplicativos de mensagens, redes sociais ou outros canais externos, o consumidor pode utilizar as ferramentas de denúncia disponíveis na Shopee. 3. Entenda como funciona a Garantia Shopee A Garantia Shopee é um dos mecanismos de proteção disponibilizados pela plataforma. Por meio desse recurso, o pagamento realizado pelo consumidor fica retido até que sejam atendidas as condições previstas para sua liberação ao vendedor. O sistema permite que o consumidor acompanhe o pedido e, quando necessário, solicite devolução ou reembolso conforme as regras e os prazos aplicáveis à compra. Para utilizar os mecanismos de proteção, é importante acompanhar as notificações e os prazos apresentados no aplicativo. 4. articles.title: O que o Brasil pode aprender com a Coreia do Sul? Seis lições de uma potência global para o varejo
articles.titleKo: O que o Brasil pode aprender com a Coreia do Sul? Seis lições de uma potência global para o varejo
articles.originalSummary: A transformação da Coreia do Sul em uma das principais referências globais de tecnologia, inovação e consumo não aconteceu por acaso. O desenvolvimento do país está associado a investimentos em educação, planejamento de longo prazo e uma articulação entre governo, empresas e instituições de ensino que ajudou a construir indústrias competitivas internacionalmente. Essa foi uma das principais conclusões da live “Made in Korea: razões da transformação em benchmark global”, realizada nesta segunda-feira, 23, pela Mercado&Consumo e pela Gouvêa & Spheria Trade Missions . O encontro reuniu Marcos Gouvêa, fundador e diretor-geral do Gouvêa Ecosystem e publisher da Mercado&Consumo ; Eduardo Komatsu, representante na Coreia do Sul da Invest Paraná; e Suk Jung Kwon, consultor e pesquisador independente e sócio-fundador da IDEA Consultoria e Marketing. A mediação foi de Aiana Freitas, editora-executiva da Mercado&Consumo. Ao longo da conversa, os especialistas relacionaram a trajetória econômica sul-coreana a práticas que podem ser adaptadas à realidade brasileira, especialmente no varejo, na indústria de beleza, na logística e na gestão de negócios. Confira seis dos principais aprendizados do encontro. 1. Educação e cultura de responsabilidade são bases da transformação A educação foi apontada pelos participantes como um dos fundamentos do desenvolvimento sul-coreano. Eduardo Komatsu destacou o elevado nível de escolaridade da população e a importância atribuída pelas famílias à formação dos jovens. Um exemplo apresentado foi o Suneung, exame nacional de acesso ao ensino superior. No dia da prova, a sociedade se mobiliza para reduzir congestionamentos e ruídos que possam prejudicar os estudantes, inclusive com apoio policial para aqueles que correm o risco de chegar atrasados. Suk Jung Kwon relacionou esse comportamento a uma cultura de responsabilidade coletiva, respeito às regras e preocupação com o bem comum. Na avaliação de Marcos Gouvêa, esses hábitos também ajudam a explicar a eficiência observada em diferentes atividades econômicas do país, da mobilidade urbana ao funcionamento dos serviços. A principal lição para o Brasil é que o avanço tecnológico não depende apenas de investimentos em equipamentos e sistemas, mas também da formação das pessoas e da capacidade de organização das instituições. 2. Planejamento de longo prazo conecta governo, empresas e universidades Outro aspecto destacado foi a maneira como a Coreia do Sul organiza suas prioridades de desenvolvimento econômico. Segundo os participantes, o país construiu uma tradição de planejamento que articula governo, setor privado, academia e instituições financeiras em torno de objetivos de longo prazo. Suk Jung Kwon citou os planos quinquenais e a participação de diferentes setores na definição de prioridades, investimentos e responsabilidades. Como exemplo recente, mencionou iniciativas de planejamento voltadas à inteligência artificial e à robótica. Marcos Gouvêa apontou a necessidade de o Brasil fortalecer essa articulação. “Só nos falta atitude e nos falta uma integração entre setor privado, sociedade e governo para caminharmos num projeto de mais longo prazo, mais estratégico”, afirmou. Para as empresas brasileiras, a discussão reforça a importância de combinar capacidade de execução com planejamento contínuo, em vez de depender exclusivamente de respostas às demandas imediatas do mercado. 3. O varejo físico precisa oferecer motivos para o consumidor sair de casa Com elevada conectividade e um mercado de comércio eletrônico desenvolvido, o varejo sul-coreano enfrenta um desafio semelhante ao de outros países: convencer consumidores acostumados à conveniência digital a frequentar lojas físicas. Marcos Gouvêa destacou que a participação do comércio eletrônico nas vendas do varejo sul-coreano está entre as maiores do mundo, em torno de 25%, conforme as referências apresentadas durante a live. articles.title: Hotpot, dim sum, Japanese: favourite Hong Kong restaurants of a health-conscious chef
articles.titleKo: Hotpot, dim sum, Japanese: favourite Hong Kong restaurants of a health-conscious chef
articles.originalSummary: Chef Hilda Leung is also a culinary and nutrition consultant, and recently worked with Hotel Icon’s Green restaurant to redesign a healthier and more locally sourced menu with chef de cuisine Don Wong. articles.title: Outlet Exagerado volta ao Rio com expectativa de R$ 30 milhões em vendas
articles.titleKo: Outlet Exagerado volta ao Rio com expectativa de R$ 30 milhões em vendas
articles.originalSummary: O outlet Exagerado retorna ao Rio de Janeiro entre 9 e 13 de dezembro para sua segunda edição na cidade. Realizado no Riocentro, no Pavilhão 2, o outlet reunirá mais de 60 marcas de diferentes segmentos, com descontos de até 90%. A expectativa é movimentar R$ 30 milhões em vendas. A entrada é gratuita. Entre as marcas previstas, estão Adidas, Nike, Lacoste, Arezzo, Aramis, Oakley, L’Occitane au Brésil, Reserva, Samsung, Stanley, Guess, John John, Osklen, Youcom e Approve. O evento terá produtos de categorias como moda, calçados, acessórios, beleza e tecnologia. Uma das ofertas já confirmadas é da Chilli Beans, que venderá óculos de R$ 599,98 por R$ 129,98, com desconto de 70%. A proposta é reunir marcas conhecidas e condições especiais de compra em um único espaço. Para Victor de Castro, CEO do Exagerado, a segunda edição representa um novo momento de expansão do evento na capital fluminense. Na estreia no Rio , foram mais de R$ 25 milhões em vendas, 80 mil visitantes, 50 marcas participantes e 2,5 mil empregos gerados. Para dezembro, a organização projeta crescimento de 30% no número de marcas e de 20% no público e nas vendas. Entre as novidades desta edição está uma dinâmica de gamificação. Os visitantes poderão acumular pontos por meio de pesquisas de satisfação, respondidas em totens no local, e de compras nas lojas participantes. Cada pesquisa garante 100 pontos. Já as compras rendem pontuações conforme o segmento: 30 pontos para lojas de roupas, 45 para calçados e 60 para eletrônicos. Ao acumular mais de 200 pontos na carteira digital, o visitante poderá trocar a pontuação por brindes na Juquita, loja oficial do evento, localizada na entrada. Entre as opções estão cangas, leques, salva-celulares, mini trenas, suportes para celular e ecocopos. A programação do outlet Exagerado no Rio de Janeiro também terá música ao vivo e apresentações de fanfarra em todos os dias. No domingo, 13 de dezembro, será realizada a tradicional Xepa, quando os expositores oferecem produtos com condições diferenciadas. Serviço – Exagerado Data: 9 a 12 de dezembro, das 10h às 22h; 13 de dezembro, das 10h às 20h. Local: Riocentro – Pavilhão 2. Endereço: Avenida Salvador Allende, 6555, Barra Olímpica, Rio de Janeiro (RJ). Entrada: Gratuita. Formas de pagamento: Pix, dinheiro e cartão de crédito, diretamente nas lojas. articles.title: Lula sanciona ajuste fiscal aprovado no Congresso
articles.titleKo: Lula sanciona ajuste fiscal aprovado no Congresso
articles.originalSummary: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sancionou nesta terça-feira (24) a lei que prevê ajuste fiscal nas contas públicas em 2027. O texto muda as regras fiscais para permitir ao Executivo limitar a execução de despesas a fim de alcançar as metas de superávit primário a partir de 2027. O texto passou pelo Senado na semana passada e foi aprovado pela Câmara na madrugada desta terça-feira . O texto aprovado prevê um superávit de cerca de R$ 18,7 bilhões no ano que vem. Ajuste fiscal A lei prevê medidas para reduzir despesas e ampliar a arrecadação, com economia estimada entre R$ 45,1 bilhões e R$ 56,1 bilhões em 2027. A projeção considera tanto o aumento da arrecadação quanto o controle das despesas e se refere ao chamado resultado primário, a diferença entre o que o governo arrecada e o que gasta antes do pagamento dos juros da dívida. Entre os itens do texto está uma mudança no arcabouço fiscal para permitir ao governo fazer bloqueios adicionais de despesas para alcançar a meta fiscal e, a partir do ano que vem, reduzir de 2,5% para 2% o limite de crescimento dos gastos acima da inflação nos anos em que forem adotadas medidas de contenção. Com informações de Agência Brasil Imagem: Agência Brasil O post Lula sanciona ajuste fiscal aprovado no Congresso apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Justiça dá 72 horas à 99Food para comprovar fim de cláusulas de banimento
articles.titleKo: Justiça dá 72 horas à 99Food para comprovar fim de cláusulas de banimento
articles.originalSummary: O Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo (TJSP) deu à 99Food o prazo de 72 horas para a empresa de entrega de refeições comprovar que retirou de seus contratos com restaurantes as cláusulas que impediam os estabelecimentos de trabalhar com a Keeta, braço internacional da Meituan e estreante no segmento no Brasil. No fim de setembro, o TJSP considerou ilegais as chamadas “cláusulas de banimento” e determinou a sua remoção imediata dos contratos. Apesar da decisão judicial, a Keeta acusou a concorrente de alteração nos contratos com restaurantes parceiros para substituir cláusulas que baniam expressamente a empresa por uma nova redação que, embora formulada sob aparente neutralidade, produziria o mesmo efeito prático de exclusão da concorrente do mercado. Por seu turno, a 99 disse estar evoluindo seus contratos com restaurantes parceiros para aperfeiçoar as condições de exclusividade parcial já praticadas pela companhia. No julgamento no TJSP, o relator, desembargador Rômolo Russo, avaliou que as cláusulas direcionadas contra a Keeta ultrapassam uma exclusividade comercial legítima e passam a funcionar como mecanismo direcionado de bloqueio à entrada de um concorrente no mercado. “O princípio constitucional da livre iniciativa, emanado da livre concorrência, garante às empresas a plena liberdade para engendrar as suas estratégias. No entanto, convém fazer entender que as empresas não podem tudo. Podem quase tudo. Podem tudo aquilo que não venha a ferir a lei vigente e o senso normal de funcionamento concorrencial do mercado”, disse. Segundo a Keeta, as mudanças feitas pela 99Food foram identificadas em pelo menos 45 contratos. A empresa usou prints de WhatsApp que mostrariam que donos de restaurantes foram ainda levados a acreditar que, apesar da decisão do TJSP, o contrato anterior e, portanto, o banimento à Keeta, continuaria valendo. Agora, a 99Food deve prestar contas formalmente das medidas de cumprimento determinadas pela Justiça , sob o risco de multa de R$ 100 mil por contrato em descumprimento. Procurada, a 99Food não se manifestou. articles.title: Quase 38% das PMEs esperam aumentar vendas na Black Friday, aponta Serasa
articles.titleKo: Quase 38% das PMEs esperam aumentar vendas na Black Friday, aponta Serasa
articles.originalSummary: Quase quatro em cada dez pequenas e médias empresas (PMEs) esperam aumentar as vendas com ações para a Black Friday de 2026. É o que aponta um levantamento da Serasa Experian, segundo o qual 37,6% dos negócios projetam crescimento no período. Entre as empresas otimistas, 18,5% esperam alta de até 10% nas vendas, enquanto 10,5% projetam crescimento entre 10% e 30%. Outros 8,6% acreditam que as ações para a data podem impulsionar as vendas em mais de 30%. Apesar das expectativas, as PMEs enfrentam obstáculos para aproveitar a oportunidade. A limitação de orçamento e os custos elevados para investir em campanhas são o principal desafio, citados por 30,8% das empresas. Na sequência aparecem a concorrência com outros negócios (23,6%), a dificuldade para alcançar o público certo (23,1%) e a cautela dos consumidores em relação aos gastos (22,6%). “Participar da Black Friday exige mais do que oferecer descontos. Para uma PME, é fundamental avaliar se a ação faz sentido para o negócio, quanto pode ser investido e qual retorno é necessário para preservar a saúde financeira da empresa”, afirma Leticia Muzzi, diretora de Pequenas e Médias Empresas da Serasa Experian. Planejamento para a Black Friday Para apoiar os empreendedores na preparação para a data, a Serasa Experian disponibiliza gratuitamente um checklist com 13 orientações. O material reúne recomendações sobre finanças, dados, estoque, marketing, tecnologia, segurança, logística, atendimento e pós-venda. Entre os cuidados indicados, estão a definição de metas, a organização do fluxo de caixa, a revisão de estoques e fornecedores, o cálculo de preços e margens e o planejamento dos canais de divulgação. A empresa também recomenda testar a capacidade de atendimento e entrega para evitar gargalos durante o aumento da demanda. O checklist está disponível no portal de conteúdo da Serasa Experian . A pesquisa ouviu 1.072 pequenas e médias empresas de todo o Brasil em outubro de 2026, com predominância de negócios dos setores de comércio e serviços e empresas de pequeno porte. As perguntas sobre os principais desafios para aproveitar a Black Friday foram respondidas apenas pelas empresas que afirmaram pretender realizar ações no período. articles.title: Inside Farrelli’s Pizza’s Strategy for Building a Smarter Marketing Tech Stack
articles.titleKo: Inside Farrelli’s Pizza’s Strategy for Building a Smarter Marketing Tech Stack
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Farrelli’s Pizza uses technology to attract new guests and build loyalty. For restaurant marketers, the technology conversation has become impossible to separate from the larger business conversation. Customer data, loyalty, online ordering, delivery marketplaces, AI, streaming platforms—the list of tools and challenges keeps expanding, often faster than operators can determine what is truly useful. Clayton Krueger has watched that evolution from a particularly grounded perspective. A partner and chief marketing officer at Farrelli’s Pizza, a 14-unit full-service regional restaurant group headquartered in DuPont, Washington, Krueger started with the company as a dishwasher in 1997. He has now held the top marketing role for 19 years, giving him a long view of how technology has reshaped both the guest relationship and the marketer’s job. “It’s hard to choose just one,” Krueger says when asked about the biggest change at the intersection of marketing and technology during his career. Restaurants, he notes, were relatively late adopters in the broader technology landscape. But over the past decade-plus, the industry has dealt with a steady stream of consequential changes: social media, loyalty and customer relationship management (CRM) platforms, online ordering, third-party delivery, customer data platforms (CDPs), and, more recently, AI embedded seemingly everywhere. Of those, Krueger sees third-party delivery as the most disruptive marketing technology shift in the business. “Third-party delivery gets a bad rap because of the high fees, disconnected guest experience, and non-owned customer data for the restaurant,” he says. “But despite those challenges, never before has there been a marketing technology in our industry that so clearly connects hungry prospects directly with our restaurant solutions.” That framing gets to the heart of how Farrelli’s thinks about delivery. The marketplace isn’t simply a margin issue or a channel to tolerate because guests expect it. It is also a powerful acquisition engine, one that can put the brand in front of consumers at the precise point they are looking to make a purchase. The harder work comes after that first transaction. “It is up to us as operators then to figure out how to use that technology to our advantage,” Krueger says. At Farrelli’s, that means pairing third-party delivery with a strong first-party loyalty and online-ordering app that offers a more cost-effective delivery option. The company’s marketing focus, in turn, is on converting third-party users into first-party guests. Rather than treating the marketplace relationship as an endpoint, the team sees it as an introduction. That emphasis on creating a fuller picture of the guest has also made customer data platforms increasingly valuable. For years, restaurant marketers largely worked from the information available inside their CRM systems, which often meant the customer relationship began when a guest enrolled in loyalty. That is useful information, but it is not the entire customer journey. CDPs help close that gap. “We are learning through our tool how to better understand the customer journey and impactful points within it, in ways that we have not previously been able to,” Krueger says. Farrelli’s can now identify the first instance of a visit and track a customer based on payment method, rather than only seeing the moment that customer joins the loyalty database. It gives marketers the ability to examine behavior at both the broad and granular levels—understanding larger guest patterns while also seeing more specific interactions along the way. “These new tools can show you the holistic picture of the customer at both a macro scale and micro details,” Krueger says. articles.title: Savvy Sliders Looks to Turn Rising Demand into Nationwide Growth
articles.titleKo: Savvy Sliders Looks to Turn Rising Demand into Nationwide Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Savvy Sliders has over 50 restaurants. The restaurant industry continues to trudge through a tricky economic environment, but consumer demand is there for Savvy Sliders, according to Happy Group COO Sonny Asker. “Our portal blows up all day with different customers in different markets, asking, ‘Hey, when are we going to bring a Savvy Sliders here,’ or when is this Savvy going to go in North Carolina or wherever it may be,” Asker says. “We’re starting to form a really big following for the brand, and I think just the slider category is expanding in general as well.” After eight years of growth, the concept, founded in Commerce Township, Michigan, operates more than 50 locations in Michigan, Ohio, Texas, Louisiana, Florida, Indiana, and Mississippi. On top of that, the brand has more than 50 units in development or under franchise agreements. Some of the newer markets on the horizon include Oregon, Kentucky, Illinois, Nevada, and New York. Asker says the brand will open four more locations before the end of the year, depending on construction and permitting timelines. That would be about one store opening per week. In 2027, the goal is to open around 30 restaurants (two to three per month), which would put the chain on track to reach 100 units in 2028. The COO believes the company can fit in several markets across the country, from coast to coast. “We do feel like our brand hits on all cylinders, hits on all categories,” Asker says. “We often get asked, who’s your target audience? Who’s your customer? And for us, it’s a broad way to answer this, but it’s very large. So you’ll be in our stores, you’ll see a senior citizen walk in. You’ll see a 15-year-old walk in, and then you’ll see a mom walk in order for her kids, if you will. So we’re willing to go pretty much anywhere. We feel our brand fits anywhere.” More specifically, Savvy’s philosophy is to go where it has strong operators. The chain recently adjusted its focus to work directly with multi-unit operators who have years of restaurant experience. However, that doesn’t necessarily mean someone with five to 10 units with another concept is automatically signed up. articles.title: Marca chinesa 361° abre primeira pop-up store no Brasil para testar expansão física
articles.titleKo: Marca chinesa 361° abre primeira pop-up store no Brasil para testar expansão física
articles.originalSummary: A 361°, marca chinesa de artigos esportivos, inaugurou sua primeira pop-up store no País, no Boavista Shopping, na zona sul de São Paulo. Com 57 m², o espaço vai funcionar até 30 de novembro e reúne cerca de 2 mil pares de calçados do portfólio da empresa. “A pop-up store é uma oportunidade de experimentar um novo formato de atuação, entender melhor o comportamento do consumidor e avaliar como podemos ampliar nossa presença física no País”, afirma Sérgio Baccaro, general manager da 361° no Brasil. A iniciativa se insere no movimento de expansão de empresas chinesas no Brasil. Nos últimos anos, companhias de setores como automotivo , tecnologia, energia e comércio eletrônico aumentaram os investimentos e passaram a ampliar suas operações no País. A trajetória da 361° no mercado brasileiro começou em 2016, durante os Jogos Olímpicos e Paralímpicos do Rio de Janeiro. Na ocasião, a companhia foi apoiadora oficial das competições e forneceu mais de 107 mil kits de uniformes para profissionais envolvidos nos eventos e no revezamento da Tocha Olímpica. Em 2025, a empresa mudou a forma de apresentar a marca e de conduzir as operações comerciais no País. Desde então, passou a vender seus produtos tanto no e-commerce próprio quanto em redes parceiras, como Centauro, Netshoes, NBA, Futfanatics e Velocità. Expansão física ganha espaço no varejo A companhia chinesa não é a única a apostar na expansão da presença física no Brasil. A Privalia , por exemplo, abriu uma loja pop-up de 350 m² em Curitiba, com cerca de 10 mil produtos de marcas nacionais e internacionais. O espaço fica no Shopping Crystal, no bairro Batel, e funciona por dois meses, de 1º de novembro a 31 de dezembro. A loja terá itens de moda feminina, masculina e infantil, calçados, bolsas, acessórios e produtos para casa. A expectativa da empresa é receber cerca de 15 mil visitantes por mês durante o período, que inclui a Black Friday e as compras de Natal. Com 12 provadores, o espaço permitirá que os clientes experimentem peças e comprem os produtos presencialmente. A seleção exposta será renovada diariamente, com mudanças na organização e na oferta de itens. articles.title: Depois da K-beauty, a China entra na disputa pela beleza global
articles.titleKo: Depois da K-beauty, a China entra na disputa pela beleza global
articles.originalSummary: Fortes em casa e cada vez mais presentes fora da China, as marcas chinesas agora enfrentam um teste mais difícil: conquistar a confiança em mercados que ainda pouco as conhecem. Em novembro, a Proya chegou a 400 lojas da Ulta Beauty nos Estados Unidos, além do comércio eletrônico da rede. Para grande parte do público americano, o nome ainda diz pouco. Na China, porém, a empresa já está entre as maiores marcas locais de beleza. O contraste diz muito sobre o momento atual da C-beauty, termo usado para definir a indústria e as marcas chinesas de beleza. Depois de crescer dentro de casa, algumas dessas empresas começaram a testar sua capacidade de conquistar consumidores em mercados muito diferentes do seu. A Proya também inaugurou um centro de inovação na França. A Florasis, conhecida por incorporar referências da cultura chinesa aos produtos e à experiência de marca, abriu em 2025 sua primeira loja própria fora da China, no distrito de Ginza, em Tóquio. A China já provou que sabe fabricar, inovar com velocidade e operar em escala. Agora precisa provar que também sabe construir marcas globais. Minha leitura é que a C-beauty já demonstrou sua capacidade de escala no mercado doméstico. O próximo desafio, bem mais difícil, será conquistar familiaridade e confiança entre consumidores que não cresceram conhecendo essas marcas. Da força doméstica ao teste internacional As marcas chinesas ultrapassaram as internacionais em participação no mercado doméstico em 2022. Em 2025, chegaram a 57,4% das vendas de cosméticos no país. Esse avanço não aconteceu apenas pelo preço. Essas empresas cresceram conhecendo profundamente o consumidor local e operando em um ambiente no qual conteúdo, comércio e resposta rápida caminham juntos. Também avançaram em pesquisa, formulação e posicionamento, deixando para trás a imagem de que uma marca chinesa compete apenas por ser mais barata. A entrada em outros países muda a natureza do desafio. A distribuição abre portas, mas não garante confiança. Um produto pode estar em uma grande rede e continuar irrelevante para quem não reconhece a marca, não entende sua proposta ou ainda associa sua origem à baixa qualidade. O próprio fundador da Proya afirmou recentemente que o conhecimento da marca nos Estados Unidos e na Europa ainda é praticamente nulo. Por isso, a chegada à Ulta deve ser vista como o começo de um teste, e não como uma consagração. O desafio agora é deixar de vender apenas produtos chineses e construir marcas que o consumidor procure e escolha pelo nome. A prateleira é apenas o começo A Proya e a Florasis ajudam a mostrar que não existe um único caminho. A Proya constrói sua expansão internacional com base na ciência. A marca destaca pesquisa, desempenho e evolução das formulações, além de ter instalado na França uma estrutura dedicada à inovação. Sua mensagem é clara: quer ser reconhecida por eficácia, e não apenas por origem ou preço. Já a Florasis fez outra escolha. A cultura chinesa aparece na estética, nas embalagens, nos ingredientes e na experiência das lojas. Em vez de neutralizar sua procedência para parecer internacional, a marca tenta transformar a própria origem em valor. São estratégias diferentes para enfrentar a mesma pergunta: como uma marca criada para o consumidor chinês ganha significado em Nova York, Paris, Tóquio ou São Paulo? Traduzir a embalagem não será suficiente. Essas empresas precisarão adaptar produtos e comunicação sem diluir sua identidade, além de compreender regras, canais e hábitos locais. Tensões geopolíticas e a percepção sobre produtos chineses também entram nessa equação. Entrar na prateleira é uma conquista. Permanecer na rotina do consumidor é outra história. koreanSummary: Fortes em casa e cada vez mais presentes fora da China, as marcas chinesas agora enfrentam um teste mais difícil: conquistar a confiança em mercados que ainda pouco as conhecem.

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . While restaurant chains across the country face continued challenges attracting customers, Detroit’s Original Chicken Shack is demonstrating that a 70-year-old brand can compete and grow in today’s restaurant environment. The Michigan-based chicken chain reported an 8.5% year-over-year increase in guest traffic in September, alongside 3.3% growth in same-store sales, continuing a period of strong performance driven by product innovation, customer loyalty and improvements to the guest experience. Perhaps most notably, Chicken Shack achieved these results without raising menu prices in either 2025 or 2026. At a time when many restaurant chains are relying on pricing to support sales amid softer customer traffic, Chicken Shack has taken a different approach: investing in its food, improving convenience and giving customers more reasons to visit. “Our strategy has been focused on growing customer traffic by delivering a better product and a better experience, not by raising prices,” said Cliff Lunney, President and Managing Partner of Detroit’s Original Chicken Shack. “While much of the restaurant industry is struggling to maintain guest visits, we’re bringing more customers through our doors. Our September results demonstrate that this approach is working.” Product Innovation Fuels Sustained Traffic Growth A key component of Chicken Shack’s recent success has been its commitment to improving the products that have defined the brand for generations. In July, Chicken Shack introduced its upgraded Crispy Tenders, featuring a crunchier exterior while preserving the distinctive flavor developed through the brand’s proprietary marination process. Rather than introducing an entirely new menu category, Chicken Shack focused on elevating an existing customer favorite, building on nearly 70 years of chicken preparation expertise. The response was immediate. Guest traffic increased following the July launch and has remained positive year over year in each of the three months since. From July through September, traffic increased 8.4% compared with the same period in 2025, with September reaching 8.5%. The increase in customer visits was accompanied by stronger sales performance. In September, same-store sales grew 3.3%, demonstrating the brand’s ability to translate additional guest traffic into revenue growth. “Our first objective was to bring more guests through the door, and our upgraded Crispy Tenders helped us accomplish that,” Lunney said. “The next step is building repeat visits and long-term loyalty. We’re encouraged by the continued traffic growth and the improvement in same-store sales.” Competing Through Quality, Value and Customer Loyalty Chicken Shack’s performance comes as restaurant operators nationwide continue to navigate changing consumer spending habits, increased competition and pressure on customer traffic. Rather than relying on menu price increases, the company has focused on strengthening its overall value proposition through product quality, convenience and customer engagement. In late 2025, Chicken Shack introduced Shack Rewards, a new loyalty program designed to strengthen customer relationships and encourage repeat visits. The brand has also expanded its digital ordering capabilities, making it easier for guests to enjoy Chicken Shack through online ordering, mobile ordering and other convenient channels. These initiatives are part of a broader modernization strategy that combines the brand’s longstanding commitment to quality with the convenience and accessibility today’s consumers expect. At the center of that strategy remains Chicken Shack’s signature marinated chicken, a proprietary product developed from recipes and preparation methods that have distinguished the brand since 1956. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . As the holiday season gets underway, birthdays, anniversaries and major holidays remain familiar reasons to celebrate, but new national research suggests Americans are also making room for smaller, more spontaneous moments of connection. Nearly 3 in 4 U.S. adults (72%) report changing how they celebrate special occasions compared with a few years ago, while about 2 in 3 (67%) say they often celebrate everyday moments, including personal achievements, good news and informal gatherings. The findings come from the first annual How America Celebrates Report , conducted by The Harris Poll on behalf of Edible Arrangements, a modern gifting destination and part of the Edible Brands portfolio. The research offers a closer look at how Americans are rethinking when, where and how they celebrate as financial pressures influence spending decisions. More than half (56%) say they are more likely to prefer celebrating at home than they were a few years ago, while nearly 3 in 4 (73%) prefer giving gifts or gestures that can be shared or experienced together rather than traditional gifts. More spontaneous celebrations are also part of the conversation. More than 2 in 5 (42%) agree that last-minute celebrations seem more frequent than they were a few years ago, reflecting how respondents perceive changing celebration habits. Together, the findings suggest that meaningful occasions extend beyond the traditional holiday calendar, raising questions about how businesses across gifting, retail and hospitality can remain relevant as consumer preferences evolve. “When people are watching their spending, they make choices about where to save, and celebrations usually aren’t the first place they look,” said Somia Farid Silber, CEO of Edible Brands. “From a gathering at home to a small personal win, the occasions may look different, but the desire to connect comes through clearly. For Edible Arrangements, that’s a valuable perspective as we continue thinking about how gifting fits into people’s lives, beyond traditional holidays and major milestones.” Americans are rethinking what makes a celebration meaningful While traditional occasions remain important, the research highlights how Americans are finding meaning in smaller gatherings, personal achievements and shared experiences. Nearly 2 in 5 respondents report celebrating special occasions at home more often than they did a few years ago, while about 3 in 10 say they focus on creating experiences or memories more frequently. When asked about the best ways to make a celebration special, nearly 6 in 10 (59%) identify spending quality time with family and friends, followed by nearly 2 in 5 (38%) who point to creating memorable experiences and more than 1 in 3 (35%) who value sharing food, treats or a meal together. The importance of shared experiences also extends to gifting. Nearly 3 in 4 Americans prefer giving gifts or gestures that can be shared or experienced together rather than traditional gifts, while the same proportion express that preference when receiving gifts. For Edible Arrangements, known for fruit arrangements, chocolate-dipped strawberries, dessert boards and platters, food-centered gifts and floral arrangements, the findings offer insight into how consumers think about meaningful gestures and the occasions worth recognizing. The research also raises broader questions for businesses traditionally focused on major holidays and milestones, particularly as consumers express interest in celebrating everyday achievements and personal connections throughout the year. articles.title: Getting the Air Right: Why a Test & Balance Matters for the Restaurant Sector
articles.titleKo: Getting the Air Right: Why a Test & Balance Matters for the Restaurant Sector
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A location that was perfectly balanced the day it opened can be meaningfully out of tune a couple of years later. Restaurants looking to optimize energy performance and efficiency typically focus on equipment and reducing consumption. But some of the biggest inefficiencies, and some of the biggest comfort problems, hide somewhere less obvious: in the air itself. How well your HVAC system is actually moving air plays a big role in the customer experience and can have a significant impact on operations. That’s where a Test & Balance (TAB) comes in. This service is often overlooked in building performance, but it’s crucial to make your restaurants more comfortable for the people who work and eat in them. In my role, I’ve seen the impact of TAB, and in this piece, I’m sharing why it matters for quick-service and casual dining locations in particular, and what we learned when we tested air balance across dozens of real sites. The Problem: Restaurants Drift Out of Balance Faster Than Most Buildings Restaurants are a uniquely demanding environment for HVAC. Kitchens run powerful exhaust hoods that pull enormous volumes of air out of the building to regulate temperature and ventilation. That air has to be replaced (i.e. “made up”) by the HVAC system, and if the balance between what’s exhausted and what’s supplied isn’t right, the whole building ends up under negative pressure. When that happens, the building is constantly sucking in unconditioned outside air through every door seal, drive-thru window, and gap it can find. Your rooftop units then spend their day fighting that infiltration, cooling and heating air that’s leaking in faster than it should. When you factor in long operating hours, heavy foot traffic, constant door cycling at the drive-thru, and the heat load from a full kitchen line, you have a system under real stress. This negatively impacts how comfortable the environment is and causes energy bills to shoot up. A location that was perfectly balanced the day it opened can be meaningfully out of tune a couple of years later, with no obvious warning sign. But subtle clues will persist: elevated operating costs, slamming doors, or comfort complaints with no clear solution. How Test & Balance Helps Test & Balance is a practice in which a technician measures how an HVAC system is performing and then corrects it as needed. By re-verifying and adjusting the airflow and static pressure across the rooftop units (RTUs), TAB makes sure each one is moving the right volume of air, at the right pressure, to the right spaces. Think of it as a tune-up for the air. Units may be running, and from the dining room everything may feel fine, but “running” and “running correctly” are not the same thing. Over time, dampers drift, belts loosen, filters load up, and settings that were dialed in on install day wander off target. A proper TAB checks the fundamentals that govern how much energy your building burns: Airflow volume: Is each unit actually delivering the cubic feet per minute it’s rated for, or is it choking or overshooting? Static pressure: Is the system fighting itself, forcing the blower to strain against restrictions? Balance across zones: Is conditioned air reaching the dining room, kitchen, and back-of-house in the right proportions? Checking these factors can make a big difference in performance and help keep energy consumption level. This not only improves comfort in the building, but also helps equipment longevity and operations. It’s just a matter of measuring what’s really happening and correcting it. Square today announced that Koibito Poké , the Arizona-based real-food poké brand with the mission of bringing healthy eating to communities across the United States, has selected Square as its unified commerce platform. Operating 10 locations and actively scaling through a regional developer franchise model, Koibito has tapped Square as the technology foundation for its next phase of national growth. Koibito was founded by Todd Stottlemyre, a former Major League Baseball pitcher who spent 15 years in the majors and won three World Series championships. The same performance mindset that defined his athletic career – embracing challenges, pivoting when the tides turn, and relentlessly pursuing continuous improvement – has served as the basis for how he built the growing poké brand . In December 2019, Stottlemyre bought out his business partner to take 100% ownership of Koibito. Three months later, the pandemic hit and shuttered brick-and-mortar locations. Rather than standing still, the Koibito team found new ways forward: launching delivery when consumers were dubious that such a product could travel well, and in the process demonstrating that poké holds up well in transit. The company’s catering expansion followed a similarly uphill path. For Koibito, obstacles repeatedly become new revenue streams. Selecting Square was motivated by Koibito’s need for an end-to-end ecosystem spanning intuitive hardware, robust APIs, and a partner willing to evolve alongside the brand as its business model diversified. Prior to choosing Square, the company felt limited by its prior stack’s reporting, loyalty, and consumer engagement capabilities. Square’s willingness to enable these needs and embrace change, rather than defaulting to legacy ways of working, was a decisive factor in making the switch. “We had incredible systems for store operations, equipment, architecture, branding, and marketing – everything an entrepreneur needs to build a world-class franchise,” said Todd Stottlemyre, Founder and CEO of Koibito. “The last piece to becoming first-class was the tech stack. Square was the last brick, and it’s delivered. It’s best in class and proved to be exactly what we were looking for.” Koibito runs Square across its 10 locations, with Square Kiosk and Square Shifts as additional tools in the stack. The partnership also gives Koibito’s franchisees access to enterprise-grade tools. Koibito’s loyalty program, online ordering, and mobile app are powered by Thanx through its newly launched, direct integration with Square. Koibito’s team now has the ability to track the full customer journey: from first visit to second, and critically, to the third – the point at which, Koibito finds, a guest’s likelihood of becoming a regular increases dramatically. Automated marketing triggers bring lapsed customers back through targeted outreach, and the platform’s data capabilities give Koibito the tools to build genuine brand loyalty rather than relying solely on discounting to drive frequency. “Koibito is building something that goes well beyond a poké concept – it’s a performance-driven franchise brand with a clear goal and a team committed to winning,” said James Schonzeit, Head of Food & Beverage at Square. “Todd has applied the same competitive mindset to building this business that defined his athletic career: raise the standard, evolve constantly, and never settle for where you were twelve months ago. The smell of fresh-baked pastries and the sound of holiday cheer are making their way to Spanish Fork. Bonrue Bakery , formerly Farmstead, is celebrating its newest location Saturday, Dec. 5, from 9 a.m.-12 p.m., with a festive grand opening featuring seasonal treats, photo opportunities and surprises for early guests. Located at 713 E. 800 North, guests can get a first taste of Bonrue’s European-style bakery favorites, from flaky croissants to its signature kouign-amann and seasonal specialties. Santa Claus and Mrs. Claus will be making a special appearance for holiday photos. The Spanish Fork High School Band will bring the holiday soundtrack with a live performance, while guests waiting in line can warm up with free hot chocolate. The first 200 guests will also receive a Bonrue-branded tote, with additional goodies, including whisks, cutting boards and other merchandise, available while supplies last. “Our bakeries are built around bringing people together, and there is no better time to do that than the holiday season,” said Chris Connors, owner and founder of Bonrue Bakery. “We are excited to share our coffee, pastries and sandwiches with Spanish Fork and to celebrate the season with the community.” Since opening in 2021, Bonrue Bakery has grown a following for its handcrafted pastries, fresh-baked bread, coffee and breakfast and lunch offerings. Spanish Fork marks the bakery’s sixth location and third opening in Utah County this year, joining its existing bakeries in Provo, Orem, St. George, Hurricane and Springdale. The Spanish Fork bakery will be open daily from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., bringing a new neighborhood gathering spot for morning pastries, coffee and lunch. For more information, visit bonruebakery.com . articles.titleKo: Ganso Hakata Yatai by yataikeiji
articles.originalSummary: Debuts at One Causeway Bay Bringing the Authentic Spirit of Fukuoka’s Iconic Yatai Culture to Hong Kong Four Culinary Masters Unite to Celebrate Japan’s Diverse Culinary Traditions, from Charcoal-Grilled Yakitori to Seasonal Kaiseki Ganso Hakata Yatai by yataikeiji , a dynamic showcase of Japan’s celebrated yatai culture, has arrived at Causeway Bay’s newest landmark, One Causeway Bay, bringing the lively spirit and communal charm of Fukuoka’s iconic open-air dining tradition to Hong Kong. Led by Yuta Abe of the renowned Yatai Keiji in Fukuoka, the culinary collective brings together kaiseki specialist Chef Yuki Tounai, yakitori master Chef Goma Shimoda, and washoku expert Chef Kensaku Narazaki, whose repertoire extends to French, Italian and pastry techniques. Together, they draw upon their diverse expertise to present an immersive exploration of Japanese gastronomy, where cherished street-food favourites meet refined omakase and contemporary culinary craftsmanship. Through a menu that spans charcoal-grilled yakitori, robatayaki and oden alongside crowd-pleasing ramen, akashiyaki and kaiseki, the venue captures the convivial atmosphere of an evening out in Hakata, where food, drink and conversation converge around intimate counter seating. Among the inaugural dining concepts at One Causeway Bay, Ganso Hakata Yatai by yataikeiji marks a franchise partnership between Yuta Abe and Hong Kong dining group CSC Collective . Centred around sharing, connection and genuine hospitality, the experience seamlessly blends long-established Japanese culinary traditions with a contemporary social dining ethos. Guests are welcomed throughout the day, whether for a quick weekday lunch, after-work drinks, celebratory gatherings or leisurely dinners with family and friends. To mark the opening, those visiting on or before 30 November 2026 can enjoy 15% off their total bill. Founded in 1991 in Akasaka, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka, Yatai Keiji has been a beloved fixture of the city’s casual dining landscape for more than three decades. Abe’s background as a miya-daiku (traditional shrine and temple carpenter) reflects a deep appreciation for Japanese craftsmanship, heritage and cultural preservation. Through this Hong Kong venture, he hopes to share the enduring spirit of Hakata’s yatai tradition with a new generation of diners. Spanning more than 2,500 sq. ft and accommodating 106 diners, Ganso Hakata Yatai by yataikeiji reimagines the atmosphere of Hakata’s famed food stalls through two signature yatai concepts: Gotetsu , dedicated to charcoal-grilled yakitori, and Yataikeiji , which celebrates comforting Japanese favourites including robatayaki, oden and akashiyaki. Each is centred around a 10-seat culinary counter, allowing diners to engage directly with the chefs and their craft. For a more intimate experience, the Akashi private dining room accommodates up to 12 people and showcases seasonal kaiseki menus alongside bespoke dining experiences. Dark wood finishes, traditional lanterns and illuminated signboards complete the setting, evoking the nostalgic yet energetic character of Hakata’s celebrated night-time dining culture. Robatayaki takes centre stage at the Yataikeiji counter, where Chef Narasaki deftly grills meat and seafood over charcoal to enhance their natural flavours with a subtle smoky aroma. articles.title: Hensol Castle Single Malt Welsh Whisky Is Officially Here
articles.titleKo: Hensol Castle Single Malt Welsh Whisky Is Officially Here
articles.originalSummary: Hensol Castle Distillery has today officially launched its inaugural Single Malt Welsh Whisky, the first whisky to be distilled and matured at the historic estate. From today, every pre-order is on its way to customers, and the whisky is pouring in selected bars, restaurants and independent retailers across Wales. The launch marks a landmark moment for the award-winning South Wales distillery and a new arrival in the fast-growing Single Malt Welsh Whisky category. Grain to glass, under one roof The whisky programme began in 2022, and on 27 February 2023 the distillery team filled “Barrel No.1”, the first cask of the inaugural edition. Every step since has been carried out at Hensol. The process starts with a 100% malted barley wash, developed with partners at Newport’s Tiny Rebel Brewery. The spirit is then distilled on-site and matured in the castle’s cellars. After more than three and a half years in premium American bourbon barrels, the result is a rich, remarkably complex spirit for its age and well-balanced Welsh single malt with notes of orchard fruit, penny toffee and honeyed oak. “Starting our journey into the whisky world wasn’t something we took lightly; whisky is a decision for the future, a legacy,” said Kyle Jones, Master Distiller at Hensol Castle Distillery . “Our goal was to craft a liquid as timeless as the castle itself, while putting our own stamp on a thriving Welsh whisky category. With precision, expertise and a quiet obsession for the craft, I can confidently say we have exceeded that goal.” “Filling that first barrel back in 2023 wasn’t about noise or chasing headlines; it was about starting something properly,” Jones added. “Welsh whisky has a proud heritage, and we wanted to respect that from day one. It’s ready, it’s distinct, and it’s everything we hoped it would be.” A strictly limited first release The first run is limited to just over 1,000 bottles : 500 bottles were set aside for the distillery’s direct-to-consumer community through pre-orders, which opened at the end of September. All pre-orders are dispatched today. 500 bottles have gone to Welsh on-trade partners, selected independent retailers and two wholesalers: Fine Wines Direct (National and South Wales) and Blas ar Fwyd (National and North Wales). Backing Welsh hospitality To recognise what the Welsh hospitality sector brings to the drinks industry, Hensol Castle has partnered with several of Wales’s top bars for the launch. The distillery has put together a map of venues where drinkers can try a dram of the first release while supporting local hospitality. follow out socials for where to grab your dram. To mark the release, Hensol Castle Distillery is hosting a press and invited-guest event at the castle and distillery on December 3rd 2026 A new Master Distiller for a new chapter The launch is also the first release under Kyle Jones , who was recently appointed Master Distiller. Jones has worked on the single malt programme since its earliest planning stages in 2022, alongside former Master Distiller and Head of Commercial Dai Wakely . After five years with the business, Wakely stepped down at the end of September and will continue working with Hensol as a consultant. With the first batch released, Jones now takes full responsibility for the whisky programme and its future development. What comes next The distillery is already planning future releases. The team recently made an 1,800-mile round trip to Bordeaux to inspect and select barrels in person, securing 12 finishing casks for a pipeline of highly limited-edition releases in the coming years. “We are thrilled to be adding our first single malt to the vibrant Single Malt Welsh Whisky category,” said Nate Sorby, Head of Marketing at Hensol Castle Distillery . “The growth and reputation of Welsh spirits over recent years has been incredible to watch, and as an award-winning distillery in the heart of South Wales, we’re proud to play a role in that momentum. Whether planning an office Christmas party, a cosy family gathering, or a festive feast with friends, Humble Grape and Vivat Bacchus are ready with open arms, warm hospitality, and a glass (or three) of wine. EARLY BIRD BONUS To kick off the season in style, the Humble Group is offering an early bird treat for those getting in the festive spirit a little sooner. If you book a Christmas party for eight or more people in November and dine from the festive party menu between the 16th and 30th of November, the Humble Group will throw in a glass of fizz for all. We’re talking rich duck and chestnut terrine, and the ultimate traditional roast turkey dinner with all the trimmings – Roast potatoes, maple-glazed carrots, braised red cabbage, sprouts & gravy . Not feeling turkey? No problem. A juicy tomahawk steak served with all the festive sides brings a modern twist to the table, perfect for those craving something a little different. Costing £60 per person at our city locations, and £35 per person at our neighborhood sites: Battersea & Islington. MEET UNDER THE MISTLETOE For the wine enthusiasts (or those excited to learn more), Humble Grape is hosting a series of Mistletoe and Wine tasting evenings. These relaxed and sociable events will start with a surprise welcome drink, followed by a guided tasting of six organic winter wines – from full-bodied reds to complex, wintery whites, all led by the in-house wine team. It’s a great way to discover new favourites and welcome in the holiday season. Tastings will run from 6.30 PM to 8.30 PM across three of our venues: Liverpool Street – Monday 7th December Battersea – Tuesday 8th December Bow Lane – Wednesday 9th December A SOUTH-AFRICAN CHRISTMAS AT VIVAT BACCHUS Meanwhile, at Vivat Bacchus , Christmas is getting a South African twist – bringing bold flavours, big energy, and warm hospitality to the table. The menu is served family style, so everyone can get involved and dig in. Expect delicious dishes like beef carpaccio with biltong aioli, turkey & boerewors sosatie, and brannas & Coke gammon all served with festive sides like braised red cabbage , Cape Malay sprouts and rooibos cranberries, cinnamon and honey butternut squash and more.. To finish it off? The much-loved South African peppermint tart – sweet, nostalgic, and totally irresistible. If you’ve never had a South African-style Christmas, now’s your chance to say “lekker” and dive right in, all for £60 per person. GIFTING MADE EASY For those looking for the perfect bottle of something special or a last-minute gift, pop into Humble Grape or Vivat Bacchus and find the perfect Christmas present. Browse an incredible selection of wines from around the world, all ideal for gifting (or keeping for yourself!). It might be a thoughtful bottle for a friend, a gift voucher, or a subscription to The Humble Club for a wine lover in your life. Every Humble Group experience is designed to capture the spirit of Christmas – simply book, relax, and leave the rest to the experts. articles.titleKo: Oscar AI Launches Mobile App and AI-Powered Chat Feature
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Oscar AI, the AI-powered operational intelligence platform for multi-unit restaurant operators, announced two new offerings: a mobile app that brings its desktop platform to operators on the go, and an AI-powered chat feature available across both desktop and mobile. Together, the new capabilities help restaurant leaders monitor performance, access business insights and make informed decisions wherever they are. “Restaurant operators need quick access to information, whether they’re at their desks or in the field,” said Quratul-Ann Malik, founder of Oscar AI. “With our new mobile app and AI-powered chat, we’re making it easier to get answers, spot issues and make decisions without slowing down.” Restaurant Intelligence, Now on the Go Oscar AI’s new mobile app gives restaurant executives, franchise operators and multi-unit managers access to business information throughout the day, without being tied to a computer. Built as AI-native from the ground up, Oscar brings intelligence into every workflow. Whether moving between locations or managing daily operations, users can review AI-generated performance recaps, monitor scorecards that surface what needs attention, access reports with built-in insights, and track key metrics all from their mobile devices. “The app is super easy to use and always up to date,” said Russ Lo Bello, President of The Phoenix Organization, a 40-unit Burger King Operator. “With our teams always in the field, it gives them the data and much needed action steps right at their fingertips.” AI-Powered Chat Turns Restaurant Data Into Answers Available on both desktop and mobile, Oscar AI’s new chat feature allows operators to ask questions in everyday language and receive answers based on their business data. Rather than searching through reports, users can quickly access insights and explore specific areas of performance. Key capabilities include: Sales: Analyze trends in chain and/or store financials within seconds. Operations: Identify performance and profitability issues and opportunities across locations. Labor: Review staffing, scheduling and overtime. Guest Feedback: Quickly summarize customer comments and recurring themes. Deeper Insights: Explore findings through suggested prompts and follow-up questions. Oscar AI has recorded thousands of customer-initiated chat sessions, with sales performance, operational priorities and labor management among the most common topics. Since early testing, chat conversations on the platform have tripled, driven by both active users and prompts per session. With both features now in place for all users of the platform, Oscar continues to grow it’s base of users across thousands of restaurants with the leading brands in the Quick Serve Restaurant industry. Pizza Guys, a Sacramento-based pizza franchise known for fresh, high-quality ingredients, announced that it has signed three new franchise agreements in Southern California. The agreements will bring new Pizza Guys restaurants to Bellflower, Highland, and Newport Beach, led by franchisees Majid Mohabatravan, Aman Jyot Singh, and Nader Iskander, respectively. The three new agreements reflect Pizza Guys’ continued expansion across California, by experienced operators. Existing franchisees Mohabatravan and Iskander are expanding their Pizza Guys footprint into new communities, while multi-unit Subway operator Singh is broadening his portfolio. Together, the agreements mark an exciting step forward in Pizza Guys’ growth and their commitment to bringing quality, signature pizzas to even more California communities. “There’s no stronger endorsement of a franchise system than existing owners choosing to grow with us,” said Shahpour Nejad, CEO and Founder of Pizza Guys. “Majid and Nader have already shown what it takes to run a great Pizza Guys, and Aman brings years of hands-on restaurant experience to his first location. Each of them is deeply invested in the community they serve, and we’re proud to support their next chapter as we continue to grow across Southern California.” From Corona to Bellflower Mohabatravan has signed a lease for his Bellflower restaurant, bringing his proven track record to a new market with an anticipated opening in December 2026. The location marks his second Pizza Guys store following the Corona restaurant he purchased in 2022, which now employs 18 people. Born in Iran, Mohabatravan earned a degree in software engineering and worked alongside his father in the family’s PVC pipe manufacturing business. After moving to the Bay Area in 2016, he set out to own a business of his own. He spent two years driving for Uber and Lyft to learn about the region and ran a profitable online resale business before reaching out directly to Pizza Guys’ corporate leadership team. Committed to learning the business from the ground up, Mohabatravan joined a Pizza Guys team in 2020, spending a year and a half mastering store operations before taking the leap into ownership. When the opportunity to purchase the Corona location came, he made a major life change relocating his family to Southern California to pursue his dream of building successful local businesses. “In business, you have to be patient and consistent,” said Mohabatravan. “Four years in, I’m still learning something new every day. Bellflower is a bigger challenge than Corona because we’re building it from the ground up, but the support from the Pizza Guys team makes all the difference. We treat our customers like family, and that’s exactly what we’ll bring to Bellflower.” Mohabatravan remains heavily involved in local outreach, regularly sponsoring school fundraisers rewarding top students with free pizza and hosting community charity events; a tradition he plans to establish in Bellflower as well. articles.title: Wonder Reportedly Shopping Grubhub to Potential Buyers
articles.titleKo: Wonder Reportedly Shopping Grubhub to Potential Buyers
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wonder first announced its acquisition of Grubhub in 2024. Wonder is exploring a potential sale of Grubhub less than two years after acquiring the third-party delivery platform for $650 million , according to The Wall Street Journal. The food technology company’s bankers have reportedly approached several major retailers, including Walmart, Target, and Kroger, to gauge their interest in acquiring Grubhub. There is no guarantee a transaction will materialize. The report comes as Wonder eyes a potential IPO. Earlier this month, the company announced it confidentially submitted a draft registration statement with the SEC . The filing followed a $650 million Series D funding round that valued Wonder at $9 billion before the investment. The company said the funding would support restaurant development, marketplace growth, and investments in robotics, AI, and technology. Wonder announced its acquisition of Grubhub from Just Eat Takeaway.com in November 2024 and completed the transaction in January 2025 . The deal included $150 million in cash and the assumption of $500 million in debt. The purchase price represented a roughly 90 percent decrease from the $7.3 billion Just Eat agreed to pay for Grubhub in 2020 . At the time, Wonder founder Marc Lore positioned the acquisition as a key piece of the company’s ambition to consolidate restaurant ordering, third-party delivery, and meal kits into one platform . In September, Wonder agreed to sell Grubhub’s campus dining business to DoorDash for $300 million. DoorDash also agreed to invest $125 million in Wonder. Earlier this month, Amazon announced it was ending its partnership with Grubhub in favor of Uber Eats. The potential sale coincides with continued consolidation in the third-party delivery industry, including DoorDash’s October announcement that it agreed to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart for $17 billion . Wonder has completed several other major acquisitions in recent years, including the $103 million purchase of Blue Apron and the $186 million acquisition of Sweetgreen’s Infinite Kitchen business. It has also acquired restaurant brands Mighty Quinn’s and Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken as it expands its company-owned restaurant network. articles.titleKo: Como a C&A usa a Ace para testar um novo modelo de negócio e abrir frentes de inovação
articles.originalSummary: Criar novos negócios sem necessariamente começar do zero. Essa é a estratégia da C&A com a Ace, marca de moda esportiva que nasceu dentro da companhia na década de 1980 e que, recentemente, ganhou estrutura própria. A varejista utiliza a operação como um laboratório para testar modelos de negócio, formatos de lojas, estratégias de produto e tecnologias, combinando a agilidade de uma startup com a escala de uma grande empresa. A transformação da Ace em uma unidade de negócios independente representa uma mudança na maneira como a C&A desenvolve novas frentes de atuação. A marca passou a ter equipes dedicadas a produto, marketing e canais de venda, enquanto áreas como tecnologia, financeiro, recursos humanos, logística e abastecimento continuam compartilhando a estrutura da companhia. A ideia é ganhar velocidade e flexibilidade para experimentar, sem precisar construir toda a estrutura do zero. “Estar dentro da C&A permitiu que a Ace nascesse leve em investimento, mas muito robusta em capacidade”, afirma Filipe Albuquerque, diretor de Novos Negócios da C&A Brasil, em entrevista à Mercado&Consumo .
