articles.title: Playa Bowls Opens First Military Base Location
articles.titleKo: Playa Bowls Opens First Military Base Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Playa Bowls, the fast-growing superfruit and acai bowl brand, has opened its first shop on a military installation at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland (JBSA-Lackland) in San Antonio, Texas. Owned by multi-unit franchise owner Dipesh Patel, his wife Amanda and their business partners Kris and Autumn Normand, who are all Air Force veterans, the shop marks Playa Bowls’ fifth non-traditional location and an expansion of its franchise development strategy beyond traditional retail spaces. For the four owners, who all completed basic training at Lackland, the opening offers an opportunity to serve a community with which they share a personal connection. Dipesh and Amanda were also stationed in San Antonio during their Air Force careers. Dipesh and his business partners have developed five other Playa Bowls shops across the San Antonio area since opening their first in May 2021. With the JBSA-Lackland shop, they are building on that experience to make better-for-you options more accessible to the military community. “Having served in the Air Force, we know how much your daily routine revolves around the base,” said Dipesh. “We wanted people to have an option that fits into that routine, whether they’re grabbing breakfast or taking a lunch break. It means a lot to us to see a business we’ve built become part of a place that helped shape our lives.” Situated within the base’s food court, the 489-square-foot shop brings Playa Bowls’ bowls, smoothies and more directly into the military community’s daily routine through a walk-up service format. It joins a growing portfolio of non-traditional shops at Newark Liberty International Airport, Grand Central Station, Penn Station and Mercedes Club, a Manhattan health and fitness club. Playa Bowls’ menu requires no cooking, baking or frying, allowing shops to operate without the large cooking equipment and exhaust systems common in restaurant kitchens. Those simpler infrastructure requirements give the brand flexibility to tailor layouts to different venues, while bowls and smoothies offer options for breakfast, lunch, snacks and dinner. The model supports further expansion into settings such as military installations, college campuses, healthcare facilities and entertainment venues. “Opening at JBSA-Lackland gives us the opportunity to grow our non-traditional footprint while proudly serving military members, their families and visitors to the base,” said Patrick Turek, chief development officer of Playa Bowls. “Our local franchise owners bring both the experience of operating Playa Bowls shops and a personal understanding of military life, making them exceptional partners to lead this opening. We are thrilled to bring our better-for-you bowls, smoothies and more to this community. As we continue to thrive in traditional retail markets, we are also pursuing significant opportunities at military bases, airports, universities and hospitals. The strength of our model is its flexibility, allowing us to adapt to these settings and bring Playa Bowls to guests throughout their day. JBSA-Lackland demonstrates that potential, and we will build on this momentum as we expand into new venues and serve those who serve our country.” The veteran-owned opening comes as Playa Bowls was recently named one of Franchise Business Review’s Top Franchises for Veterans for 2026. To learn more about Playa Bowls, visit www.playabowls.com and follow the brand at @playabowls on Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook for the latest news. To learn more about Playa Bowls and its franchising opportunities, visit franchise.playabowls.com/. The post Playa Bowls Opens First Military Base Location appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: TipHaus Reports 672 Percent Growth, Earns Spot on Deloitte Technology Fast 500
articles.titleKo: TipHaus Reports 672 Percent Growth, Earns Spot on Deloitte Technology Fast 500
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . TipHaus makes tip management and tip operations software for hospitality. TipHaus announced that it ranked number 105 on the Deloitte Technology Fast 500, a ranking of the 500 fastest-growing tech companies in North America, now in its 32nd year. TipHaus grew 672% from 2022 to 2025. TipHaus’s chief executive officer, Leif Magnuson, said, “Hospitality operators are realizing that managing tips through spreadsheets, cash envelopes, and disconnected systems simply doesn’t scale. Our growth reflects a fundamental shift in how the industry approaches tip management, with more restaurant groups and enterprise operators investing in automation, transparency, and better experiences for their employees. Ranking No. 105 on the Deloitte Technology Fast 500 is a testament to the trust our customers place in us and the team behind our success.” TipHaus co-founder and chief operating officer Kirk Grogan added, “Nearly 700% growth in three years is an incredible milestone, but what makes me most proud is the team behind it. In hospitality, getting tips right isn’t just an operational priority. It directly impacts people’s livelihoods. Our employees understand that responsibility, and they’ve built the trust, service, and reliability that make this kind of growth possible.” TipHaus makes tip management and tip operations software for hospitality. Restaurants, entertainment venues and hotel groups, including bartaco, Bluegrass Hospitality, Legal Sea Foods and SSP America, use it to calculate, distribute, reconcile and report tips across every location. The recognition follows the company’s Nov. 16 announcement of a strategic growth investment from Vista Equity Partners. articles.title: Com impasse sobre combustíveis fósseis, COP31 termina sem acordo final
articles.titleKo: Com impasse sobre combustíveis fósseis, COP31 termina sem acordo final
articles.originalSummary: A 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31), realizada em Antália, na Turquia, terminou neste domingo, 22, sem a elaboração de um acordo final. O impasse ocorreu em função de divergências de países produtores de petróleo sobre menções a um prazo para o fim do uso de combustíveis fósseis. As negociações para a definição de metas para barrar a utilização de combustíveis fósseis já trilhavam o caminho da falta de consenso desde sexta-feira, 20, quando a conferência deveria ter sido encerrada oficialmente. Devido ao impasse, as negociações foram retomadas por mais dois dias, mas a falta de consenso foi mantida durante a última sessão plenária da COP, realizada na manhã deste domingo. O Greenpeace Brasil classificou o resultado da COP31 como decepcionante. Para a entidade, a conferência deixa de responsabilizar os combustíveis fósseis pela crise climática mundial e dá sobrevida ao setor. “Diante dos rascunhos da COP31, que mostravam graves retrocessos, acelerava tecnologias caras e ineficientes que beneficiam a indústria fóssil e sequer mencionavam os combustíveis fósseis, foi melhor não ter um acordo de capa do que ter um acordo ruim”, declarou. O WWF Brasil também lamentou o resultado da conferência e disse que a COP deveria ter consolidado uma mudança clara das negociações para efetivar as ações climáticas. “Os mapas do caminho da presidência da COP30 sobre Combustíveis Fósseis e Florestas sequer foram reconhecidos ou acolhidos. Houve uma ênfase preocupante em tecnologias de captura de carbono, que não substituem a redução das emissões”, comentou a entidade. articles.title: Mais da metade das empresas leva mais de 24h para analisar crédito
articles.titleKo: Mais da metade das empresas leva mais de 24h para analisar crédito
articles.originalSummary: Mais da metade das empresas brasileiras demora mais de 24 horas para aprovar ou negar pedidos de crédito, segundo pesquisa da Assertiva, empresa brasileira de tecnologia que oferece uma plataforma para validar dados cadastrais, analisar riscos de crédito e apoiar a gestão de cobranças. O levantamento, feito com 150 profissionais envolvidos em processos de análise de risco e concessão, aponta que 31,3% das organizações levam de um a dois dias úteis para decidir, enquanto 22,7% precisam de mais de dois dias úteis. A demora aparece em empresas de diferentes portes. Entre as microempresas, 64,8% levam ao menos um dia útil para decidir. O porcentual é de 51,3% nas pequenas e médias, 52% nas grandes e 49,1% na categoria “enterprise”, segundo a classificação da pesquisa. Na outra ponta, 13,3% das companhias concluem a análise em minutos, de forma totalmente automatizada, e 6,7% concluem o processo em menos de uma hora. De acordo com o levantamento, 14% ainda fazem a avaliação com planilhas e análise manual; outros 16,7% consultam birôs de crédito – empresas que reúnem informações financeiras e cadastrais – sem integrar essas consultas aos sistemas internos. Apenas 6,7% utilizam sistemas que aprovam ou negam crédito automaticamente com inteligência artificial (IA). Para Hederson Albertini, CEO da Assertiva, a demora não se restringe às empresas menores. “Tamanho e capacidade de investimento não se traduzem necessariamente em eficiência operacional”, afirma. Segundo ele, processos manuais e sistemas sem integração podem reduzir a agilidade das decisões. O estudo classifica 41,3% das empresas como maduras em seus processos de análise de crédito; 58,7% estão em estágio de desenvolvimento ou têm processos incipientes. A pesquisa foi realizada entre 23 de junho e 6 de outubro de 2026, com profissionais de todo o País. A região Sudeste concentrou 78,7% dos entrevistados, conclui. articles.title: Agentes de IA entram no radar dos bancos e devem mudar pagamentos
articles.titleKo: Agentes de IA entram no radar dos bancos e devem mudar pagamentos
articles.originalSummary: Agentes de Inteligência Artificial (IA) começam a ganhar espaço nas compras online e podem mudar também a relação dos consumidores com os bancos. Segundo o estudo de “Tecnologias Emergentes para o Setor Bancário 2026”, da Febraban com a Accenture, o uso da tecnologia para pesquisar ofertas, comparar preços e concluir pagamentos automatizados é uma das principais transformações previstas para o setor financeiro. O levantamento identifica seis frentes tecnológicas que devem influenciar o setor: Inteligência Artificial e agentes, banco conversacional, comércio agêntico, computação quântica, ativos virtuais e tokenização e segurança digital. No comércio agêntico, agentes de IA assumem etapas da jornada de compra, desde a busca por produtos até a conclusão do pagamento. Para viabilizar esse modelo, bancos e empresas de pagamentos trabalham no desenvolvimento de sistemas que permitam transações seguras, integração com plataformas de comércio eletrônico e conversão de comandos dos consumidores em operações financeiras. Segundo pesquisa da Nexus citada no estudo, 37% dos brasileiros já fizeram ao menos uma compra influenciada por Inteligência Artificial. Já um levantamento da Worldpay aponta que 40% dos consumidores do País estão dispostos a delegar todo o processo de compra a assistentes de IA. O sucesso desse modelo dependerá de investimentos em infraestrutura tecnológica, canais de relacionamento com o consumidor e mecanismos de controle e segurança de dados, tanto no B2C (comércio entre empresas e consumidores) quanto no B2B (transações entre empresas). Também será necessário estabelecer mecanismos para confirmar quem está autorizado a agir em nome do consumidor, com qual finalidade e dentro de quais limites. Relacionamento com o banco Segundo a pesquisa da Febraban, o orçamento do setor para investimentos em tecnologia deve alcançar R$ 50 bilhões em 2026, dos quais cerca de R$ 3 bilhões serão destinados à Inteligência Artificial. O levantamento também aponta que 92% dos bancos brasileiros já registram ganhos de eficiência com o uso da IA. O uso avançado de Inteligência Artificial pode reduzir custos operacionais, criar fontes de receita e ampliar a oferta de serviços personalizados. A tendência é que essas ferramentas passem a interpretar informações, recomendar soluções e executar operações dentro dos limites estabelecidos pelos bancos. A mudança também se estende a plataformas fora do sistema bancário. Ferramentas de IA já auxiliam consumidores na pesquisa e comparação de opções antes de decisões de compra ou contratação. Segundo dados globais apresentados no estudo, cerca de um em cada três consumidores utiliza IA conversacional para buscar informações sobre finanças pessoais. Tokenização avança na infraestrutura A tokenização, que permite representar ativos e direitos em formato digital, começa a avançar para além da fase de testes e a integrar a infraestrutura financeira. Segundo a pesquisa, os bancos poderão atuar na emissão, custódia, liquidação e distribuição desses ativos. Entre as possibilidades estão o uso de dinheiro digital, a tokenização de depósitos e operações em mercados que funcionam 24 horas por dia, todos os dias da semana. Segurança digital e computação quântica Os bancos brasileiros destinam cerca de R$ 5 bilhões por ano à cibersegurança, o equivalente a 10% do orçamento total de tecnologia. Embora a Inteligência Artificial ajude a identificar e responder a ameaças, a tecnologia também pode ser usada por criminosos para golpes. O estudo destaca a necessidade de monitorar o uso de ferramentas de IA e estabelecer limites para agentes que executam tarefas e transações. O levantamento também recomenda maior atenção aos fornecedores de tecnologia e o compartilhamento de informações sobre ameaças e golpes entre os bancos, como forma de prevenir incidentes e manter os serviços em funcionamento. articles.title: Roldão aposta em low cost para renovar loja na Grande São Paulo
articles.titleKo: Roldão aposta em low cost para renovar loja na Grande São Paulo
articles.originalSummary: O Roldão Atacadista reinaugurou sua unidade em Franco da Rocha, na Grande São Paulo, com atuação baseada no modelo low-cost, que prioriza a redução de custos operacionais e investimentos em serviços e produtos considerados essenciais para o consumidor. A loja passou por uma modernização e ganhou novos espaços e um mix ampliado. Entre as novidades está uma área da Vestcasa , com produtos de cama, mesa, banho e utilidades domésticas. A unidade também oferece serviços como açougue e padaria, além de uma seção de hortifrúti. “O low-cost model parte de uma premissa clara: reduzir custos que não geram valor ao consumidor e investir naquilo que realmente importa. Queremos entregar qualidade, variedade e preços agressivos, ampliando o poder de compra dos nossos clientes”, afirma Victória Roldão, gerente de Marketing e Trade Marketing do Roldão Atacadista. Roldão inaugura maior loja em São Vicente São Vicente, no litoral paulista, recebeu a maior unidade do Roldão Atacadista. Com 22 mil metros quadrados, a loja combina atacarejo e galeria comercial na mesma operação, além de contar com empório de frios em parceria com a BRF e açougue operado pela Marfrig. A área de atendimento conta com 16 caixas tradicionais e seis terminais de autoatendimento, em linha com o avanço da automação no varejo alimentar, com o objetivo de reduzir o tempo de espera. O funcionamento segue o padrão das demais unidades da rede, com atendimento de segunda a sábado, das 7h às 22h, e aos domingos, das 8h às 20h, inclusive em feriados. A unidade dispõe de 405 vagas de estacionamento, sendo 269 regulares, 80 para motocicletas, 23 destinadas a idosos, 17 para gestantes e 16 reservadas a pessoas com deficiência (PNE). O espaço foi dimensionado para acompanhar o fluxo previsto de clientes, especialmente em períodos de maior movimento. A galeria integrada, composta por um conjunto de lojas e serviços anexos à unidade principal, reúne operações de diferentes segmentos, como a chocolateria Brasil Cacau , a academia Smart Fit , a lotérica da Caixa Econômica Federal , além de marcas como 10 Amore, Doutor Sorriso, Grão & Glacê, Jockey, Kasado Express, Laundry Mat, Macaros Tech, Ótica Ysa, Plush 4 Fun, Popular e Tangerina. Ele não deu detalhes e disse que ainda não havia informado seus próprios funcionários sobre a medida. O presidente republicano exortou os americanos a acolherem a construção de centros de dados em suas comunidades e a obterem concessões dos desenvolvedores, repetindo um argumento que apresentou antes das eleições de meio de mandato. “Vocês devem tirar proveito dos centros de dados”, disse Trump em uma entrevista à imprensa na Casa Branca. “Façam com que eles paguem a vocês, façam com que paguem à sua comunidade, mas não os impeçam de operar.” O Senado, liderado pelos republicanos, aprovou na quinta-feira, 19, uma legislação bipartidária que visa acelerar as análises de licenciamento para a construção de usinas de energia, linhas de transmissão e outras infraestruturas energéticas, à medida que os legisladores buscam aumentar o abastecimento energético do país para atender à crescente demanda e reduzir os preços da eletricidade. As mudanças abrangentes da legislação reduziriam o prazo para o início de grandes projetos de energia e garantiriam que os data centers paguem pela energia que consomem. A indignação em relação aos data centers e ao aumento dos preços da eletricidade ajudou a dar início a uma onda de democratas que se comprometeram a reprimir esses gigantes devoradores de energia. Espera-se que se siga um ambiente regulatório mais rigoroso para os gigantes da IA e os desenvolvedores de data centers, mesmo que Trump – talvez o maior defensor do setor – adie qualquer ação repressiva federal. Apesar do apoio de Trump, os data centers que alimentam o boom da Inteligência Artificial tornaram-se politicamente tóxicos. O setor de tecnologia afirma ter entendido a mensagem. Além de ampliar os incentivos financeiros, representantes do Google e da Meta disseram, em entrevistas à AP, que estão tentando combater a desconfiança por meio de maior transparência com as comunidades onde pretendem construir. As empresas também estão assumindo compromissos para reduzir seu impacto sobre o meio ambiente e oferecendo garantias de que os data centers elevarão o valor dos imóveis locais – tudo isso enquanto afirmam que a IA é uma força positiva para a economia americana, apesar dos céticos. Com as comunidades anfitriãs em todo o território dos EUA se voltando contra seus gigantescos data centers, os gigantes da tecnologia americana prometem receber menos recursos dos contribuintes, manter menos segredos ou injetar mais dinheiro nas comunidades dispostas a permitir a instalação desses centros de servidores. O governo Trump divulgou na segunda-feira novas regras para restringir o acesso remoto a chips e servidores avançados dos EUA, marcando o mais recente passo para limitar a capacidade da China de usar chips americanos para treinar seus melhores modelos de inteligência artificial. A medida atualiza as restrições às exportações de chips avançados para data centers de IA instalados no exterior, o que deve dificultar o acesso de empresas chinesas a tais componentes. As novas regras afetam o envio dos semicondutores para vários países, entre os quais o Brasil. articles.title: Maksoud Plaza: hotel de luxo fechado em 2021 pode virar condomínio com 398 apartamentos
articles.titleKo: Maksoud Plaza: hotel de luxo fechado em 2021 pode virar condomínio com 398 apartamentos
articles.originalSummary: Fechado em 2021 após enfrentar desafios financeiros por causa da pandemia e disputas entre os sócios, o antigo hotel de luxo Maksoud Plaza pode virar um edifício de uso misto, com apartamentos residenciais e unidades de hospedagem. De acordo com a prefeitura de SP, o prédio está em análise para uma reforma que prepara o novo empreendimento, ainda sem nome definido. “A Secretaria Municipal de Urbanismo e Licenciamento (SMUL) informa que consta em análise na pasta pedido de Alvará de Aprovação de Reforma para o local onde funcionava o antigo Hotel Maksoud (Rua São Carlos do Pinhal, 424)”, informou a Prefeitura. O edifício do hotel foi arrematado em 2011 pelos irmãos Fernando e Jussara Simões, da Simpar, para quitar dívidas trabalhistas, mas recursos na Justiça e impasses entre os herdeiros de Henry Maksoud sobre a entrega do prédio e o destino dos bens se arrastaram por anos. Procurados, os sócios da Simpar não quiseram comentar sobre o empreendimento. O projeto do empreendimento terá 398 apartamentos residenciais, 152 unidades de uso não residencial (hospedagem) e cinco lojas no térreo. O edifício terá ainda seis subsolos, térreo e mais 26 andares. No estacionamento, entre vagas para moradores e hóspedes, estão previstas 595 posições. A Prefeitura informou que, até o momento, não há previsão de data para a conclusão da análise. “O pedido segue em tramitação com verificação do atendimento à legislação urbanística e edilícia vigente”, diz a nota. Em 2020, o Maksoud Plaza entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial com dívidas de mais de R$ 500 milhões e fechou as portas no ano seguinte. O hotel foi símbolo de luxo na capital paulista nos anos 80 e 90 e é conhecido, também, por apresentações do tenor Frank Sinatra, bem como por ter hospedado vários artistas. O fechamento do hotel encerrou a disputa pela propriedade. Em seu perfil público no LinkedIn, Henry Maksoud Neto, herdeiro do hotel, conta a história do encerramento e venda do imóvel. “Negociei e executei, com sucesso, a liquidação ordenada e o desinvestimento estratégico do portfólio imobiliário e dos ativos corporativos do grupo, transformando uma crise histórica aguda em uma saída institucional definitiva e saneada”, diz o perfil na rede social, em uma seção sobre sua trajetória no Maksoud Group. Procurado, Maksoud Neto disse que, desde que entregou o prédio em 2022, não tem mais informações sobre o destino do imóvel. articles.title: Norte lidera participação de bebidas alcoólicas nos mercados autônomos
articles.titleKo: Norte lidera participação de bebidas alcoólicas nos mercados autônomos
articles.originalSummary: Nos mercados autônomos do Norte, as bebidas alcoólicas representam 45,1% das unidades entre os 20 produtos mais vendidos. O percentual é mais que o dobro do registrado no Sul, onde a categoria responde por 21,8%, de acordo com levantamento do market4u . . A diferença é influenciada pelo resultado do Pará, que concentra 83,9% das unidades analisadas na região. Quando os Estados recebem o mesmo peso na comparação, a participação das bebidas alcoólicas no Norte cai para 31,3%. O recorte por Estado mostra que o Pará tem a maior participação da categoria entre os 20 produtos mais vendidos, com 49,3%, seguido pela Bahia, com 47,5%. Já Santa Catarina apresenta o menor percentual, de 14,9%. As bebidas não alcoólicas aparecem à frente das alcoólicas em 18 das 20 unidades da Federação incluídas no levantamento. Pará e Bahia são as únicas exceções. Diferenças entre bebidas não alcoólicas O levantamento também mostra diferenças na participação das bebidas não alcoólicas. Os refrigerantes reprsentam 47% das unidades entre os 20 produtos mais vendidos no Centro-Oeste e a 45,4% no Sul. No Distrito Federal, a categoria responde por 51,6% do ranking local, enquanto na Paraíba representa 23,3%, uma diferença de 28,3 pontos percentuais. Outro destaque é a participação dos refrigerantes zero ou sem açúcar, que representam 60,5% das unidades da categoria. O percentual supera 50% em 18 das 20 unidades da Federação analisadas. No Nordeste, a fatia chega a 69,3%, a maior entre as regiões. As águas minerais têm maior participação em Pernambuco, onde representam 34,6% dos produtos listados. No recorte regional, Sudeste e Nordeste registram os maiores percentuais, com 19,2% e 18,6%, respectivamente. Os energéticos também apresentam diferenças conforme a região. O Sudeste registra o maior volume absoluto, com 143.327 unidades, seguido pelo Sul, com 129.716. Quando considerada a participação da categoria no total de produtos mais vendidos, porém, o Sul assume a liderança. Os energéticos representam 10% do ranking regional, ante 2,8% no Sudeste. Assim, a participação proporcional no Sul é 3,6 vezes maior que a do Sudeste, apesar do menor volume absoluto de unidades comercializadas. Os percentuais indicam a participação de cada categoria entre os 20 produtos mais vendidos, e não o total de vendas da rede, o consumo por habitante ou o volume geral de bebidas comercializadas. A base analisada não informa o período das vendas nem o número de lojas consideradas. articles.title: Skechers abre unidade de 363 m² em outlet no interior paulista
articles.titleKo: Skechers abre unidade de 363 m² em outlet no interior paulista
articles.originalSummary: A Skechers inaugurou uma loja no Catarina Fashion Outlet, em São Roque, em São Paulo, com 363,5 m² de área total. O espaço é a oitava unidade própria da marca no Brasil e integra o plano de expansão da empresa. A unidade oferece mais de 9 mil itens e 700 modelos de calçados e acessórios. O portfólio contempla diferentes estilos, ocasiões e atividades, com categorias como Bobs Sport, Go Walk, Go Run, Tech Running, Kids, Soccer, Pickleball, Basketball, Active, Court and Classic, Work e Sport. “Estamos avançando com nosso plano de expansão no Brasil, levando a experiência Skechers a novos mercados e aproximando cada vez mais a marca dos consumidores.”, afirma Sabrina Mônaco, country manager da Skechers Brasil. Loja no Catarina Fashion Outlet, em São Roque Com cerca de 5,3 mil lojas em todo o mundo, a Skechers está presente em seis continentes. No Brasil, a marca mantém sua atuação por meio de lojas próprias, pontos de venda parceiros e grandes varejistas, além de comercializar suas coleções e tecnologias pelo comércio eletrônico. Com faturamento previsto de mais de US$ 10,5 bilhões neste ano, a Skechers planeja ampliar sua presença no País e chegar a 100 lojas próprias nos próximos anos. O plano de expansão começou a ser desenhado há cerca de um ano e meio, quando a matriz decidiu alinhar a operação brasileira aos padrões globais da marca. Para iniciar este novo ciclo, a companhia investiu dezenas de milhões de reais, com recursos destinados a campanhas de marketing, aquisição de estoque, ampliação da estrutura de distribuição e um novo escritório corporativo em São Paulo, construído em menos de 65 dias. A companhia projeta dobrar o volume de negócios no Brasil a cada dois ou três anos. articles.title: De olho em mercado de R$ 2 bilhões, Swift estreia na culinária japonesa

articles.originalSummary: A Swift, marca da JBS, está entrando no segmento de culinária japonesa com uma linha de produtos voltada ao consumo doméstico. O movimento busca ampliar a presença da empresa em um mercado que movimentou mais de R$ 2 bilhões no food service brasileiro nos 12 meses encerrados em junho de 2025, crescimento de 9% na comparação anual, segundo dados do CREST/Instituto Foodservice Brasil (IFB). A estratégia é aproveitar a demanda por gastronomia asiática e oferecer alternativas ao consumo em restaurantes e ao delivery. O portfólio reúne produtos congelados e semiprontos que permitem preparar refeições japonesas em casa, com opções para consumo individual ou em grupo. Entre os lançamentos estão sashimis de salmão, atum e peixe-prego defumado, já fatiados e congelados, além de tartar de salmão, shimeji, edamame, guiozas de carne suína e vegetais e harumakis de queijo e vegetais. Alguns produtos podem ser preparados em aproximadamente dez minutos na air fryer. “Queremos que preparar uma refeição japonesa em casa seja uma escolha tão prática quanto pedir de um restaurante. Para isso, simplificamos etapas que exigem mais técnica, como o corte dos peixes”, afirma Aécio Patuzzi, diretor comercial da Swift. A entrada na categoria faz parte da estratégia da companhia de ampliar as ocasiões de consumo e fortalecer seu portfólio de marca própria. Atualmente, a Swift mantém mais de 480 lojas físicas e pontos de venda no varejo paulista, além de operar por canais digitais. Os produtos da nova linha custam entre R$ 15,90 e R$ 30,90 e chegam de forma escalonada às lojas, ao e-commerce e ao aplicativo da marca. Para 2027, a empresa prevê ampliar o portfólio com hot roll de salmão, ceviche de tilápia, salmão para poke, tempurá de camarão e mix para yakisoba. articles.originalSummary: A Bershka inaugurou uma nova loja no ParkShopping, em Brasília. Com 555 m² de área de vendas, a unidade possui quatro salões comerciais e dois acessos, em um projeto que privilegia a integração dos ambientes e a experiência de compra. O espaço reúne as linhas Bershka, BSK e MAN, cada uma com identidade visual própria. A área Bershka combina revestimentos minerais brancos e superfícies de melamina, enquanto a BSK se destaca pelos azulejos rosa. Já a seção masculina mantém uma paleta neutra, com revestimentos cerâmicos em tons claros. A arquitetura aposta em materiais naturais e elementos contemporâneos. O teto, composto por módulos de madeira de bordo e luminárias suspensas, é um dos destaques do projeto. Nos provadores, o mesmo material reveste paredes e cabines, criando um ambiente mais acolhedor. A música também integra o conceito da unidade. Caixas de som revestidas em madeira foram incorporadas aos pilares centrais, transformando elementos estruturais em pontos de destaque. A loja conta ainda com módulos de atendimento assistido nos caixas. A proposta é combinar moda, design e experiência em um ambiente que valoriza a circulação dos clientes e a identidade das diferentes linhas da marca. Em setembro, a marca também inaugurou unidade no Rio de Janeiro . Em março, a primeira loja chegou ao Brasil, no Morumbi Shopping. Lançou, na mesma fase, sua plataforma online, marcando o início da presença no País. Pela plataforma digital da Bershka, os clientes podem verificar a disponibilidade de produtos e localizar peças dentro da loja. Também é possível fazer pedidos online e retirar na loja em cerca de duas horas. O espaço ainda conta com caixas dedicados para devoluções, um ponto de retirada de pedidos online e uma área de self checkout. articles.title: Taco John’s Brings Back Holiday Favorites Nachos Navidad and Apple Grande
articles.titleKo: Taco John’s Brings Back Holiday Favorites Nachos Navidad and Apple Grande
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . For those craving a winter treat, Taco John’s welcomes back one of its most requested seasonal menu items, the Apple Grande. From the comeback of its classic beef chili to the return of Nachos Navidad and fan-favorite Apple Grande, Taco John’s is giving fans plenty of reasons to celebrate the season, and the bold flavors of West-Mex. “The holidays are all about traditions, and at Taco John’s, that includes bringing back the seasonal flavors our guests know and love,” said Kevin Flaherty, Chief Marketing Officer at Taco John’s. “From favorite menu items to opportunities to give back in our communities, we’re serving up the food, value and holiday spirit that make this time of year so special.” For those craving a winter treat, Taco John’s welcomes back one of its most requested seasonal menu items, the Apple Grande. This sweet-and-savory treat features a crispy cinnamon-sugar tostada topped with warm apple pie filling, Cheddar cheese, and cinnamon candy flavored seasoning. Taco John’s is bringing back its Nachos Navidad, a festive, colorful classic featuring crispy red, green and white corn chips fried in-house daily and sprinkled with sea salt then layered with warm nacho cheese, seasoned 100% North American Beef, refried beans, four-cheese blend, diced tomatoes, sour cream, and guacamole. For nearly three decades, participating Taco John’s franchisees have donated a portion of Nachos Navidad proceeds to worthy causes within their local communities, raising millions of dollars to support hundreds of organizations in Taco John’s markets. The beloved holiday tradition brings together great food and the spirit of giving, making every order meaningful. Beyond menu highlights, Taco John’s is spreading even more holiday cheer with special offers* through the in-app TJ Rewards program throughout the season: November 30-December 6 – Cozy Week of Deals: Taco John’s is warming up the season with a week of special offers, giving guests even more ways to enjoy their favorites while celebrating the holidays. December 17-19 – Feed Your Fiesta Rewards Exclusive: Feed your crew for less with deals on sharable items as families and friends come together to make merry this season! Taco John’s is also helping guests give (and get) a little more this season. Now through December 31, guests who purchase $25 in gift cards will receive a $5 bonus card, redeemable Jan. 1 – Feb. 28, 2027. articles.title: Krystal Celebrates the Holidays with 31 Days of Deals and Giveaways
articles.titleKo: Krystal Celebrates the Holidays with 31 Days of Deals and Giveaways
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Twelve days of Christmas? Krystal is going for 31. The Southern-born fast-food chain is bringing back Krystalmas: A Season of Merry Moments, delivering an entire month of holiday savings, festive flavors and chances to win. From Dec. 1 through 31, Club Krystal members can enjoy a new deal every day on guest favorites, from breakfast biscuits to the brand’s signature square sliders. Whether fueling up for holiday shopping or bringing home a Sackful to share, members can celebrate the season without breaking the bank. Among the deals guests can look forward to are $4 Merry Mornings, featuring any biscuit, small tots and a small coffee during breakfast hours, and Jingle Bucks Thursdays, when Club Krystal members can score Original Krystals for just $1 each, up to five per member. And that’s just a taste of what’s in store, with additional daily deals and surprises waiting to be unwrapped throughout December. “The holidays are all about finding little moments of joy, and we want Krystal to be part of those moments,” said Kaitlin Kees, Senior Director of Marketing at Krystal. “Whether guests are fueling up while holiday shopping or picking up a Steamer Box on the way to grandmother’s house, Krystalmas gives our loyal fans more ways to enjoy their favorites at a great value all season long.” A Chance to Win a Holiday Getaway The holiday cheer doesn’t stop with daily deals. Krystal is teaming up with Coca-Cola to give Club Krystal members a shot at a theme park getaway, complete with tickets and travel funds. From Dec. 1 through 31, Club Krystal members who purchase a Coca-Cola beverage or a Krystal combo with a Coca-Cola beverage through the Krystal app will automatically earn an entry into the Krystalmas Coca-Cola Sweepstakes. Each qualifying order counts as an entry, giving members another chance to win throughout the month. Even More Holiday Savings with the $9.94 Holiday Haul Krystal is extending the holiday savings to all guests with its $9.94 Holiday Haul. With holiday shopping, travel and family gatherings stretching budgets this time of year, Krystal is making it easier to feed a hungry crew without breaking the bank. Available Saturdays and Sundays from Nov. 21 through Jan. 3, the offer includes 10 Original Krystals for just $9.94, a nod to the brand’s 94th year. Unlike the daily Krystalmas deals, the Holiday Haul is available to all guests ordering in-store and online, with no Club Krystal membership required. Guests can join Club Krystal through the Krystal app or visit Krystal.com/rewards to access the holiday offers. For restaurant locations and additional information, visit Krystal.com. Krystalmas offers are exclusive to Club Krystal members Dec. 1–31 at participating locations. Prices, participation, offer limits and availability may vary. Holiday Haul is available to all guests in-store and online on Saturdays and Sundays from Nov. 21, 2026, through Jan. 3, 2027 at participating locations. articles.title: Software Companies Guarantee Performance. Why Don’t Advertising Agencies?
articles.titleKo: Software Companies Guarantee Performance. Why Don’t Advertising Agencies?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . For too many years, agencies have kept themselves out of the line of fire. Over the past 12 months, I’ve talked with restaurant marketers across the food franchise space, and a clear theme came through: a wave of new expectations is being placed on them by their brands. They were all pretty unified that they are under tremendous pressure, and the strongest pressure point is showing unit-level performance within 90 days. Unit-level economics is what keeps franchisees, CEOs, boards, and private equity at ease, and marketers are expected to move that number fast. If they can’t show that number moving in the right direction, they will not be granted time to develop new creative that builds brand momentum, improve their tech stack, or address anything else. These are the items marketers used to tackle first to bring cohesiveness and structure to a brand. Now, time limits in the role have pushed them to the back burner. No room to build, no room to fix, no room for anything but survival. Under this pressure, marketers need a new mode of support from their agency partners. They don’t need another report or another promise. They need a partner willing to share the risk, not just the credit, when the results come in. A 150-Year-Old Model The modern agency relationship traces back to Philadelphia. In the 1870s, N.W. Ayer & Son introduced the “open contract,” which put the agent squarely on the advertiser’s side instead of playing a balancing act between channel rep and brand rep. In the 150 years since, the basic advertising agency model for performance and compensation has stayed the same. The agency buys media, reports on deliverables like impressions and clicks, and gets paid either way. We’ve added influencers, creative development, loyalty, and other services along the way, but the model itself hasn’t changed significantly. The Technology Caught Up Everything around that model has changed. Attribution has made huge strides since the advent of Google, and with online ordering, media optimization has become far more effective, which leads to better revenue performance at the location level. POS systems and loyalty marketing give brands a closer touch with their guests, which leads to better activation. Today we can run media location by location, attribute online revenue to each one, and use restaurant data platforms to read the results while factoring in inclement weather and other variables. Influencer marketing is moving toward full attribution, and other media are moving in the same direction. For instance, we are running a social campaign with lead gen activation that sends guests a $5-off-$25 Toast coupon code by SMS, and we’ve validated a 5x return in-store revenue to media spend for this campaign. Stack enough measurable tactics like that together, and you can predict what a location will do. The technology caught up. The agency model hasn’t. Software Figured This Out Years Ago Software companies have long let the product prove itself before the customer carries the full risk. Pilots, 90-day trials, and service-level commitments with credits when the vendor falls short are standard in SaaS. The vendor stands behind what it sells because it can measure whether it delivered. Advertising has not followed, and there is no longer a technical reason why. With food marketers in such a box, isn’t it time for agencies to shoulder more of the burden? What an Agency Guarantee Could Look Like Borrow straight from the SaaS playbook. A brand selects a test group of its locations. Each one gets a revenue goal, measured against the same period last year and agreed by the brand and the agency before any work begins. That goal should cover every channel the location has: dine-in, takeout, catering, and third-party delivery. articles.title: NRF 2027: O que Walmart, Zara, Levi’s, Etsy e Target vão levar ao palco nesta edição
articles.titleKo: NRF 2027: O que Walmart, Zara, Levi’s, Etsy e Target vão levar ao palco nesta edição
articles.originalSummary: Como transformar Inteligência Artificial em vendas? Esta tem sido a pergunta do milhão no mercado. De que maneira as marcas tradicionais podem continuar relevantes diante das mudanças no comportamento do consumidor? E como recuperar o crescimento sem depender apenas de promoções e descontos? Essas são algumas das questões que estarão no centro das apresentações de Walmart, Zara, Levi’s, Etsy e Target na NRF 2027: Retail’s Big Show, que acontece entre 10 e 12 de janeiro, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos. As cinco empresas estão confirmadas na programação do evento e levarão aos debates diferentes perspectivas sobre as transformações do varejo. Entre os assuntos anunciados estão o avanço dos agentes de Inteligência Artificial, a personalização da jornada de compra, a evolução das lojas e dos canais digitais e a busca por crescimento sustentável. A programação antecipa discussões que interessam diretamente ao varejo brasileiro, especialmente em um cenário de pressão sobre margens, transformação dos canais de venda e consumidores cada vez mais exigentes. Walmart: quando a IA passa a participar da compra Uma das apresentações será a do Walmart, que reunirá David Guggina, CEO do Walmart nos Estados Unidos, e Chris Nicholas, CEO do Walmart International. Na sessão “One Walmart, Many Markets: Leading the Next Era of Retail”, os executivos discutirão como a companhia está respondendo às mudanças nas expectativas dos consumidores em diferentes mercados, com atenção à Inteligência Artificial e ao chamado comércio agêntico ( agentic commerce ). O tema envolve uma transformação na jornada de compra: ferramentas de IA que deixam de apenas recomendar produtos e passam a participar de etapas como descoberta, comparação e seleção. Para os varejistas, o avanço desse modelo traz questões sobre como os consumidores encontrarão produtos, como as marcas disputarão visibilidade e qual será o papel das plataformas digitais nas decisões de compra. Zara: como continuar relevante sem perder a identidade No varejo de moda, o destaque será Óscar García Maceiras, CEO da Inditex, grupo controlador da Zara e de marcas como Pull&Bear, Bershka, Massimo Dutti e Stradivarius. Na apresentação “The Future of Fashion Retail: Staying True, Moving Forward”, o executivo discutirá a evolução do modelo de negócios da companhia e sua capacidade de responder às mudanças no comportamento do consumidor. O enfoque estará na combinação entre identidade de marca, desenvolvimento de produtos, experiência nas lojas e canais digitais. A Zara construiu parte de sua trajetória sobre a capacidade de interpretar as preferências dos consumidores e adaptar seu modelo comercial. Na NRF, a discussão será como preservar esses princípios em um ambiente de consumo que exige respostas cada vez mais rápidas e experiências integradas. Para o varejo brasileiro de moda, a apresentação traz questões sobre diferenciação, agilidade comercial e o papel da loja física em uma operação cada vez mais digital. Levi’s e Etsy: como preparar o negócio para consumidores que compram com ajuda da IA A Levi’s e a Etsy dividirão uma apresentação dedicada à transformação das empresas diante do avanço da Inteligência Artificial agêntica. Jason Gowans, vice-presidente executivo e diretor de Digital e Tecnologia da Levi Strauss & Co., e Rafe Colburn, diretor de Produto e Tecnologia da Etsy, discutirão como estão incorporando IA às operações e à experiência do consumidor. As empresas partem de modelos distintos. A Levi’s está ampliando sua atuação direta ao consumidor e suas capacidades digitais, enquanto busca evoluir de uma marca historicamente associada ao jeans para uma empresa de moda e estilo de vida com portfólio mais amplo. A Etsy, marketplace especializado em produtos criativos e diferenciados, enfrenta o desafio de preservar o valor da criatividade humana em um ambiente comercial cada vez mais automatizado. articles.title: Ruby Tuesday is Going Back to What Made it Great
articles.titleKo: Ruby Tuesday is Going Back to What Made it Great
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ruby Tuesday's new menu contains approximately 25 percent fewer items and puts greater focus on the company's signature categories. Ruby Tuesday wants customers to remember why they fell in love with the brand in the first place. The casual-dining chain has been serving guests since 1972, building a reputation around its Garden Bar, burgers, ribs, and familiar American comfort food. But more than five decades of history have also brought challenges, including a crowded menu, inconsistent execution, and a reliance on discounts to attract customers. The concept also notably filed for bankruptcy in 2020 and has shuttered hundreds of restaurants over the past decade. Now, the company, with around 160 U.S. locations, according to its website, is making significant changes to its food, pricing, marketing, and restaurant experience in an effort to reconnect with longtime customers and introduce itself to a new generation. CMO Kevin FitzPatrick says the changes respond to mounting financial pressures on consumers and the company’s need to deliver a more consistent dining experience. The previous menu had grown substantially, partly because of limited-time promotions that introduced numerous dishes. That expansion created operational complexity and made it more difficult for customers to navigate the offerings. Introduced nationwide November 17, the new menu contains approximately 25 percent fewer items and puts greater focus on the company’s signature categories. The decision was informed by sales data, customer reviews, and conversations with restaurant employees. FitzPatrick says the company identified dishes that contributed relatively little to sales and could be eliminated without significantly limiting customers’ choices. Some pasta and chicken selections were removed, allowing employees to concentrate on preparing fewer dishes consistently and improving food quality. “I’ve done a lot of consumer research in my past, but like the biggest source of consumer research is sales data. Customers are voting with their wallets, and we had a lot of items that just didn’t have a lot of a lot of reps,” FitzPatrick says. Ruby Tuesday expanded its burger selection with the Jalapeno Smashed and Garlic Parmesan Smashed burgers and brought back the Colossal Burger, a longtime customer favorite. The Colossal Burger had previously returned as a limited-time offering in May 2022, but customers continued requesting it after the promotion ended. The chain also upgraded its chicken sandwiches and entrées to feature eight-ounce chicken breasts and introduced appetizers such as Pretzel Bites, Loaded Fries and Tots, and a Dip Trio. Other signature dishes, including the Hickory Bourbon Salmon and fall-off-the-bone ribs, received greater prominence. The chain previously relied on rotating daily promotions and coupons, a strategy that appealed to its established customer base but required guests to keep track of which offers were available on particular days. Its new Everyday Fresh Meals platform replaces that complexity with consistent pricing seven days a week. Introduced nationally in November, the program features 13 entrées across four price tiers of $9.99, $11.99, $14.99, and $17.99. Each meal includes an entrée, unlimited trips to the Garden Bar, and a bottomless beverage. Selections range from burgers and chicken sandwiches to Cajun Chicken Pasta and a half rack of ribs. The company believes the combination offers a compelling alternative to dining at home, especially as consumers face elevated grocery prices and other household expenses. “It’s on the menu, so it’s easy for them to understand the value they’re getting, and know that they can get it anytime they want, not just on Tuesdays, not just on Thursdays, as an example,” FitzPatrick says. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Before joining P.F. Chang's in November 2026, Breitegan spent nearly 11 years with Grimaldi's Pizzeria, rising to Chief People Officer and serving on the leadership team and advisory board. P.F. Chang’s announced today the appointment of Danny Breitegan as Senior Vice President of Human Resources. He leads the company’s HR function, focusing on cultural alignment, team member engagement, organizational design and building high-performing teams. Breitegan brings 25 years of progressive HR leadership experience across restaurant and hospitality, oil and gas, aerospace manufacturing, real estate and corporate relocation, and renewable energy. He has worked for three Fortune 100 organizations and led HR initiatives and day-to-day operations across the U.S., Asia-Pacific, EMEA, Latin America and Canada. Before joining P.F. Chang’s in November 2026, Breitegan spent nearly 11 years with Grimaldi’s Pizzeria, rising to Chief People Officer and serving on the leadership team and advisory board. He led HR strategy for more than 2,000 employees, overseeing talent acquisition, employee engagement and cultural alignment, compensation and benefits, performance management, data analytics and payroll. At P.F. Chang’s, Breitegan will guide efforts to attract, develop and retain talented team members and leaders. He will also help bring the company’s PRIDE Values—Passion, Respect, Innovation, Discipline and Excellence—to life across the team member experience. “Danny’s broad HR leadership experience and background in the restaurant industry make him a strong addition to our leadership team,” said Jim Mazany, Chief Executive Officer of P.F. Chang’s. “His focus on building engaged, high-performing teams will help us strengthen our culture and bring our PRIDE values to life across the organization. We’re excited to welcome him as we continue to build for the future.” “I’m excited to join P.F. Chang’s and contribute to a growing brand with such a distinct identity and sense of purpose,” said Breitegan. “Throughout my career, I’ve seen how a strong culture helps people and businesses succeed, and I look forward to bringing that perspective to the role.” Breitegan holds a Bachelor of Arts in Management from Texas Christian University and a Master of Business Administration from Texas A&M University. He is certified as a Senior Professional in Human Resources (SPHR) by the HR Certification Institute and as a Senior Certified Professional (SHRM-SCP) by the Society for Human Resource Management. He also holds a Six Sigma Green Belt certification. The post P.F. Chang’s Appoints Danny Breitegan SVP of Human Resources appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Smalls Sliders Makes Room for More Restaurants
articles.titleKo: Smalls Sliders Makes Room for More Restaurants
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A shipping container helped make Smalls Sliders one of the industry’s most recognizable emerging brands. Now, the company is discovering that its signature building can also stand in the way of expansion. Since opening its first restaurant in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in 2019, Smalls has built its identity around bright orange shipping-container restaurants known as Cans. The compact buildings, streamlined kitchens, and focused menu of cheeseburger sliders, waffle fries, and milkshakes have provided a foundation for franchise growth. But the format comes with real estate limitations. A standalone Can cannot easily fit into a downtown shopping district, an airport terminal, or a college campus. Some communities also prohibit drive-thrus, eliminating potential development opportunities before franchisees can seriously consider them. Smalls is preparing to address those obstacles with its first inline and endcap restaurant formats, which will allow franchisees to open locations in existing retail spaces, shopping centers, and other commercial properties. A rendering of Smalls Sliders’ endcap design. Chief development officer Ryan Crumley says the expansion is a natural evolution of the business, giving operators more freedom to pursue opportunities that previously fell outside the company’s real estate requirements. The shift could open new markets, reduce certain development expenses, and eventually increase the number of restaurants Smalls can open annually. However, the company is not abandoning the Can that helped establish its identity. The new formats will complement the standalone prototype, which will continue serving as the primary vehicle for introducing customers to Smalls. Meanwhile, the new designs will allow operators to consider dense urban districts with substantial pedestrian traffic, suburban shopping centers, malls, and multi-tenant commercial properties. Existing buildings could also offer financial advantages over developing a standalone restaurant from the ground up. An inline or endcap location would generally eliminate the need to construct an entire building shell, parking lot, and utility infrastructure. Those savings could lower the initial investment required of franchisees, although Smalls has not established specific cost comparisons or profitability projections. Crumley says the company expects to learn more as the first locations begin operating. “At the end of the day, our goal and [the franchisees’] goal is for them to be very profitable, and the more you can make that initial investment economical, the better, the faster they get to that point,” Crumley says. The potential savings are only one consideration. Smalls also wants to ensure that opening restaurants in existing buildings does not sacrifice the operational efficiencies that have helped distinguish its business model. The original Can was developed around the needs of employees working inside the restaurant. Its kitchen layout and processes were established first, with the physical structure built to accommodate them. Smalls is applying that same thinking to the new formats, allowing employees to operate in familiar environments regardless of the building type. That consistency is important as franchisees pursue multiple restaurant formats within their territories. A team member moving from a standalone Can to an endcap location should encounter essentially the same kitchen procedures and workflow. The exterior presents a different challenge. Smalls has invested years in making its signature Smorange color and industrial shipping-container appearance instantly recognizable. Recreating those elements in a traditional retail building requires some creativity, especially when landlords have their own architectural standards. articles.title: Com a IA, o cliente sabe tudo. Por que ainda precisa de você?
articles.titleKo: Com a IA, o cliente sabe tudo. Por que ainda precisa de você?
articles.originalSummary: Durante décadas, a autoridade do vendedor veio de saber o que o cliente não sabia: o preço praticado, a diferença entre versões, a letra miúda do contrato. Essa informação continua valendo. Só ficou fácil de conseguir, e quem vivia dela precisa recalcular o próprio valor. O mercado imobiliário americano mostra até onde isso já foi. Segundo a Zillow (2026) , 45% dos compradores que usaram IA na compra disseram ter deixado a ferramenta negociar em seu nome. Mesmo assim, 85% contrataram um corretor. E só 7% o escolheram pela tecnologia. Quando li o relatório, voltei a uma sala de reunião de poucas semanas antes. Eu tinha mostrado ao time comercial de uma grande siderúrgica como o papel de quem vende mudou com a tecnologia. Primeiro, o vendedor sabia mais, e o cliente dava semanas para uma resposta. Depois, o cliente passou a cotar cinco fornecedores ao mesmo tempo, e o prazo caiu para dias. Hoje, ele chega com a decisão encaminhada por busca , rede e IA, e espera resposta em minutos. Na próxima década, aposto que o agente do cliente vai negociar antes mesmo do pedido. A primeira reação foi de ceticismo. Como aquilo entraria na rotina deles? Até eu mostrar o último estágio, em que o vendedor sobe uma camada e cuida do que a máquina não resolve: relacionamento e decisão. Aí as cabeças começaram a balançar, principalmente quando o assunto era a negociação com outras indústrias. A pesquisa mostra onde esse valor foi parar. Quem escolheu corretor pesou conhecimento local, experiência e confiança. A IA levanta o preço do metro quadrado; o corretor sabe se aquele preço faz sentido para aquela rua. E tem um dado que nenhuma planilha resolve: dois em cada três compradores acharam a compra estressante. Informação o cliente já tem. O que pesa é decidir. Agora coloque esse comprador diante de um vendedor treinado no roteiro de sempre: apresentação, características, alternativas. Tudo correto, e tudo o que ele já sabe. Ele precisava de alguém que questionasse as conclusões dele, apontasse o risco que ficou de fora e, quando preciso, corrigisse a IA sem queimar a relação. Vejo a mesma cena numa concessionária, no banco, na consultoria e na negociação entre indústrias. Preparar o time de vendas para usar IA melhora a produtividade interna. Preparar o time para atender quem já usa IA decide a experiência do cliente na ponta. Quanto mais a IA sobe na pré-venda, mais o vendedor precisa subir uma camada. Esse lugar existe, e a sala da siderúrgica, que começou cética, terminou reconhecendo isso. Mas só ocupa quem chega à conversa com algo que a máquina não entregou. Se o seu cliente chegasse amanhã com a resposta da IA na mão, o que o seu time acrescentaria? E me conta, no seu setor, o que o cliente já chega sabendo que, dois anos atrás, perguntava para o seu time? Alexandre van Beeck é fundador da BCK . *Este texto reproduz a opinião do autor e não reflete necessariamente o posicionamento da Mercado&Consumo. articles.title: The Day You’re Closed is the Easiest Room to Sell
articles.titleKo: The Day You’re Closed is the Easiest Room to Sell
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Not every closed day is worth the same money. Sherri Kimes asked in this column how long a menu price should live. Her examples were the Trader Joe’s banana and the Costco hot dog, prices that have lasted for decades because customers carry them around in their heads. I read her piece from the other side of the counter, and the price I kept thinking about is one almost nobody sets at all: what you charge for your restaurant on the day it is closed. Chick-fil-A is dark every Sunday. Most independents take a Monday. A lot of fast-casual dining rooms are empty by eight on a weeknight. Any of those rooms can be sold, once, to a company of thirty that needs somewhere to meet, provided somebody answers the same hour. I run eight event venues in Paris, mostly for companies. The figures below come from 4,048 dated requests that venues using my software have received since March, most of them in Paris. I doubt the behavior changes much between Paris and Columbus. What a Company Actually Buys When a company rents a closed restaurant, it is rarely buying the menu. It wants the whole place, a firm end time, and a kitchen that is cooking for nobody else that night. Nobody at the next table, and the boss can stand up and give a speech without a manager coming over at ten to ask for quiet. Which is why I would not quote a closed Monday as a table for thirty. Quote the house: one number for the room, the staff and the hours, with food on a second line. There is nothing to compare it against, because no customer has ever seen a price for your restaurant on a Monday. In Kimes’s terms this is the most forgettable price you own, and that is what makes it the easiest one to move. Not every closed day is worth the same money. In our requests, 34 percent ask for a Thursday, 21 percent for a Tuesday, and only 10 percent for a Monday, so a Tuesday is worth about twice a Monday. A Monday is not worthless, though: one Thursday request in six says, unprompted, that the date can move. When your Thursday is already taken, that is the moment to offer the day you are closed. The Reply That Goes Out Within the Hour Only 6 percent of requests mention a budget, so waiting to be asked for a price means waiting for almost everyone. The first reply should carry a price, a decision date, and a reason to visit. The price is the easy part on a closed day. There is no service to protect and no regular to displace. The room is simply free, so the number can be decided once and quoted every time. The date is the one most people forget. Of the requests we lost where a reason was recorded, nearly one in four just went silent, and only 17 percent died on budget. Ask the planner when they decide. Then you know when you may call back, and they know when the room goes back on the market. The reason to visit is whatever you leave out. Somebody has to see the room anyway, so keep the layout and the menu for that. An email that answers every question also removes every reason to drop by, and the groups that never drop by are the ones that go quiet on us. Speed matters more than polish here. Just over a third of the quotes that got signed came back within 24 hours of the request. The off-site sits on somebody’s desk for a day or two, and then it is booked somewhere else. What a Closed Day Does to the Week None of this works until the closed day has a price and a team. The price takes an afternoon. The team is harder, because the day you are closed is also the day your people rest, and if you quietly take it from them you will lose more than one event brings in. So I would not try to sell every Monday. Decide in advance how many events a month the house can carry, who volunteers for them, and which day off they get in exchange, and write that down next to the price. Then a request that lands at four on a Friday afternoon is no longer a debate about principles.

articles.title: Stop Letting That Problem Employee Cost Your Restaurant
articles.titleKo: Stop Letting That Problem Employee Cost Your Restaurant
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . You can't tell managers they own the result and then take away their authority the moment it gets uncomfortable. Every restaurant I’ve ever worked with has a Mike. He’s the employee who has been warned about showing up late. He’s been told to follow the recipe. Mike and his manager have had the same conversation so many times they could both recite it from memory. Yet Mike continues to be on the schedule because the owner can’t figure out who else would work sauté on Friday night. How can you avoid the Mikes? Stop comparing the employee to an empty shift When restaurant owners decide whether to keep a problem employee, they compare that person to having nobody at all. That’s the wrong comparison. The real question is: What is this person costing my entire team? That cost never shows up on your P&L. There’s no line item for your best cook getting fed up or your manager losing credibility because everyone knows Mike gets away with things nobody else does. But those costs are real, and they compound. When one person shows up late with no consequence, everyone else starts wondering why they bother being on time. When one person ignores the recipe, the cook who follows it starts to feel like a sucker. Culture isn’t what you put on the wall. Culture is what you allow. Run every problem through “know, can, choose” In some cases, you don’t have the wrong employees. Instead, you have an employee who doesn’t know what’s expected of them. The best way to determine if an employee is the wrong person, ask three questions. Do they know the standard? If you haven’t made the expectation clear, trained it and shown them what “good” looks like, that’s not an employee failure. It’s a leadership failure. Teach them. Can they meet the standard? Some people know exactly what’s expected but can’t perform at that level yet. That calls for more training, more practice or more time. Sometimes it means a different role. A great server may never be a great manager, and a great line cook may not belong in the sous chef job. Do they choose to meet the standard? If they know the closing checklist, can complete it and decide not to, you don’t have a training problem. You have a choice, and choices require accountability. Know when coaching turns into tolerating I’m not telling you to fire someone for their first mistake. Everyone screws up, and people deserve feedback and coaching. But coaching isn’t having the same conversation 14 times. Every time you repeat it with no change and no consequence, you teach that employee your words don’t mean anything and the only consequence is another conversation. At that point, you’re not coaching. You’re tolerating. Back up your managers If you tell your managers to hold the team accountable and then step in with “We really need them this weekend,” you’ve just taught your managers not to manage. Do that a few times, and six months from now you’ll wonder why nobody on your management team confronts anyone. You can’t tell managers they own the result and then take away their authority the moment it gets uncomfortable. That’s pretend delegation. Accept the short-term pain Being short-staffed is not a strategy, and it’s not fun. You may have to cut hours, close a section or work a shift yourself. But temporary pain is very different from permanent dysfunction. Usually, you’ll find when the wrong person finally goes, the team gets lighter and shifts get calmer. Productivity can actually go up with fewer people, because one toxic or unreliable employee can create more work than they accomplish. Put your Mike through the test You already know who your Mike is. Run that person through “know, can, choose” today. If they don’t know, fix the clarity. If they can’t, decide whether more training or a different role makes sense. If they know, they can and they keep choosing not to, stop pretending you have a traini

San Diego-based Rise & Shine Hospitality Group will officially open its second Breakfast Republic in Coachella Valley, Calif., on Tuesday, November 24, in downtown Palm Springs, joining the Palm Desert location that opened in 2023. Rise & Shine Founder and CEO Johan Engman made the announcement. The new restaurant at 333 South Palm Canyon Drive takes over the space most recently occupied by Impala Bar & Grill. The 3,500-square-foot Breakfast Republic will have a capacity of about 150, including bar seating and patio dining. A fundraising soft opening will be held on Sunday, November 22, from 9:00 a.m. – 1:30 p.m. that is also open to the public. One hundred percent of sales from the day will benefit The LGBTQ Community Center of The Desert. Spots are limited, and interested guests must email Rocky Martinez at rocky.martinez@riseandshinerg.com to request a time slot. The Breakfast Republic menu features comforting breakfast and brunch favorites, including Chilaquiles, Steak ‘n’ Eggs, Breakfast Jambalaya, Bae Mac (mac ‘n cheese), The Cluck Burger, California Breakfast Burrito, and a variety of omelets, scrambles, and benedicts. All eggs are sourced from Vital Farms, whose hens are pasture-raised with at least 108 square feet of space. The sweet side of the menu offers pancakes with varying flavors like Oreo, churro, cinnamon roll, strawberry cheesecake, and blueberry crumble. French toast options include s’mores, banana split, and strawberry & mascarpone. The Rooster Flight for Two allows guests to choose any combination of three pancake and French toast flavors. Gluten-free pancakes and vegan options – such as the Veggie Frittata, Harvest Omelet, Vegan Breakfast Burrito, and Tres Leches Pancakes– are also available. The drink menu has Bloody Maries, bubbles, and breakfast cocktails, including the Morning Mule, Sparkling Strawberry Screwdriver, and Morning Buzz (a take on the classic martini). “Downtown Palm Springs has always been – and always will be – one of the most vibrant and fun areas in all of Southern California,” Engman said. “It truly is a special place, and we are honored that we can bring our ‘cluckin’ good time’ concept to bring even more fun.” Regular hours of operation for Breakfast Republic Palm Springs are 7:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m., seven days a week. The restaurant will be open on Thanksgiving Day with normal hours. In addition to street parking, there is a parking lot behind Breakfast Republic, and it can be accessed from the restaurant’s cross street of West Baristo Road. Palm Springs marks Rise & Shine’s 12th Breakfast Republic location overall in Southern California, including five in San Diego, three in Los Angeles, and two in Orange County. Two more Breakfast Republic restaurants will open in Southern California in early 2027 – Highland Park (Los Angeles) and Huntington Beach. Rise & Shine also owns three Breakfast Company restaurants, including two in San Diego (Gaslamp Breakfast Company and Mission Valley Breakfast Company) and one in the Los Angeles area (West Hollywood Breakfast Company). A fourth – Greenville Breakfast Company – will open in Dallas in December, marking the group’s first concept outside of Southern California. articles.originalSummary: Caviar House & Prunier’s Piccadilly flagship introduces new dishes, whilst keeping the firm favourites that have made the restaurant a destination in its own right. The additions bring fresh personality to the offering, from an elevated take on a British classic to a highly indulgent seafood club sandwich. The New Additions The Royal Fish Fillet (£75) takes the humble fish finger sandwich somewhere unexpected. Battered hake served in a brioche bun with melted American cheese and the chef’s homemade tartar sauce, finished with a generous portion of caviar. It’s elevated comfort without losing what made it comforting in the first place. Caviar Spaghetti (£44) keeps things simple with an exquisite white wine sauce gently folded with fresh Prunier caviar and al dente spaghetti. A staple at Prunier’s original Paris restaurant, this dish is a match made in heaven that will please and delight every palate. Watch the dish being made here instagram.com/p/DXPRxz7MlSu . The Lobster & Caviar Club Sandwich (£45) is the dish everyone covets. Half a lobster, boiled egg, tomato, mixed leaves and Emmental, brought together with the chef’s signature Caviar Marie Rose sauce between thick wholemeal bread, served with fries. A showstopper set to become a firm favourite. King Crab & Caviar (£115) rounds out the new arrivals with restraint. Succulent King Crab paired with 10g of Prunier caviar and a green leaf salad, letting two exceptional ingredients speak for themselves. The Favourites Staying Put Some dishes have earned their permanent place. The Caviar Baked Potato (£75), for example, with 30g of Prunier caviar atop an indulgently twice-baked potato, remains one of the restaurant’s most requested dishes. It’s a nod to Jackie Kennedy’s own love of caviar and jacket potato, scaled up for extra indulgence. Caviar & Crisps (£50) continues to hold its title as London’s most talked-about bar snack, presented with 30g of Prunier caviar served simply with lightly salted, hand-cooked potato crisps and a side of crème fraîche. Designed to be shared alongside a glass of perfectly chilled fizz. The all-day brunch menu also remains a firm fixture, with eggs served every way alongside smoked salmon and caviar. Scrambled Eggs & Caviar (£18), Eggs Royale (£20), and The Royal Trio (£22), scrambled eggs with both smoked salmon and caviar, all continue to draw regulars back for breakfast, lunch, or anything in between. For something more elaborate, the Tsarina (£44) brings 10g of Prunier caviar and Balik smoked salmon together on a savoury pancake with crème fraîche. Each new dish follows the same principle that runs through the entire menu: exceptional ingredients, given the attention they deserve, without unnecessary complication. The full menu, including all new additions, is available now at Caviar House & Prunier, 161 Piccadilly, London. Reservations recommended. For reservations or further information, please see www.caviarhouse-prunier.co.uk

articles.originalSummary: Pardeh , a new contemporary Persian restaurant founded by former theatre set designer, Sahar Gilabadi, officially opened on November 18 , in East London’s Bethnal Green. Located within Empress Works on The Oval, the restaurant brings a fresh perspective to Persian dining, combining traditional Iranian recipes and ingredients with international techniques and influences. With a menu designed for sharing, a considered wine programme and distinctive interiors that bring together industrial architecture and traditional Persian antiques, Pardeh offers a contemporary interpretation of the warmth and generosity of Iranian hospitality. Taking its name from the Farsi word for curtain , Pardeh draws inspiration from the traditions of Persian home cooking and the conviviality of gathering around the table. The restaurant’s kitchen, launch menu and wine list were developed in consultation with Iranian-born chef Yma Apa, formerly of The Drunken Butler and Tehran-Berlin, whose experience cooking across Europe has informed a distinctive approach to Persian cuisine. Rooted in traditional flavours and ingredients, the menu incorporates classical French techniques alongside influences from wider Asian cooking, bringing together familiar dishes and more unexpected interpretations. At the heart of Pardeh’s menu is a selection of signature dishes celebrating the rich culinary heritage of Iran through contemporary interpretations. Designed to be enjoyed across the table, the menu balances the comforting familiarity of traditional Persian cooking with a contemporary, international sensibility. Menu highlights include Green Mango Shirazi , a vibrant reinterpretation of the traditional Persian chopped salad; Saffron Chicken , celebrating one of Iran’s most prized ingredients; and Ghorme Sabzi , a green lamb stew with tahdig, bringing together slow-cooked lamb, fragrant herbs and the distinctive crisp golden rice synonymous with Persian cooking. Alongside these signatures, a regularly changing selection of specials will showcase locally sourced meats, fish and seafood, from leading suppliers such as Fin & Flounder, guided by the availability and quality of ingredients. Complementing the food is a carefully curated wine list, bringing together established European producers, emerging winemakers and lesser-known discoveries. Developed with a focus on independent growers and wines of character, the selection spans accessible everyday bottles through to rarer expressions, with rotating additions to reflect the changing menu and seasons. The cocktail programme takes a similarly international approach, combining classic serves with inventive interpretations incorporating Persian ingredients and flavours. The signature cocktails all nod to Persian flavours, including the arak based Tehran 75, alongside a saffron Martini, and tamarind Margherita Conceived as a welcoming neighbourhood destination, Pardeh offers several distinct spaces designed to accommodate different dining occasions. The main restaurant, seating 50, features two central communal tables for up to 14 guests each alongside more intimate tables for two to four. For private gatherings, a curtain-enclosed dining area accommodates up to 12 guests, available for exclusive bookings with a minimum spend of £750, irrespective of party size. At the entrance to the restaurant, Gilas Wine Bar offers a more informal setting for drinks and small plates. Conceived as a lively standing wine and snack bar, Gilas welcomes guests for a spontaneous glass of wine, a selection of seasonal snacks or an aperitif before dinner, creating an accessible neighbourhood destination in its own right. Towards the rear of the restaurant, a dedicated bar and listening space brings another dimension to Pardeh’s atmosphere.
