articles.title: ‘DOU’ Extra traz decreto de regulamentação do fim da 6×1, com cálculo da hora de trabalho
articles.titleKo: ‘DOU’ Extra traz decreto de regulamentação do fim da 6×1, com cálculo da hora de trabalho
articles.originalSummary: O governo do presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), publicou nesta quinta-feira, 19, em edição extra do Diário Oficial da União ( DOU ) , o decreto que regulamenta o fim da escala de trabalho 6×1. As disposições são aplicadas aos empregados urbanos, aos empregados rurais, aos empregados domésticos e, no que couber, aos trabalhadores avulsos. O texto traz o cálculo da hora de trabalho e também especificações para os empregados que trabalham em turnos ininterruptos e em jornadas de 12 horas. O decreto foi assinado na manhã desta quinta-feira pelo presidente reeleito, em cerimônia realizada no Palácio do Planalto. Estiveram presentes o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin; os ministros do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho, e da Secretaria Geral, Guilherme Boulos; o presidente do Tribunal Superior do Trabalho (TST), Luiz Philippe Vieira de Mello Filho; e representantes sindicais. Também estiveram presentes vários congressistas, entre eles o deputado Reginaldo Lopes (PT-MG), autor da PEC que acabou sendo votada, o deputado André Janones (Rede-MG), e o líder do governo na Câmara, Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS). O vereador e deputado federal eleito Rick Azevedo (Psol-RJ), que começou o atual movimento de pressão pelo fim da escala 6×1 por meio do Movimento Vida Além do Trabalho (VAT), também participou do evento. A principal ausência foi da deputada Érika Hilton (Psol-SP), autora de uma das propostas de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que levaram à redução da jornada de trabalho. Segundo o decreto, para os empregados sujeitos à duração normal do trabalho, o salário-hora será calculado com base no divisor 210, para jornadas máximas de 42 horas semanais, e no divisor 200, para jornadas de até 40 horas semanais. O divisor é um parâmetro usado para calcular o valor da hora de trabalho a partir do salário mensal. O cálculo normal estabelece a multiplicação do total de horas trabalhadas por cinco (por isso as 42 horas semanais têm divisor de 210 e as 40 horas, de 200). Em discurso na cerimônia de assinatura do decreto, o ministro do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho, explicou que hoje, na jornada de 44 horas, é normalmente utilizado o divisor 220. “Isso significa que um trabalhador que recebe hoje R$ 3.000,00 continuará recebendo os mesmos R$ 3.000,00, mas o valor de referência de sua hora passará agora, em 16 de dezembro, de R$ 13,64 para R$ 14,29. Em dezembro de 2027, a hora passará para R$ 15,00”, exemplificou. “É uma mudança importante para o cálculo das horas extras e de outros direitos trabalhistas.” E afirmou: “Os empresários falam, poxa, mas vai impactar. É só não convocar hora extra, é só substituir por contratações que não terá nenhum impacto.” Esse cálculo, porém, não impede a aplicação de um divisor menor, desde que previsto em lei, convenção ou acordo coletivo de trabalho, ou decorrente de jornada contratual inferior à duração normal semanal. Segundo o decreto, deve prevalecer, “em qualquer hipótese”, o divisor mais favorável ao empregado. O decreto ainda determina que os empregados que trabalham em turnos ininterruptos de revezamento terão assegurada jornada de seis horas diárias, exceto se houver disposição diversa estabelecida em convenção ou acordo coletivo de trabalho. Deverá ser observado, no mês-calendário, a média de duração do trabalho correspondente ao limite semanal constitucional e o repouso semanal remunerado de dois dias. Por sua vez, os empregados que trabalham em jornadas de 12 horas consecutivas de trabalho por 36 horas ininterruptas de descanso terão a compensação das horas trabalhadas ou o pagamento de horas extras quando a jornada resultar, no mês-calendário, em média superior ao limite semanal constitucional, nos termos estabelecidos em convenção ou acordo coletivo de trabalho. A emenda à Constituição que acaba com a escala 6×1 foi promulgada em 16 de outubro pelo Congresso. articles.title: When Franchise Technology Becomes a Legal Liability
articles.titleKo: When Franchise Technology Becomes a Legal Liability
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A brand standard tells a franchisee what result the system expects: a clean store, a consistent product, a safe delivery. How to get there stays with the franchisee. A franchisee asks for help: a competitor down the road just adopted software that clocks workers in, prompts upsells, and reports every sale. The franchisor responds by rolling out its own version to every location. Years later, that software is the centerpiece of a lawsuit against the franchisee and the franchisor. In that case and ones like it, plaintiffs may call their theory joint employment, vicarious liability, or agency, but each asks the same question: did the franchisor stay within the minimum standards that protect its brand, or did its control reach the franchisee’s day-to-day operations? The answer often depends on the kind of control at issue, as a review of more than 600 franchise decisions issued since 2020, from motions to dismiss through trial, shows. When courts relied on allegations that a franchisor’s control went beyond enforcing brand standards, and those allegations did not involve technology, they treated those facts as evidence of impermissible control roughly a third of the time. When the allegations involved the franchisor’s technology platform—an allegation that has been observed to occur 3 times more often since 2020—that figure rose to more than half. Why Technology Is Different A brand standard tells a franchisee what result the system expects: a clean store, a consistent product, a safe delivery. How to get there stays with the franchisee. Software may implicitly take that choice away. It may clock in the crew, script the upsell, and keep a timestamped record of each step. In other words, it may perform the daily work that standards are supposed to leave to the operator and create evidence that it did. Massage Heights Franchising v. Hagman shows how far brand standards can go. There, the franchisor required franchisees to run background checks on massage therapists, controlled the draping method therapists used, specified their training, detailed how they should interact with clients, and set protocols for responding to sexual assault allegations. After a franchisee’s therapist allegedly assaulted a customer, a jury found the franchisor negligent. In 2025, the Texas Supreme Court reversed, finding that the franchisor’s alleged control was not enough for it to be held liable. Ronquillo v. Doctor’s Associates shows the opposite. A worker at a Subway franchise sued the Subway franchisor under Illinois’s biometric privacy law. She alleged that Subway’s point-of-sale software, which the franchisor “exclusively controls,” captured workers’ fingerprints when they clocked in. In 2022, a federal court in Chicago refused to let the franchisor put the collection solely on its franchisee, and the claim went forward. The difference between the two cases is not how much control the franchisor had. In Massage Heights , the franchisor set rules and left the work to the franchisee. In Ronquillo , the franchisor’s software did the work itself. Using Technology The Safest Way Courts have yet to decide whether a franchisor’s AI tool can make it liable for a franchisee’s workforce, and some assume that question will require a new analysis. It should not. The numerous decisions where franchisor technology was at issue provide plenty of guidance for how this analysis should proceed and what franchise systems can do to protect themselves: 1. Provide Technology to Aid, Not Dictate, Operations. A court held that requiring franchisees to use one brand of point-of-sale system did not make them a national coffee chain’s agents, because that control did not reach the system’s “functionality or operation.” Similarly, a pizza franchisor required drivers to use its delivery app, but a court held that a tool that “mechanically aids deliveries” is

articles.titleKo: The Salty Enters CPG Space with Bottled Clean-Label Syrups
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Salty, a national modern donut and coffee brand with more than 20 location across the U.S. known for its premium 24-hour brioche donuts and meticulously sourced coffee program, has entered the CPG space with the launch of its new bottled, clean-label syrups. Designed to bring The Salty coffee shop experience home, the inaugural collection features three signature syrups to infuse premium flavor to homemade lattes, cold brew, matcha and more. The Salty’s core collection includes: Salted Vanilla : Sweet, creamy vanilla with a subtle hint of salt for a smooth, balanced flavor that goes with just about anything Cinnamon Cereal: Warm, toasted cereal milk flavor with cinnamon spice and creamy sweetness for a nostalgic twist on your everyday coffee or matcha Maple & Brown Sugar : Deep, caramelized brown sugar blended with real maple syrup for a rich, cozy sweetness “From the beginning, we’ve believed that great flavor starts with great ingredients, and our house-made syrups are a natural extension of that philosophy,” said Amanda Pizarro, The Salty’s Founder and Chief Brand Officer. “Our customers have always looked for ways to recreate their favorite drinks at home, and we’ve made that possible without compromising on the quality, creativity or attention to detail that defines The Salty. These syrups will allow us to reach guests well beyond our shops and we hope to see The Salty become a part of more people’s daily coffee ritual.” True to The Salty’s brand ethos, the syrups are crafted with clean ingredients and without the use of artificial flavors, dyes or preservatives. Each eight-ounce recyclable glass bottle has approximately 10 servings and a shelf life of two-years unopened or six-months open and refrigerated. Flavors can be purchased individually ($16) or in a three-pack ($45) and are available at all Salty locations or online at saltydonut.com with nationwide shipping. In addition to its signature offerings, The Salty plans to release limited-edition seasonal flavors. Its fall collection includes Brown Sugar Pumpkin (real pumpkin, rich brown sugar and warm fall spices for a cozy sip) and Salted Hazelnut (rich, nutty hazelnut with a subtle hint of salt for smooth balanced sweetness). Deputing Nov. 27, the holiday collection will feature Apple Pie and Honey & Cardamom Bun. Founded by Amanda Pizarro and her then-boyfriend, now-husband Andy Rodriguez as a Miami pop-up in 2015, The Salty has since grown to more than 20 brick-and-mortar locations across eight states. The brand’s entrance into the CPG category comes on the heels of its rapid retail growth, opening eight of its locations since January 2025 and unveiling a new savory food menu at select stores. Deeply rooted in community and guest experience, The Salty has hosted high-profile brand collaborations including Poppi, Snif, Summer Fridays, Salt & Straw and MINI to bring immersive guest activations to its locations nationwide. For more information about The Salty, visit saltydonut.com. The post The Salty Enters CPG Space with Bottled Clean-Label Syrups appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Produtividade: estamos medindo e direcionando esforços corretamente?
articles.titleKo: Produtividade: estamos medindo e direcionando esforços corretamente?
articles.originalSummary: Produtividade é, diversas vezes, associada à quantidade de tarefas realizadas, ao volume de trabalho executado ou, simplesmente, ao número de horas que cada profissional permanece na empresa. Mas será que estar ocupado significa, necessariamente, ser produtivo? Essa é uma pergunta que empresários e lideranças precisam começar a fazer com mais frequência. Especialmente em um momento em que as margens estão pressionadas, os custos operacionais exigem atenção redobrada e o consumidor pensa cada vez mais antes de abrir a carteira. Segundo o IBGE, as vendas do comércio varejista brasileiro cresceram apenas 0,2% em setembro de 2026, na comparação com agosto. Já a Confederação Nacional do Comércio (CNC) apontou que 81,6% das famílias brasileiras estavam endividadas em outubro. Embora endividamento não signifique necessariamente inadimplência, o dado reforça a necessidade de compreender as limitações e prioridades do orçamento do consumidor. Nesse contexto, crescer não depende apenas de atrair mais clientes. Depende também de aproveitar melhor as oportunidades que já existem. Recentemente, ao discutir a transição da escala 6×1 para a 5×2, provoquei os empresários a repensar a distribuição de suas equipes antes de assumir novas contratações como única alternativa. Fernando Cardoso, sócio-diretor da Gouvêa Foodservice, deu continuidade à reflexão ao explorar as particularidades das operações de alimentação , demonstrando que o redesenho do trabalho envolve também processos, abastecimento, tecnologia e desenvolvimento de competências. Mas gostaria de avançar um pouco mais nessa conversa: o que estamos, de fato, considerando produtividade dentro das nossas empresas? Equipes ocupadas nem sempre são equipes produtivas Imagine uma loja de moda em que os vendedores passam boa parte do expediente organizando araras, conferindo etiquetas, movimentando mercadorias e realizando atividades administrativas. Todos parecem ocupados. Quantas oportunidades de atendimento e venda estão sendo perdidas enquanto essas tarefas são executadas? Em uma farmácia, os colaboradores podem dedicar tempo excessivo a processos manuais, conferências e atividades operacionais, enquanto clientes aguardam atendimento ou deixam de receber orientações e sugestões relevantes. Em um restaurante, a equipe pode trabalhar intensamente durante todo o expediente, mas enfrentar atrasos, retrabalho, desperdícios e dificuldades de comunicação entre cozinha e salão. Perceba que, nos três exemplos, não estamos necessariamente falando de falta de esforço ou comprometimento das pessoas, mas da forma como o trabalho foi organizado. Uma operação pode ter profissionais extremamente dedicados e, ainda assim, apresentar baixa produtividade. E esse é um dos principais equívocos da gestão: confundir intensidade de trabalho com geração de resultados. Estamos medindo o esforço ou o resultado? O varejo evoluiu muito no acompanhamento de indicadores: faturamento, ticket médio, conversão, itens por atendimento, margem e metas individuais fazem parte da rotina de inúmeras empresas. Mas quantas delas conseguem relacionar esses resultados à quantidade de horas efetivamente trabalhadas? A receita gerada por hora trabalhada, por exemplo, ajuda a compreender quanto a operação consegue produzir comercialmente com o tempo disponível. Vamos imaginar duas lojas com características semelhantes, ambas faturando R$ 300 mil mensais: A primeira utiliza 1.500 horas de trabalho no período. A segunda,1.200 horas. A primeira gera R$ 200 por hora trabalhada. A segunda, R$ 250. Ou seja, a segunda apresenta produtividade comercial por hora 25% superior. Mas atenção: Isso não significa, automaticamente, que seja mais rentável. Se a segunda loja trabalha com descontos excessivos, apresenta perdas elevadas ou compromete a experiência dos clientes, parte dessa aparente vantagem pode desaparecer. Por isso, não basta analisar apenas a receita por hora. É preciso relacioná-la também à margem, às despesas operacionais, à qualid

articles.title: Port of Subs Hits Major Franchise Milestone, Expands to Cuba
articles.titleKo: Port of Subs Hits Major Franchise Milestone, Expands to Cuba
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Port of Subs, the neighborhood sandwich franchise known for its fresh, made-to-order subs, closed out a milestone third quarter of franchise development, completing its founding “Twenty Club” of Regional Developers and signing four new Regional Developers in total. The brand also expanded to Cuba with a new location at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, earned a spot at No. 384 on the 2026 Franchise Times Top 400 , and has opened 11 new locations year-to-date, building momentum as it heads into the final quarter of the year. The Q3 results reflect Port of Subs’ deliberate growth strategy: partnering with experienced, entrepreneurial Regional Developers who serve as local extensions of the brand, leading franchise sales and providing long-term support to operators in their markets. Backed by more than 54 years in business and franchise growth engine Area 15 Ventures, the brand continues to expand across both traditional and non-traditional venues nationwide. Port of Subs Completes Its Founding “Twenty Club” In Q3, Port of Subs reached a key benchmark: completing the elite “Twenty Club” consisting of the founding 20 Regional Developers who will set the stage for the brand’s national expansion. The brand’s Regional Developer momentum didn’t stop there. Port of Subs went on to multiple additional Regional Developers during the quarter, extending its reach into new markets across the country: Regional Developer No. 22: Mitul Chothani and Hitesh Barvaliya will lead development of 10 locations across Fort Myers. Chothani and Barvaliya are successful multi-unit franchisees of several QSR brands across Florida. Regional Developer No. 23: Richard Wenschlag and Ed Kofol will lead development of nine locations across Boise. Wenschlag and Kofol are multi-unit owners and developers of a frozen yogurt brand. Each Regional Developer will lead franchise sales and support in their respective markets, identifying strong local operators and building out the brand’s neighborhood presence. Port of Subs provides Regional Developers and franchisees with real estate, operations, marketing, training and technology resources, along with a simplified operating model that requires no cooking or grills. From Guantanamo Bay to Sea-Tac: A Non-Traditional Push On the development front, Port of Subs has opened 11 new locations year-to-date through Q3, bringing its footprint to more than 129 locations across the U.S. The brand forged ahead with its push into more non-traditional venues throughout Q3, highlighted by the opening of a location at Naval Station Guantanamo Bay in Cuba, in partnership with the U.S. Navy. Located at the Navy’s oldest overseas base, the new store brings Port of Subs’ made-to-order subs to service members, their families and civilian personnel stationed on the island. The brand also opened a store at Naval Air Station Oceana, also in partnership with the Navy, as well as a location at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. “This quarter showed what’s possible when you pair a proven, simple model with the right local leaders,” said Healey Mendicino, President & CEO of Port of Subs. “Completing our Twenty Club was a milestone we’ve been building toward, and signing three more Regional Developers right behind it tells us the momentum is real. We’re entering the fourth quarter in a strong position to keep bringing Port of Subs to more neighborhoods across the country.” To learn more about franchising opportunities with Port of Subs, please visit www.franchising.portofsubs.com. Penn Station Sandwiches, the fast-casual sandwich franchise beloved for its grilled-to-order subs, fresh-cut fries, and hand-squeezed lemonade, is excited to announce expansion of the brand in Troy, Michigan. The newly signed development agreement was inked by mother-son team Brendan and Colleen Gumbel, marking the beginning of their family’s venture into franchise ownership with the brand. A Michigan native and 2022 graduate of Michigan State University, Brendan brings a background in supply chain management, purchasing and project management to the new business venture. His interest in Penn Station began with a personal connection to the brand: a cousin who owns two Penn Station restaurants in Michigan. After learning more about the franchise opportunity through his cousin and connecting with Penn Station’s development team, Brendan and Colleen began exploring what ownership could look like. Their conversations eventually led to a signed single-unit development agreement for Troy. “Having grown up with Penn Station just down the road, I’ve always loved the food and been familiar with the brand,” said Brendan Gumbel. “What really stood out to us was the people and the support behind the franchise. After meeting the corporate team and learning more about the business, we felt very comfortable moving forward. We’re excited about the opportunity to build something of our own with Penn Station.” Colleen, who lives in nearby Rochester Hills, is partnering with Brendan on the investment. The family plans to bring the brand to Troy, a market they believe offers strong potential given its mix of businesses, schools, retail destinations and established dining options. “We’re excited to welcome Brendan and Colleen to the Penn Station family as we continue to grow our franchise network in Michigan,” said Don Champion, vice president of sales and franchise development for Penn Station Sandwiches. “Our refreshed brand identity and expanded menu reflect the continued evolution of the brand and the opportunities ahead for new franchise owners. We look forward to supporting the Gumbels as they bring Penn Station’s signature sandwiches to Troy.” The Troy restaurant is currently targeted to open in 2027, with the specific site and construction timeline still being finalized. Founded more than 40 years ago, Penn Station Sandwiches has grown to more than 300 restaurants nationwide while maintaining a focus on quality ingredients, made-to-order food and operational excellence. The brand’s recent rebrand bringing an expanded menu for more occasions is part of a strategy that prioritizes sustainable growth, franchisee profitability, and market development opportunities for qualified operators like the Gumbels. Now, for the first time, he’s putting his name on a food product: meet the Keith Lee Pork Belly Fried Rice Dumpling , created in collaboration with Brooklyn Dumpling Shop . This week, Brooklyn Dumpling Shop launched its newest creation in partnership with creator, food critic, and Brooklyn Dumpling brand investor Keith Lee: the Keith Lee Pork Belly Fried Rice Dumpling. It’s smoky-sweet char siu pork belly and fried rice folded into a dumpling and available now across Brooklyn Dumpling Shop locations in New York, New Jersey, Philadelphia, Miami, and Dallas, including at the brand’s latest opening in DeKalb Market Hall in Brooklyn, New York. The launch marks Lee’s first-ever food product, featuring a flavor he developed with Brooklyn Dumpling Shop and his chef, Alexia Grant . The new dumpling was chosen by Lee’s fans following his taste test at Brooklyn Dumpling Shop’s Dallas, TX location, where he sampled four specially requested dumpling flavors and invited his audience to vote for their favorite . Famous for candid restaurant reviews and inspiring audiences to explore new dining experiences, Lee knew he wanted to create a dumpling that not only tasted delicious, but also brought the distinctiveness of the Brooklyn Dumpling Shop brand by putting a reimagined twist on a familiar dish. “We’re built on ‘Everything’s Better in a Dumpling™,’ and we nailed the beloved flavor of pork fried rice in our delicious way,” said Jeff Galletly, Chairman and CEO of Brooklyn Dumpling Shop. “It was a dream to co-create this product alongside Keith and his team. We’re all about highly craveable fusion flavors, and we’re proud to launch Keith’s first-ever food item as a memorable moment for our fans, shop team members, and our franchisees.” “Making this dumpling with Brooklyn Dumpling Shop has meant a lot to me. I wanted to ensure it’d be something I’d be proud to share with my community, and the team really got it just right,” said Keith Lee, creator and Brooklyn Dumpling Shop investor. “Bringing this vision to life has been an unforgettable experience and we knew our fans had to be involved in choosing the final dumpling, because y’all are the reason I get to do any of this. I’m so grateful and I really hope everyone enjoys it as much as we enjoyed making it for you.” The dumpling is available on the “ Keith Lee’s Faves ” menu in every U.S. Brooklyn Dumpling Shop location, including the latest opening at DeKalb Market Hall in Brooklyn, and through TikTok Go. articles.title: Burger King Brings Snoopy and the Peanuts Gang to its Menu
articles.titleKo: Burger King Brings Snoopy and the Peanuts Gang to its Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The centerpiece is the Peanuts Pack, an adult meal served in a collectible Snoopy Doghouse Box. Snoopy and the Peanuts gang are heading to Burger King this holiday season, bringing new menu items, collectible merchandise, and a dose of nostalgia to the fast-food chain. Beginning December 1, participating U.S. restaurants will introduce a limited-time Peanuts menu featuring new food items, holiday beanies, collectible toys, and packaging inspired by Snoopy’s iconic red doghouse. The collaboration is Burger King’s latest effort to create experiences that appeal to customers of all ages. The centerpiece is the Peanuts Pack, an adult meal served in a collectible Snoopy Doghouse Box. Customers can choose a Whopper with Cheese or 10-piece Chicken Nuggets with Woodstock Golden Ranch, a new creamy, tangy dipping sauce. The meal also includes Charlie Brown Loaded Potato Tots, filled with cheese, bacon bits, sour cream, chives, and potatoes, along with a new Snoopy Cookies & Creme Pie featuring a chocolate cookie crust, vanilla-flavored creme filling, holiday sprinkles, and chocolate cookie crumbles. A medium fountain drink and one of two collectible Snoopy beanies complete the bundle. The beanies come in brown and red versions, featuring Snoopy resting on his doghouse or wearing a Santa hat. Burger King is also introducing a Peanuts-inspired King Jr. Meal featuring a hamburger, cheeseburger, or four-piece Chicken Nuggets, along with a side and beverage. Each meal comes in a Snoopy Doghouse Box and includes one of eight collectible toys featuring characters such as Charlie Brown, Lucy, Linus, Sally, and Snoopy. One option features Snoopy’s doghouse with stickers that children can use to decorate it. The promotion follows Burger King’s entertainment partnerships involving SpongeBob SquarePants, The Mandalorian, and Dragon Ball, but this collaboration has a more deliberate holiday connection. CMO Joel Yashinsky said the chain evaluates potential partnerships through consumer research. Burger King considered approximately 10 holiday collaborations before selecting Peanuts, whose decades-long association with Christmas made it a natural fit. The company worked with the Peanuts team over the past year to develop the promotion, seeking a property that could connect with children, parents, and grandparents. “What types of partnerships will connect with everyone from five to 95? We really try to find that multi-generational interest,” Yashinsky says. The promotion also supports Burger King’s efforts to rebuild its family business after years of marketing around its King mascot, whose unconventional appearance alienated some parents. “We had a mascot that a lot of moms, in particular, found creepy,” Yashinsky says. He believes the company’s previous marketing direction contributed to a long-term decline in its family business, leaving younger generations without the same connection to Burger King that their parents had. “We lost a generation of kids and families, and so now we’re working to get them back as part of our overall elevation and telling the story because they didn’t go up with Burger King, the Gen Zs of today,” he says. Burger King has since focused on creating more welcoming experiences for families, including revisiting elements of its earlier BK Kids program and exploring ways to give children greater choice during restaurant visits. Yashinsky says the company wants its entertainment partnerships to stand out through creative execution, distinctive merchandise, and memorable food offerings, even against competitors with larger restaurant footprints. “What we’re trying to do is execute it bigger and better than anybody else so the biggest and best want to work with us, knowing that we’re maybe not the biggest in terms of number of restaurants, but we believe we’re going to do everything we do better than everybo

articles.title: Durigan prevê impacto inicial da reforma tributária sobre inflação
articles.titleKo: Durigan prevê impacto inicial da reforma tributária sobre inflação
articles.originalSummary: O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, afirmou, nesta terça-feira, 17, que a implementação da reforma tributária pode gerar pequeno impacto inicial sobre a inflação. A observação foi em resposta à preocupação manifestada por senadores com uma eventual alta do índice. Segundo o ministro, esse efeito tende a diminuir gradualmente à medida que as empresas se adaptem às novas regras tributárias e ajustem a formação de preços. “Pode haver algum pequeno impacto inflacionário, mas estamos passando por um processo em que os empresários vão aprender a precificar seus bens e serviços de acordo com a nova legislação tributária, considerando os créditos a que têm direito e os débitos pelos quais são responsáveis”, disse Durigan durante audiência na Comissão de Assuntos Econômicos (CAE) do Senado . Na avaliação do ministro, “à medida que essa precificação for sendo compreendida e ajustada ao longo dos próximos meses, teremos uma redução desse impacto inflacionário”. Ele acrescentou que o Ministério da Fazenda acompanhará o processo de perto. Tributação corporativa Durante a audiência, Durigan defendeu o avanço de uma reforma da tributação corporativa, incluindo a desoneração da folha de pagamentos. Segundo o ministro, a medida deve ser discutida diante das mudanças no mercado de trabalho e da crescente incorporação de tecnologia pelas empresas. “É importante desonerar a folha, mas sem causar um prejuízo significativo à Previdência”, afirmou. De acordo com Durigan, a discussão deve ocorrer com “total compromisso de neutralidade fiscal”, transferindo para outras bases de incidência tributária parte da carga atualmente cobrada sobre a folha de salários, como o faturamento ou o resultado das empresas. articles.title: Número de desempregados há dois anos ou mais é o menor já registrado
articles.titleKo: Número de desempregados há dois anos ou mais é o menor já registrado
articles.originalSummary: O número de desempregados que procuram emprego há pelo menos dois anos foi o menor em 14 anos no terceiro trimestre de 2026. O dado foi divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 18, pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ), na Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (Pnad) Contínua. O desemprego de longa duração atingia 971 mil pessoas entre julho e setembro deste ano, o menor contingente desde 2012, início da série histórica do IBGE. Essa foi a primeira vez que o grupo impactado pela desocupação de longo prazo somou menos de 1 milhão de pessoas. O número é resultado da redução de 17,6% do desemprego longo em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, quando havia 1,179 milhão de pessoas em busca de trabalho por mais de 24 meses. Também houve queda de 8% na comparação com o segundo trimestre de 2026, quando o desemprego longo já estava no menor patamar da série histórica, em 1,058 milhão. Mínimas históricas Os números do IBGE apontam que, no terceiro trimestre de 2026, o total de trabalhadores à procura de ocupação entre um e dois anos ficou em 590 mil, também o menor nível da série histórica. Ao se considerar o total de pessoas desempregadas há pelo menos um ano ─ isto é, somando também quem está à procura de ocupação há dois anos ou mais ─, o IBGE aponta 1,56 milhão de pessoas, também o menor número registrado desde 2012. A pesquisa mostra que o patamar mais alto de pessoas em busca de trabalho há pelo menos dois anos foi em 2021, no pico da pandemia de covid-19. Naquele ano, o contingente nessa condição se manteve acima de 3,5 milhões de pessoas, chegando a 3,810 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2021. No segundo trimestre de 2021, havia ainda 3 milhões de desempregados entre um e dois anos, e o total de desempregados há mais de um ano somava 6,74 milhões de trabalhadores. Mercado de trabalho aquecido De acordo com o analista da pesquisa, William Kratochwill, esse comportamento reflete um mercado de trabalho aquecido . “É um sinal de que o mercado está contratando cada vez mais”, diz. Ele detalha que, desde o fim da pandemia, as vagas vêm apresentando sinais de crescimento. “Se o mercado precisa da mão de obra, ele sempre pega primeiro aqueles que acha mais qualificados e, depois, vai trazendo as pessoas com tempo de busca maior para dentro da ocupação”, detalha. O levantamento do IBGE indica também que, no terceiro trimestre de 2026, havia 1,136 milhão de pessoas buscando trabalho há menos de um mês. Esse contingente teve um acréscimo de 0,8% na comparação com o mesmo trimestre de 2025 (eram 1,127 milhão). “Mostra uma maior rotação no mercado de trabalho”, sinaliza Kratochwill. Pnad Contínua A Pnad apura o comportamento no mercado de trabalho para pessoas com 14 anos ou mais e leva em conta todas as formas de ocupação, seja com ou sem carteira assinada, temporária ou por conta própria, por exemplo. Pelos critérios do instituto, só é considerada desocupada a pessoa que efetivamente procurou uma vaga 30 dias antes da pesquisa. São visitados 211 mil domicílios em todos os Estados e no Distrito Federal. O instituto já havia divulgado que o Brasil fechou o terceiro trimestre com desemprego em 5,2%, o menor para o período desde 2012. O país tinha 5,6 milhões de desempregados, patamar mínimo que perdia apenas para o último trimestre de 2025 (5,5 milhões). Do total de desocupados no trimestre até setembro, 17,2% estavam na busca por trabalho há pelo menos dois anos, enquanto 10,5% estavam na janela de um a dois anos. Cerca de metade (52,1%) estava no período de um mês a menos de um ano. Uma em cada cinco pessoas (20,2%) estava há menos de um mês nessa condição. articles.titleKo: Red Robin Wants to Turn its Comeback into Something Bigger
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Red Robin wants to focus on boosting its family and dinner business. Red Robin is finding its footing again, but the casual-dining chain sees an opportunity to turn its improving sales momentum into something more sustainable by giving customers new reasons to visit. After spending much of the past year rebuilding operations, introducing value offerings, and restructuring its finances, the burger chain is turning its attention to dinner, family dining, and menu innovation in 2027. The strategy follows a third quarter that delivered Red Robin’s strongest same-store sales performance in more than three years. Comps increased 3.9 percent, outperforming the industry by 70 basis points, according to Black Box Intelligence. Traffic declined 1.7 percent, but the company gained market share in areas where it competes with other restaurants. The company now wants to build on that success with new offerings targeting dinner and family occasions. “Going forward, you’ll see us put more focus on dinner and family occasion. This is a part of our business with room to grow and an area where our guests see a natural fit for Red Robin,” CEO David Pace said during the company’s Q3 earnings call. The chain is testing promotions and menu offerings aimed at families, with the results informing its plans for 2027. Its culinary pipeline includes potential additions across appetizers, salads, entrees, burgers, and beverages. Red Robin is also pursuing a barbell strategy that combines affordable meals with premium offerings. The company recently introduced its Prime Rib Stack Burger as a holiday special and expanded its Big Yummm platform with a $16.99 tier, giving customers opportunities to trade up. That strategy helped lift average check 5.6 percent during the third quarter, including a 3.4 percent increase from pricing and a 2.2 percent benefit from menu mix and discounts. The company also benefited from lapping the initial discounts associated with the Big Yummm launch. Despite the increase, Red Robin is exercising caution with additional pricing after previous increases affected its competitive positioning. The chain took one pricing action earlier this year and is evaluating its options for 2027. “As I look at ’27, I want to be equally cautious and try and figure out how can I get us positioned back to where I want to be within the competitive set of the industry, but still cover inflation, still make sure we’ve covered our cost structure and protected it,” Pace said. The company is also adjusting its marketing strategy under Scott Hudler, who joined as CMO in September, succeeding Russ Klein. Selling expenses increased to $9.4 million in the third quarter from $6.8 million a year earlier, driven by investments in the Big Yummm platform and personalized marketing. Pace expects spending in 2027 to be similar to or slightly below current levels, with more dollars directed toward consumer-facing advertising instead of internal marketing costs. Operational improvements are also contributing to Red Robin’s turnaround. Restaurant-level operating margin increased 90 basis points to 10.8 percent during the third quarter, including approximately 40 basis points of savings from labor efficiencies. The company is using AI to improve restaurant operations and eliminate redundant technology systems, along with supply chain initiatives aimed at reducing ingredient costs. articles.title: Com queda de 13,4%, abate de bovinos fecha 3º tri em 9,82 milhões de cabeças, diz IBGE
articles.titleKo: Com queda de 13,4%, abate de bovinos fecha 3º tri em 9,82 milhões de cabeças, diz IBGE
articles.originalSummary: Os produtores brasileiros abateram 9,82 milhões de cabeças de bovinos sob algum tipo de serviço de inspeção sanitária no terceiro trimestre de 2026, uma queda de 13,4% em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025 , segundo os primeiros resultados das Pesquisas Trimestrais do Abate de Animais, do Leite, do Couro e da Produção de Ovos de Galinha, divulgados pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ). Na comparação com o segundo trimestre de 2026, houve redução de 8,4%. O volume resultou em uma produção de 2,62 milhões de toneladas de carcaças bovinas no terceiro trimestre de 2026, queda de 12,0% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. Ante o segundo trimestre, houve redução de 5,0%. Em sentido contrário, o abate de suínos somou 16,65 milhões de cabeças no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 5,2% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. Na comparação com o segundo trimestre deste ano, houve aumento de 6,1%. O peso acumulado das carcaças de suínos foi de 1,59 milhão de toneladas, crescimento de 6,4% na comparação anual e de 5,5% em relação ao segundo trimestre de 2026. O abate de frangos totalizou 1,79 bilhão de cabeças no terceiro trimestre, aumento de 5,8% ante igual período de 2025 e de 6,0% em relação ao segundo trimestre de 2026. O peso acumulado das carcaças de frango alcançou 3,86 milhões de toneladas, alta de 7,4% na comparação anual e de 3,3% em relação ao trimestre imediatamente anterior. China impõe tarifa à carne brasileira A carne bovina brasileira pagará uma tarifa total de 67% para entrar no mercado chinês. A cobrança adicional de 55% será aplicada sobre a tarifa regular de 12%, após o Brasil esgotar a cota anual de exportações estabelecida pelo país asiático. A medida preocupa frigoríficos e pecuaristas, que já avaliam antecipar abates e embarques para aproveitar a cota de 2027. O Brasil atingiu o limite de 1,106 milhão de toneladas previsto para 2026. Para o próximo ano, a cota sobe para 1,128 milhão de toneladas, mas representantes do setor estimam que o novo limite possa ser alcançado em março ou abril de 2027. O país asiático é o principal destino da carne bovina brasileira e ganhou espaço significativo nas exportações do setor na última década. De 2016 a 2025, o Brasil enviou 8,2 milhões de toneladas de carne bovina à China, movimentando US$ 42,3 bilhões. O volume saltou de 164,9 mil toneladas, em 2016, para 1,6 milhão de toneladas, em 2025. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Paula Martini). articles.title: Black Rock Gets Flexible as Development Costs Climb
articles.titleKo: Black Rock Gets Flexible as Development Costs Climb
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Black Rock Coffee Bar expects five California openings this year and 15 to 20 in 2027. Black Rock Coffee Bar’s next wave of growth is getting more expensive. But the chain sees an opportunity in buildings other brands leave behind. Average costs for its 2026 store class are coming in around $800,000 per location, accounting for tenant improvement allowances that offset the company’s investment. That compares with an initial expectation of $700,000 to $750,000 and approximately $650,000 last year. The increase hasn’t slowed Black Rock’s opening ambitions. The company raised its full-year target to 40 stores from 38 during its third-quarter earnings call and expects to substantially increase California development next year. Instead, it’s balancing different build types to manage capital and expand the pool of sites it can pursue. “We are actually balancing the capital in California with conversions, which are really helping,” CFO Rodd Booth said. READ MORE : Black Rock Finds More Room to Grow Beyond the Morning Rush Second-generation buildings with existing drive-thrus are a particular opportunity. They allow Black Rock to preserve a feature it considers central to the brand—its lobby—without taking on the same capital requirements as other development approaches in a higher-cost market. Booth said conversions are part of the strategy across Black Rock’s markets, not just California. But their value becomes especially apparent as the company builds its presence there. Black Rock expects five California openings this year and 15 to 20 in 2027. “It allows us to prioritize the lobby, but also not go out and really see the capital grow substantially in terms of a per-unit cost in California,” Booth said. That lobby also influences which properties Black Rock can make work. Asked what makes a good conversion, CEO Mark Davis pointed to a difference between Black Rock and competitors built exclusively around drive-thru service. Having a dining room means the chain doesn’t need the same long vehicle stack as a concept without one, he said. That gives Black Rock another option when evaluating existing buildings, alongside its ability to adapt to different site configurations. As other concepts close, Davis said, the development team is moving quickly to assess the spaces they leave behind. “We’re able to make a variety of different sites work,” he said. For landlords, the appeal extends beyond filling a vacancy. Davis said Black Rock’s flexibility and speed can help get properties through permitting, construction, and into operation sooner. “When you think of yourself as a landlord, they want somebody that can come in, that can go through the permitting quickly, that can adapt and get that open and get it going,” Davis said. “And what that does for them is it allows them to charge rent faster.” Becoming publicly traded last year has also helped generate interest from property owners, Davis added. Moving quickly, however, still requires work before a lease is signed. Davis said Black Rock has improved its pre-lease follow-up to better manage conversion costs. He connected that diligence to cash-on-cash returns of 35 percent in the first year and 40 percent in the second. Conversions are one part of the development mix. Black Rock also expects a near-term shift toward more reverse build-to-suit projects, which Booth said give the company greater control over planning and delivery. The benefit there is predictability. Booth said opening cadence has improved each quarter, with reverse build-to-suit stores helping Black Rock gain more control over when locations come online. The company opened 11 stores in Q3 across California, Arizona, Colorado, and Texas, finishing the period with 211. It has opened 35 for the year, with the remaining five expected in the coming weeks. articles.title: Government confirms transition period for strengthened tipping law
articles.titleKo: Government confirms transition period for strengthened tipping law
articles.originalSummary: The government has confirmed there will be a transition period around the implementation of strengthened tipping legislation. Changes to the statutory tipping law, which include the new requirement for employers to hold formal consultations whenever a new tipping policy is introduced, are scheduled to take effect on 1 January. However, the draft revised code of practice on the fair and transparent distribution of tips, published this week, confirms that operators do not need to apply the new code until the next review of their tipping policy after 1 January 2027, which must be no later than three years from the date their current policy commenced. Peter Davies, client services partner at WMT Troncmaster Services, has welcomed the announcement of a transitional implementation period, saying it will help support operators and ensure they’re not distracted over the busy festive season.

articles.title: The Most Important Part of Modernizing a Landmark Hotel’s Menu is Learning What Not to Change
articles.titleKo: The Most Important Part of Modernizing a Landmark Hotel’s Menu is Learning What Not to Change
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Landmark hotel dining should not operate like a museum. Modernizing a dining program is often described in terms of what needs to change, whether that be new menus, new ingredients, new techniques, new presentations, or new ways of engaging today’s guest. Working as an executive chef at the landmark Biltmore Hotel has taught me that there is another, equally important question to ask: What shouldn’t we change? At a property with a century of stories embedded in its walls, dining traditions are not simply items on a menu. They become part of the hotel’s identity. Guests return not only for the cuisine, but for how an experience makes them feel – and often that feeling is tied to something they have enjoyed for years or hope to share with the next generation, which creates a different responsibility for a chef. Rather than working with a blank canvas, we are stewards of something that existed before us, while also being responsible for making it relevant to the guest sitting in front of us today. The challenge is knowing the difference between something that needs updating, and something that is timeless . Protect the Ritual, Evolve the Details The Biltmore’s Traditional Afternoon Tea is a perfect example. It’s truly a ritual and is about much more than tea and pastries. There is a certain anticipation that begins before the first cup is poured: the setting, the service, the tiers of savory and sweet offerings, the pacing and, most importantly, the invitation to slow down. At a time when so much of the modern dining experience has become faster, more casual and increasingly driven by convenience, there is something contemporary about asking guests to sit, linger and be present. That is why I believe some traditions should not be modernized simply for the sake of modernization. The menu can evolve with the seasons, ingredients can be refined, presentation can be updated, and techniques can become more sophisticated. However, the essence of the experience – the ritual, the sense of occasion, the gracious pace – deserves to remain, because we do not preserve a tradition by freezing it in time, but by understanding what makes it worth returning to. Start With Who You’re Feeding That same philosophy helps clarify where change is necessary, and Fairways, our classic golf club restaurant and bar, presents a very different opportunity. Its location connects it naturally to the golf course, but today’s leisure traveler does not define a resort dining experience only by the activity happening outside. One guest might have just finished 18 holes, while another spent the morning at the pool. A family may simply be looking for a relaxed lunch or dinner in a beautiful setting. A local guest may know the course intimately, while someone else has never picked up a club. The restaurant needs to welcome all of them. For Fairways, modernization means looking beyond the traditional definition of a golf restaurant and creating an experience that feels connected to its surroundings without being limited by them. The food should be approachable but thoughtfully prepared, the beverage program engaging, and the atmosphere inviting enough that guests want to stay awhile. The menu should also reflect how people dine while traveling today – whether casually, socially, after an activity, or simply because they have found a place they enjoy. In other words, the question isn’t, “What should we put on the menu?” The better question is, “Who are we feeding, and what do we want them to experience when they sit down?” Use Heritage as a Guide, Not a Constraint That distinction is particularly important in a landmark hotel, where heritage should inform the dining experience without becoming a constraint that keeps it from evolving. articles.title: Why 30-Day Labor Certification Option Should Matter to Restaurant Operators
articles.titleKo: Why 30-Day Labor Certification Option Should Matter to Restaurant Operators
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The immigration system is much more than a policy issue for operators today, it’s become a workforce issue that deserves a deeper look. Restaurants are acutely aware of the chronic shortage of workers that’s been plaguing numerous industries for years now. Both quick and full-service operators deal with the implications of this labor gap every single day, scrambling schedules, spiking overtime, and forcing managers onto the line. In recent years, that day-to-day pressure has gotten worse as the industry deals with higher expenses associated with labor, food supplies, and other costs, leaving even less room to absorb persistent vacancies and staffing disruptions. That means, more so than in previous years, unfilled positions like cooks, dishwashers and managers can have an outsized effect on operating hours, service levels, and profitability. Foreign-born workers already make up a critical component of the restaurant workforce, accounting for nearly one in four employees nationwide . Their role in the kitchen is even more pronounced, accounting for 44 percent of chefs and 33 percent of cooks. The immigration system is much more than a policy issue for operators today, it’s become a workforce issue that deserves a deeper look. As restaurants look for lawful, long-term solutions to the shortage of workers, delays in the employer-sponsored green card process can have serious operational consequences. One of those lawful pathways is the EB-3 visa program, which allows U.S. employers to sponsor foreign workers for permanent, full-time, year-round positions when they cannot find enough qualified and available U.S. workers to fill those jobs. For most employers using the EB-3 process, one of the first major steps is PERM, which is now taking around 10 months to complete. What PERM Actually Does PERM stands for Program Electronic Review Management and is the Department of Labor (DOL) labor-certification process used by employers pursuing permanent employment-based immigration. It is used to determine whether an employer has demonstrated that there are not sufficient able, willing, qualified and available U.S. workers for a permanent position. PERM exists to protect U.S. workers. Before a restaurant can sponsor a foreign worker for a permanent position, it must first test and prove the domestic labor market through required recruitment. The DOL must also be satisfied that employing the foreign worker will not adversely affect the wages or working conditions of similarly employed U.S. workers. In other words, PERM is not a way around local recruiting. Local recruiting is built into it. The Waiting Happens Early The biggest problem with PERM, as it stands today, is the wait time. As of October 31, 2026, DOL reported PERM applications at the analyst review stage were averaging 315 days over the 90-day period prior to the reporting date. For restaurant operators, that can include multiple hiring cycles. In that time, an eatery can lose employees, train replacements and still find itself recruiting yet again while one long-term labor certification is still being reviewed. In fact, that cycle can play out repeatedly during the wait. That matters because this staffing problem is no longer limited to one rough week here or there. It’s systemic and ongoing. While the entry-level labor pipeline shrinks, the pool of younger workers restaurants traditionally relied on is becoming less dependable. PERM would not solve turnover. It can matter, however, for operators struggling to keep permanent full-time jobs filled solely through domestic recruiting. What the Bill Would Change A bipartisan proposal in Congress, known as the PERM Backlog Reduction Act , would help to fast track the ETA-9089 form that is used for permanent labor certification. articles.title: HTeaO Announces Record-Breaking Year for October Round-Up Campaign
articles.titleKo: HTeaO Announces Record-Breaking Year for October Round-Up Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . HTeaO, the nation’s leading iced tea franchise, announced a record-breaking year for its annual October Round-Up campaign, raising $159,823.97 to benefit the Ryan Palmer Foundation Breast Cancer Initiative. Now in its sixth year, the campaign surpassed its previous fundraising record of $150,110 set in 2025, reflecting the continued generosity of HTeaO customers, franchise owners, and team members nationwide. From October 1–31, guests at all HTeaO locations nationwide were invited to round up their purchases to the nearest dollar, with 100% of donations funding the RPF Breast Cancer Initiative. The Initiative supports women at every stage, from early detection to treatment. Its programs include mobile mammograms, HOPE Kits for comfort, and cold cap therapy to help minimize hair loss. “Brewing Purpose is about more than giving back. It’s about bringing people together to make a difference in the communities we serve,” said Brittany Knollmiller, Director of Marketing of HTeaO. “Every October, we see that mission come to life as our guests, franchise partners, and team members rally behind a cause that touches so many families. This year’s record-breaking campaign is a reflection of that generosity and the impact we can make when everyone comes together, one small contribution at a time.” “When we started this partnership with HTeaO five years ago, Jen and I never imagined it would grow into what it is today. Setting a new record this year means a lot to our family and the Foundation. These funds will bring mobile mammograms to underserved communities and HOPE Kits into the hands of women going through treatment, and that’s what this is all about. To everyone who rounded up this October, and to the entire HTeaO family, thank you. We’re so grateful for your continued support of our Breast Cancer Initiatives.” The Ryan Palmer Foundation was established in 2003 by professional golfer and Amarillo native Ryan Palmer to provide opportunities for youth and support families in need. Inspired by his wife’s experience with chemotherapy, Palmer launched the Breast Cancer Initiative in 2019. Since then, the initiative has expanded access to early detection in underserved communities, and supported hundreds of breast cancer patients through the distribution of Hope Kits and Warrior Caps across the country. HTeaO celebrated the month-long campaign with pink straws at all locations in recognition of Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a visible reminder of the brand’s ongoing commitment to community impact. With more than 180 locations nationwide, HTeaO continues to demonstrate its dedication to giving back through initiatives like the annual Round-Up campaign. By uniting franchise owners, team members, and customers under its Brewing Purpose platform, HTeaO aims to create positive change one cup at a time. articles.title: Shoppings projetam alta de 3% nas vendas na temporada de descontos
articles.titleKo: Shoppings projetam alta de 3% nas vendas na temporada de descontos
articles.originalSummary: Os shopping centers brasileiros estão otimistas para a Black Friday deste ano: 79% dos empreendimentos esperam crescimento no faturamento, com projeção de alta de 3% nas vendas em comparação com a edição de 2025, segundo levantamento da Associação Brasileira de Shopping Centers ( Abrasce ). O estudo aponta ainda que 71% projetam aumento nas vendas em relação ao ano anterior. Com descontos médios previstos de 37%, que podem chegar a 70%, a data, marcada para 27 de novembro, mobiliza os empreendimentos. O fluxo de visitantes deve crescer 1,7%, com 65% dos respondentes esperando movimento superior ao registrado em 2025. Já o ticket médio estimado é de R$ 237,35, acima do registrado no ano passado. “A Black Friday tem um papel estratégico para o varejo. Nos shoppings, a combinação de ofertas com a possibilidade de comparar produtos, contar com atendimento presencial e levar a compra na hora amplia a conveniência para o consumidor”, afirma Gabriella Oliveira, diretora de Planejamento Estratégico e Operações da Abrasce. Perfumaria lidera apostas de vendas na Black Friday Os descontos previstos pelos shoppings variam de 10% a 70%, com média de 37%. Perfumaria e cosméticos lideram as categorias com maior expectativa de destaque nas vendas, citadas por 74% dos respondentes. Na sequência aparecem eletrônicos e informática (65%), vestuário (63%), calçados (60%) e eletrodomésticos e eletroportáteis (57%). A liderança de perfumaria e cosméticos reforça o avanço da categoria na Black Friday. Em 2023, o segmento ocupava a sexta posição entre as apostas dos empreendimentos, citado por 43% dos participantes. Em 2024, passou ao segundo lugar, com 69%, e assumiu a liderança em 2025, com 73%. Shoppings diversificam ações promocionais Embora a Black Friday ocorra na última sexta-feira de novembro, as campanhas dos shoppings se distribuem por diferentes períodos. Neste ano, 42% dos empreendimentos concentrarão as ações entre sexta-feira e domingo, de 27 a 29 de novembro, enquanto 29% promoverão iniciativas durante toda a semana, de 23 a 29. Outros 11% estenderão as campanhas ao longo de novembro, e a mesma parcela concentrará as ações apenas na sexta-feira. As redes sociais são o principal canal de divulgação, citadas por 80% dos participantes. Entre as iniciativas para atrair consumidores, também estão roletas de prêmios (33%) e distribuição de brindes (27%). Além disso, 35% dos shoppings preveem ações especiais para a data, como a ampliação do horário de funcionamento até as 23h, para que os consumidores tenham mais tempo para aproveitar as promoções. articles.title: Estados Unidos entram em alerta após sucessivas panes tecnológicas
articles.titleKo: Estados Unidos entram em alerta após sucessivas panes tecnológicas
articles.originalSummary: Os Estados Unidos (EUA) entraram em alerta após as sucessivas panes tecnológicas que afetaram serviços críticos do país, desde a aviação civil, passando pelo sistema bancário, até mesmo o sistema de comunicação da Agência Nacional de Segurança (NSA), o órgão responsável pela inteligência do país. Ainda na semana passada, os serviços de comunicação da Microsoft saíram do ar, o que prejudicou serviços também no Brasil. Na última sexta-feira, 13, uma pane nos sistemas de controle da Administração Federal de Aviação (FAA) levou ao cancelamento de todos os voos nos EUA. Casos de panes tecnológicas continuaram ocorrendo nos dias seguintes. Na segunda-feira (16), o banco JPMorgan Chase registrou instabilidade em seus sistemas, prejudicando o acesso dos clientes a algumas ferramentas digitais. No mesmo dia, uma pane nos sistemas da empresa de transporte aéreo United Airlines levou a uma série de atrasos nos voos. Uma “falha generalizada” no sistema teria provocado o problema. Na terça-feira, 16, foi a vez da NSA relatar que sofreu uma “degradação temporária” durante uma manutenção de rotina, o que não teria prejudicado as “capacidades essenciais” da agência de inteligência do país, segundo reportou a CNN. Na quarta-feira, 17,novas panes tecnológicas foram registradas. Os sistemas da Apple, a fabricante de celulares e outros aparelhos móveis, ficaram fora do ar por algumas horas. Outro caso foi o da corretora de investimentos Charles Schwab, que concentra ativos de clientes de US$ 13 trilhões. A Schwab ficou fora do ar por algumas horas nessa terça-feira, 17, em pleno horário de funcionamento do mercado. Tanto as empresas , quanto o governo de Donald Trump, afirmam que as panes nos sistemas informáticos foram provocados por problemas técnicos, desde a instalação de roteadores no caso da FAA, quanto a atualização de sistemas por Inteligência Artificial (IA) que teriam provocado quedas de plataformas. O diretor de Inteligência Nacional dos EUA, Jay Clayton, afirmou à imprensa que não há indícios de que as panes tenham sido provocadas por ataques cibernéticos de atores mal intencionados. “Não vemos indícios de um ataque cibernético coordenado. E também não vemos indícios de atividade patrocinada por um Estado”, disse Clayton à Fox Business. O presidente Trump minimizou os episódios, dizendo que tudo estaria “bem”. Ele culpou a administração democrata de Joe Biden por não modernizar o sistema da FAA, que teria causado a paralisação completa do setor aéreo dos EUA. O secretário de Estado Marco Rubio afastou a hipótese de ataques hackers coordenados ou interferência de Estados estrangeiros, como o Irã, ainda em guerra com os EUA. Rubio reconheceu que os acontecimentos são “perturbadores”, mas destacou que não há evidência de que tenham sido causados por ataques cibernéticos. “Não estamos sofrendo um ataque sistêmico”, disse a repórteres. O pesquisador do Núcleo de Estudos Estratégicos em Comunicação, Cognição e Computação, Reynaldo Aragon, avaliou à Agência Brasil que ainda não é possível saber se houve ataques cibernéticos em alguns casos, mas aponta que essas panes expõem certa fragilidade dos EUA. “O maior país do ocidente e do mundo em economia e tecnologia ficou quatro horas e meia com os voos todos cancelados. Ou seja, o Estado americano perdeu o controle do seu próprio espaço aéreo durante esse período. Isso é muito grave do ponto de vista histórico”, disse. Congressistas questionam Congressistas norte-americanos têm considerado as respostas das autoridades ligadas à Casa Branca como insuficientes. Mesmo aliados do presidente Donald Trump têm levantado suspeitas sobre as razões das panes e pedido mais informações. O senador republicano do Missouri, Josh Hawley, disse a jornalistas que se “tudo isso for uma coincidência, é a maior coincidência da história do mundo”. “Todas essas interrupções, talvez seja porque alguém desconectou um roteador no Arkansas, ou algo assim. Não sei, francamente, acho isso um pouco difícil de acreditar. Port

articles.title: Black Friday 2026: fatia de consumidores decididos a comprar salta para 32,3%
articles.titleKo: Black Friday 2026: fatia de consumidores decididos a comprar salta para 32,3%
articles.originalSummary: A aproximação da Black Friday 2026 acelerou as decisões de consumo no País. Uma pesquisa do Reclame Aqui aponta que a fatia de consumidores decididos a comprar na data saltou de 19% em agosto para 32,3% em novembro, um avanço de 13,3 pontos percentuais. O movimento é acompanhado pela redução da indecisão, que recuou 9,4 pontos percentuais, de 61% para 51,6%, e da rejeição ao evento. Apenas 16,1% dos entrevistados afirmaram que pretendem ficar de fora. Há também potencial de renovação do público, já que 54,2% dos consumidores dispostos a comprar ou ainda indecisos são estreantes no evento ou voltam a participar após ficarem de fora da edição de 2025. Compras se espalham por novembro A distribuição do orçamento indica que a tradicional sexta-feira de promoções perdeu exclusividade. Em vez de concentrar os gastos em um único dia, quase metade dos consumidores (48,1%) decidiu não definir um orçamento com antecedência e pretende acompanhar as ofertas ao longo de novembro. Apenas 17,4% dos entrevistados planejam concentrar a maior parte das compras na data oficial da Black Friday, enquanto os demais preferem aproveitar promoções antecipadas ou decidir no momento da compra. Orçamento limita compras na Black Friday O levantamento identificou uma mudança na percepção dos consumidores que decidiram não comprar nesta edição. A desconfiança em relação às promoções, associada à ideia de que o evento não oferece descontos reais, prática conhecida como “metade do dobro”, deixou de ser o principal motivo para não comprar. O percentual recuou de 51,6% em agosto para 15,6% em novembro. Atualmente, os principais obstáculos ao consumo são de ordem financeira: 34,9% dos que pretendem ficar de fora afirmam que o orçamento não permite gastos extras; 34,5% dizem não precisar de nenhum produto no momento. IA auxilia pesquisa O consumidor também passou a enxergar a Inteligência Artificial não apenas como novidade ou curiosidade, mas como uma ferramenta prática de apoio às compras e de controle do orçamento. Para a Black Friday, o uso da tecnologia se concentra em atividades de pesquisa e economia: 66,3% utilizam a IA para pesquisar as características dos produtos desejados; 40,2% recorrem à ferramenta para comparar preços e encontrar ofertas; 25,8% usam a tecnologia para localizar lojas que vendem os itens procurados. Reputação pesa na decisão de compra A reputação das empresas também deve influenciar as decisões de compra na Black Friday 2026. Segundo a pesquisa, 76,1% dos entrevistados afirmam que pretendem consultar o Reclame Aqui durante o evento. A preocupação vai além dos descontos oferecidos: Reputação das lojas: 69,1% pesquisam o histórico das empresas para verificar se cumprem prazos e entregam os produtos anunciados; Suporte pós-venda: 34,1% analisam o histórico de reclamações e o índice de resposta das marcas para evitar problemas com trocas, devoluções e assistência técnica; Segurança digital: 20,9% utilizam ferramentas de verificação para verificar a legitimidade das páginas antes de inserir dados de pagamento. articles.title: CCJ aprova punição a fraude financeira para evitar ‘caso Americanas’
articles.titleKo: CCJ aprova punição a fraude financeira para evitar ‘caso Americanas’
articles.originalSummary: A Comissão de Constituição e Justiça (CCJ) do Senado aprovou, nesta quarta-feira, 18, por 15 a 0, o Projeto de Lei 2.091/2023 , que cria um tipo penal para punir fraudes contábeis no mercado de capitais. Um dos objetivos é evitar casos semelhantes ao das Lojas Americanas. O texto ainda precisará passar por uma votação suplementar antes de ir para a Câmara. Durante a tramitação, o texto foi alterado pelo relator, Oriovisto Guimarães (PSDB-PR), que retirou quatro dos cinco novos crimes previstos na proposta original e manteve a tipificação da fraude contábil. Pela versão atual, cometerá crime quem fraudar a contabilidade ou fornecer documentos falsos à auditoria independente, inserindo operações inexistentes, dados inexatos ou deixando de incluir operações efetivamente realizadas. A pena prevista é de reclusão de dois a seis anos, além de multa. O texto também estabelece o aumento das penas de metade até o dobro, a depender da magnitude dos prejuízos, da vantagem ilícita obtida, do abalo à confiança no sistema financeiro nacional ou da pluralidade de vítimas. Em caso de reincidência, a pena poderá chegar ao triplo. Outro trecho prevê a possibilidade de o condenado ficar inabilitado para exercer atividade empresarial, impedido de ocupar cargos em conselhos de administração e fiscais, diretorias ou gerências, além de não poder gerir empresas por mandato ou gestão de negócio. Esse impedimento poderá durar por até cinco anos após o trânsito em julgado. O texto também altera a Lei dos Crimes contra o Sistema Financeiro Nacional para aperfeiçoar o crime de induzir ou manter em erro sócios, acionistas, investidores ou repartições públicas sobre a situação financeira, contábil ou patrimonial de uma sociedade, por meio da omissão ou prestação de informações falsas. A pena passa a ser de reclusão de dois a seis anos e multa. Na proposta original, a autora, senadora Augusta Brito (PT-CE), estabelecia cinco novos crimes: indução a erro no mercado de capitais, fraude contábil, influência imprópria em auditorias, falsidade ideológica em manifestação e administração infiel. O projeto também estabelecia o dever de agir de diretores, gerentes, administradores, executivos, conselheiros, auditores independentes, consultores e analistas para evitar os crimes. O relator considerou que parte das tipificações era excessivamente abrangente ou repetia crimes já previstos na legislação. O caso das Lojas Americanas veio à tona em janeiro de 2023, quando a companhia revelou inconsistências contábeis estimadas inicialmente em R$ 20 bilhões, relacionadas principalmente à contabilização de operações de risco sacado como despesas com fornecedores, em vez de dívidas bancárias. A prática teria inflado artificialmente os resultados da empresa e ocultado seu real endividamento, levando à descoberta de um rombo bilionário, à crise financeira da varejista e ao pedido de recuperação judicial. O episódio provocou prejuízos a investidores e credores e levantou questionamentos sobre a atuação de administradores e auditorias independentes. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Naomi Matsui). Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop, announced today the opening of a new shop at EastVillage on November 14, the 425-acre mixed-use development taking shape along East Parmer Lane in Northeast Austin’s Tech Ridge corridor. Serving EastVillage residents, nearby neighborhoods and employees throughout one of Austin’s largest technology and employment centers, the new Potbelly brings the brand’s signature neighborhood experience to the community. It joins more than 60 shops operating throughout Texas and offers the toasty warm sandwiches the brand is known for, alongside wraps, signature salads, hand-dipped shakes, freshly baked cookies and other craveable menu items. “EastVillage is creating something Northeast Austin has needed – a place where residents, employees and visitors can spend time together without having to head across the city,” said Jignesh Patel, who is opening his third Potbelly with business partner Nitin Patel, as part of a 15-unit Central Texas development agreement. “This is a natural home for Potbelly. We’re excited to serve the people who already live and work nearby while growing alongside a community that is just beginning to take shape.” Designed to bring a more walkable, downtown-style experience to a traditionally car-oriented part of the city, EastVillage is adding restaurants like Potbelly, along with retail, entertainment, residences, office space and outdoor recreation. Its plans include a 1.5-acre village green, more than five miles of hike-and-bike trails and a 150-acre natural preserve. Following recent shop openings in Georgetown and Hutto, Jignesh and Nitin were drawn to the energy surrounding EastVillage and the opportunity to serve a unique mix of guests. To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a celebration on December 14. Guests can also enjoy a ribbon-cutting, a spin wheel activation and a Potbelly Perks Plinko game for chances to win exclusive merchandise, free food and other prizes. The new shop will offer convenient options for lunch, dinner and everything in between. Regular operating hours are 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Delivery, order ahead and catering are available in-shop, through Potbelly.com and in the Potbelly App, with third-party delivery services also available. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where members can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. To entice these shoppers into becoming customers, ensure you’re getting in front of them when it matters most. Whether through custom designed holiday cards mailed to your community or seasonal flyers handed out at pop up markets or festivals to spread the word, customers pay attention to the details, especially when they make a spot standout during the hectic holiday rush. Choose something intriguing to customers, but not so overwhelming they turn away. This can be something as simple as a sidewalk A-frame sign outside your restaurant featuring all your best holiday deals and an online QR code for a virtual menu, or a branded banner that offers a fun photo opp and offers a discount for sharing on socials. Think of a customer walking by chilly after a long day of shopping and festive activities, they need a cozy escape to relax and refuel. For a cohesive look, choose one festive design style and stick to it while interspersing brand fonts, colors and illustration styles to make patrons affiliate it with your store. Ruby Tuesday, a leading casual American bar and grill chain, is introducing a refreshed core menu nationwide, putting a renewed focus on the categories that have long defined the brand: burgers, ribs, seafood and the signature Garden Bar. The menu features an expanded burger selection, including the return of the fan-favorite Colossal Burger, larger eight-ounce chicken breasts in every chicken sandwich and entrée, and new appetizers with an updated queso recipe. “We know what our guests come to Ruby Tuesday for, and this menu is about putting even more focus behind those favorites while making ordering easier,” said Kevin FitzPatrick, chief marketing officer at Ruby Tuesday. “By streamlining our menu and strengthening the offerings we’re known for, we’re making it easier for guests to find what they love. When Jana Brodeur joined TCBY in 2017, she was a high school senior planning to open a dance studio. Her sister helped her get the job at the frozen yogurt shop. Brodeur did not foresee it becoming the foundation of her career. That possibility emerged as she took on more responsibility. The owners offered her a college internship. By the time she graduated in 2021 with a degree focused on business and entrepreneurship, she had worked across nearly every part of the operation. “I worked all the time,” Brodeur says. “I learned every aspect of the business.” The dance studio gave way to a different entrepreneurial opportunity. Brodeur had developed customer relationships, found room to be creative, and discovered the family environment she wanted professionally. She eventually acquired the TCBY where she started as an employee. Her progression gave her an advantage most new franchisees do not have. She understood the products, procedures, customers, catering business, and daily rhythms. Her knowledge impressed the instructor when she traveled to Salt Lake City for franchise training. Brodeur also inherited a team that understood the restaurant. She did not replace any employees, which created continuity during a major personal transition. Also, her daughter was born near the time Brodeur became the franchisee. The circumstances forced her to balance motherhood with first-time ownership. Brodeur could not immediately spend as much time inside the shop as she envisioned, so she relied on employees to run shifts as she handled administrative work. She recalls making business calls from her hospital bed the day after giving birth. Six days later, her daughter joined her for a photo shoot at the restaurant. “I had to make things work, and it’s something that I’m proud of saying that I was able to do this at that time, and I wouldn’t have changed it for anything,” she says. Her experience under the prior owners prepared her for operations, but ownership exposed her to financial responsibilities she had not seen. She needed to monitor food costs, labor, and other expenses that had not fallen within her employee duties. “I definitely think it would have to be on the financial side of things, making sure that all of my costs are where they should be, and all of my labor is where it should be,” says Brodeur, discussing what surprised her the most about franchise ownership. Longtime guests remembered Brodeur from her first shifts and watched her progress into ownership. They knew when she became a mother and regularly asked how her daughter was doing. Those connections influence how she wants employees to interact with customers. “I’m communicating with these customers like they’re my best friends,” Brodeur says. “I want my employees to see that as well, because I want them to do the same thing.” That service has helped make the shop one of TCBY’s stronger performers.
