articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The 2027 report findings point to a generation reshaping when, why and what people eat. Yum! Brands, Inc. today released its second annual Food Trends Report, “What’s Next in Dining,” developed with its in-house marketing strategy, consumer insights and innovation agency Collider Lab. With more than 44,000 restaurants across its KFC, Taco Bell and Habit Burger & Grill brands, Yum! draws on global consumer insights, cultural analysis and menu testing to explore how all-day snacking, more memorable restaurant experiences and globally inspired flavors are changing what people crave and where they dine. The 2027 report findings point to a generation reshaping when, why and what people eat. Among the biggest takeaways: Gen Z is officially in permanent snack mode: 20% of restaurant visits among QSR customers ages 18–24 are for snack occasions, double the rate of customers 25 and older. Restaurants are becoming destinations: Younger consumers are nearly twice as likely to choose a restaurant that offers a more special experience. Global flavors are bringing a new sense of adventure to familiar favorites: Globally inspired menu ideas accounted for 35% of the top concepts ranked highest on modernity in the U.S., up from just 5% in 2025. “The next generation isn’t organizing its day around three meals, and it isn’t choosing restaurants on convenience alone,” said Ken Muench, Chief Marketing Officer, Yum! Brands and Co-Founder of Collider Lab. “People want food that fits the moment, an experience that feels worth having and a chance to discover something new. Understanding those shifts is central to our Raise the B.A.R. priorities and our work to Battle for the Future Consumer. Jimmy John’s is bringing a little Griswold-style chaos to the holidays with the Christmas Vacation Feast, a limited-time meal inspired by the legendary holiday film, National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation . Packed with festive flavors, collectible swag and plenty of over-the-top holiday spirit, it’s everything fans love about the movie, served Jimmy John’s style. The Christmas Vacation Feast is stacked with festive favorites, including the Jelly of the Month Club Sandwich, Stuffing Flavored Jimmy Chips and the Griswold Family Chaos Cookie, complete with a Crunch Enhancer Clark Griswold himself would appreciate. Everything comes wrapped in custom National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation-inspired packaging, bringing a little extra holiday chaos to every order. And because no Griswold holiday is complete without Cousin Eddie, every feast also includes an exclusive collectible turtleneck dickie. Available in four colors and featuring iconic movie quotes, it’s the perfect finishing touch for ugly sweater season. Each bite delivers a dose of much-needed holiday nostalgia. Stuffing Flavored Jimmy Chips deliver all the savory, herby goodness of classic holiday stuffing in a kettle-cooked chip. All the stuffing flavor, none of the prep work. The Griswold Family Chaos Cookie does what the Griswolds would do: goes completely overboard with chocolate chips, festive candies, peppermint, pretzels, marshmallows, sprinkles and a cornflake “Crunch Enhancer” inspired by Clark’s unforgettable holiday creation. The Cousin Eddie-inspired turtleneck dickie comes in four festive colors. Featuring fan-favorite movie quotes like “You Serious, Clark?” and “Save the Neck,” the collectible dickies offer four styles worthy of any holiday gathering. While the Jelly of the Month Club is sure to get gobbled up this holiday, those craving their go-to Jimmy John’s Favorite sandwich can customize the Christmas Vacation Feast with any Toasted sandwich, chips, or cookie. For fans collecting all four of the Cousin Eddie-inspired dickies, whether it’s for stocking stuffers or an ugly sweater party, each will also be available for individual purchase. “When it comes to the holidays, Clark Griswold set the bar impossibly high,” said Suzanne DeRouchie, Vice President of Integrated Marketing Communications at Jimmy John’s. “We wanted to capture that same over-the-top energy in a way only Jimmy John’s could. articles.title: Vivara inaugura loja “ícone” no Shopping JK Iguatemi
articles.titleKo: Vivara inaugura loja “ícone” no Shopping JK Iguatemi
articles.originalSummary: A Vivara inaugurou uma nova loja no Shopping JK Iguatemi, em São Paulo, reforçando sua presença em um dos principais endereços de luxo da capital paulista. A empresa informou que o espaço representa um movimento de renovação da experiência de compra, com um projeto que preserva a identidade da joalheria brasileira enquanto soma uma interpretação contemporânea de seus elementos tradicionais. Com arquitetura assinada pelo Estúdio Tupi, o projeto parte do conceito de “de-novo”, uma proposta que revisita os elementos já reconhecidos no universo visual da Vivara para reorganizá-los em outras formas e composições. A ideia é construir uma nova identidade para o espaço mantendo a tradição da marca e estabelecendo um diálogo entre sua trajetória e uma nova maneira de apresentar suas joias. “Ao longo de sua história, a Vivara construiu uma identidade muito forte e acreditamos que evoluir também significa encontrar novas formas de expressar essa essência. A loja ícone no JK Iguatemi representa esse movimento, ao reunir a tradição da nossa joalheria a uma visão contemporânea de varejo. Queremos continuar proporcionando experiências que fortaleçam a relação dos nossos clientes com a marca”, afirmou Marina Kaufman, presidente do Conselho de Administração da Vivara . A proposta ganha forma por meio da combinação de materiais, texturas e volumes. Revestimentos em pedra, marcenaria em madeira, balcões de mármore rosado e um piso de desenho geométrico criam um ambiente que equilibra sofisticação e contemporaneidade. As vitrines, os expositores e as áreas de atendimento integram essa composição, com espaços pensados para valorizar as joias e proporcionar uma experiência de compra única, individual e acolhedora. Milk & Honey, the Southern-inspired flagship brand of Thompson Restaurants, a family-run hospitality company, officially opens its newest restaurant at Tysons Corner Center on Wednesday, Nov. 18. The brand’s 22nd location is also its largest and most elevated to date, and it introduces Milk & Honey Express, a fast-casual concept next door. The restaurant is located at 1961 Chain Bridge Road, G21U, in Tysons, inside one of the Washington region’s premier shopping, dining and entertainment destinations. It follows back-to-back openings in Gainesville and Manassas this summer and marks the brand’s latest push into Northern Virginia. “Opening Milk & Honey at Tysons Corner Center is a milestone for our brand,” said Alex Berentzen, chief operating officer of Thompson Restaurants. “As our largest location to date, it reflects the continued evolution of the concept and brings our signature hospitality and Southern-inspired cuisine to one of the most dynamic destinations in the DMV. We’re also proud to introduce Milk & Honey Express, a convenient new way for guests on the go to enjoy their favorites whether you’re shopping, working or visiting Tysons.” At approximately 4,907 square feet, the Tysons restaurant is the brand’s most ambitious project yet. An open kitchen lets guests see the energy and craftsmanship behind the culinary operation, and spacious dining areas are designed for everyday meals as well as larger social gatherings. The restaurant is visible and accessible directly from inside the mall. Next door, Milk & Honey Express serves signature breakfast items, coffee beverages, quick-service meals and select dinner offerings for shoppers, commuters and guests on the go, with online ordering through Thompson Restaurants’ website. Together, the two make up the first dual-concept experience in the brand’s history. The restaurant seats 230 guests across 156 indoor seats, a 10-seat bar and a 64-seat patio. The opening is expected to create more than 100 jobs across management, culinary, hospitality and service roles. Guests can enjoy the brand’s full menu of Southern-inspired favorites throughout the day, including signature dishes such as Smothered Chicken and Biscuits, Chicken and Biscoff Waffles, Fried Green Tomatoes, Crispy Salmon Hash, House-Rubbed Steak and Eggs, and Carolina Low Country Gumbo. The beverage program features signature cocktails including the Biscoff Espresso Martini, Jim Beam Blackberry Smash and Spicy Guava Margarita, alongside a selection of mocktails. articles.title: O que Jeff Bezos tem a ver com a escolha de Robert Pattinson como o novo James Bond?
articles.titleKo: O que Jeff Bezos tem a ver com a escolha de Robert Pattinson como o novo James Bond?
articles.originalSummary: O fundador da Amazon, Jeff Bezos, afirmou, na terça-feira, 17, que esteve “bastante envolvido” na escalação de Robert Pattinson como o próximo James Bond no 26º filme de 007, que terá direção de Denis Villeneuve. Segundo informações da Reuters , a declaração ocorreu na conferência Silicon Valley & The World, organizada pelo Semafor. A relação entre a Amazon e 007 veio a público em 2022, quando a multinacional de e-commerce finalizou a compra da MGM, estúdio-mãe da franquia de James Bond. Em fevereiro de 2025, as ligações se estreitaram ainda mais: a companhia assumiu o controle dos direitos criativos sobre o filme, que pertencia à família Broccoli desde 1962. Como declarou Bezos, a Amazon foi decisiva na escolha de Pattinson, conhecido por seus papéis em Crepúsculo e Batman, para encarnar o lendário espião. A empresa teria reduzido a lista de candidatos e realizado os testes de câmera com cinco atores – onde cada um interpretou três cenas com figurinos completos e em cenários de filmagem -, informou a Reuters . “Nos reunimos na sexta-feira para passar algumas horas assistindo a todos os testes de câmera e analisando tudo”, disse o empresário na conferência. Pattinson, de 40 anos, venceu uma disputa que contava com Nicholas Hoult (Superman), Josh O’Connor (Rivais), Callum Turner (Só Por Uma Noite) e Jack Lowden (Slow Horses). Bezos também revelou que, inicialmente, a escalação de Pattinson como James Bond lhe causava certo receio devido ao seu já consolidado alcance em Hollywood: “Pensamos que talvez devêssemos escolher alguém um pouco menos conhecido”. Nos testes de câmera, entretanto, ficou evidente que o ator seria o próximo James Bond, contou o presidente da Amazon. Robert Pattinson sucederá Daniel Craig como o protagonista da mais famosa franquia de espionagem. Experiente em sucessos de bilheteria, o ator já esteve em dois deles só neste ano: A Odisseia, de Christopher Nolan, que acaba de chegar ao streaming com 90 minutos de bastidores, e O Drama, de Kristoffer Borgli. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Maria Fernanda Barros). Batizada de Hybrid House, a unidade oferece sessões gratuitas e abertas ao público às terças e sábados, mediante inscrição prévia. As aulas ocorrem diariamente, das 5h30 às 19h30, de segunda a sexta-feira, e das 6h às 11h, aos sábados e domingos. O espaço também recebe alunos matriculados na rede de academias e usuários do Totalpass e Wellhub, que podem agendar as aulas. O projeto foi desenvolvido em parceria com o Hyper Training Club (HTC) e com a Urbia, concessionária gestora do parque. “O Parque Ibirapuera já recebe cerca de 9,6 milhões de pessoas anualmente para a prática esportiva. Com a chegada da Hybrid House, os visitantes poderão conhecer e experimentar gratuitamente uma nova modalidade que está em ascensão”, afirma Samuel Lloyd, diretor da Urbia. Os frequentadores têm acesso a ativações da Adidas e podem experimentar produtos da marca, como os modelos da linha Adizero Dropset. A Hybrid House é a oitava unidade do HTC em São Paulo. Ser a primeira loja da América Latina a fazer um projeto com a Adidas Consortium é muito especial para a gente, para o Brasil e para todo mundo que nos acompanha desde o começo”, contou Pedro Prado, sócio da Guadalupe Store. Hi Auto, the AI Order Taker technology purpose-built for quick-service restaurant drive-thrus, today announced that Checkers & Rally’s has extended its partnership with the company through 2030, building on a relationship that began in 2023. Checkers & Rally’s also plans to expand its Hi Auto footprint by 38% by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Hi Auto currently takes orders at 267 Checkers & Rally’s drive-thrus and has processed more than 11 million orders at the brands this year. The technology has lifted average ticket size by 1.1% while cutting the number of orders that need a crew member to step in by half since January, freeing restaurant teams to focus on food quality and hospitality. “Checkers & Rally’s challenged us to prove that AI in the drive-thru drives growth, not just efficiency,” said Roy Baharav , CEO and Co-Founder of Hi Auto. “Today we process more than a million of their orders every month, grow the average ticket and serve guests in English and Spanish without missing a beat. Extending our partnership through 2030 and expanding into more restaurants shows what this category can deliver when the technology performs at scale.” A key differentiator in the deployment is Hi Auto’s ability to take orders in English and Spanish, including when a guest switches between both languages in the same order. That capability fits the diverse communities Checkers & Rally’s serves and sets the deployment apart from single language systems. “At Checkers & Rally’s, speed, convenience and accuracy are central to the drive-thru experience,” said Dave Pelletier, Chief Operating Officer at Checkers & Rally’s. “Our partnership with Hi Auto reflects our continued investment in technology that supports restaurant operations while making the ordering experience more seamless for our guests. We’re excited to build on this partnership and continue exploring how AI can drive greater efficiency and enhance the guest experience across our system.” “Since bringing Hi Auto into my drive-thrus, we’ve seen a real bump in ticket size and smoother service, and every guest gets the same great experience whether they order in English or Spanish,” said Bobby Barrios , Chief Operating Officer at Barrios Foods Inc. Hi Auto’s AI Order Taker greets guests, takes and upsells orders, and posts them directly to the POS, with a human fallback whenever a guest needs a team member. To learn more, visit https://hi.auto. articles.title: Your Holiday Campaign is Ready. Your Franchisees Aren’t
articles.titleKo: Your Holiday Campaign is Ready. Your Franchisees Aren’t
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Every year, QSR marketing teams ship holiday campaigns they’re proud of. Then those campaigns hit 800 franchisees, each with their own stores, local priorities and ad buys across every conceivable channel. The store near the mall wants to push gift cards and grab-and-go. The suburban store wants family bundles. The franchisee two exits down the highway is fighting a new competitor and needs a sharper price. Not to mention the different state regulations that need to be catered for. They all want to utilize the national creative because they understand the value of the brand they’ve bought into,but none of them can use it exactly as it is. So they email corporate. Corporate adds their request or approvals to the queue, and by the time the localized version comes back, the week that mattered is gone. That’s the real holiday problem for franchise brands, and it lives in the last mile, when getting it wrong is the most expensive. National sets the tone. Local wins the sale. Nobody’s arguing against national campaigns. They build the brand, set the look and keep the message consistent across a thousand doors. That job matters. But customers don’t buy from a national campaign. They buy from a store, on a street, against whoever’s across the road. Demand, pricing and competition change from one neighborhood to the next, and over the holidays those gaps get wider. A location near a shopping center might see its busiest period during last-minute holiday shopping, while another may depend on catering orders or family meals. Both are working from the same national campaign, but their immediate priorities are different. Most franchise marketing systems still treat every restaurant as if it were the same. The answer isn’t to abandon the national playbook. It’s to build it so stores can adapt it without asking permission for every change. The bottleneck is process. QSR brands aren’t short on ideas. What they’re short on is time and budget. They can’t produce enough content quickly enough across every channel for every market. Think about what one holiday promo needs before it works locally: different prices, different offers, store hours and addresses, plus a dozen formats from window clings to Instagram stories. Every change can mean a request, a revision and an approval. Multiply that by a few hundred stores and your marketing team is now running a design agency without the resources to do it properly. And the requests don’t all arrive at once. One franchise needs a new offer approved on Monday, another needs updates creative for a location promotion on Wednesday. A third discovers that the available assets don’t fit the advertising channel they are using. Franchisees miss their moment. Corporate drowns in admin and still can’t see what’s running where. Making more content won’t fix that. Getting it through the system faster will. Where AI earns its keep. There’s plenty of noise about AI writing entire campaigns. For franchise brands, the bigger win is far less glamorous:eliminating the busywork. Resizing. Swapping prices. Updating store details. Reformatting for every channel. Chasing sign-off on routine changes that already meet brand requirements.A person doesn’t need to touch every one of those tasks. Lock the brand elements nationally, open up the fields franchisees can change, and let predefined rules handle the routine approvals. Location, offer and call to action stay editable. Logo, layout and tone stay locked. Corporate reviews the exceptions instead of every flyer. This also makes it easier to respond when plans change. If a promotion needs to be updated across multiple locations, approved changes can be made without restarting the creative process for every store. People still own the strategy, the brand standards and the big calls. Automation just stops them from spending December resizing banners. Freedom

articles.title: Receita: organização criminosa do ramo das bets movimentou R$ 11 bi em 2025
articles.titleKo: Receita: organização criminosa do ramo das bets movimentou R$ 11 bi em 2025
articles.originalSummary: A Operação Cash Out, que atingiu um grupo empresarial do ramo das bets , identificou que a organização criminosa movimentou cerca de R$ 11 bilhões no exercício de 2025. O negócio, sediado em Curaçao, ocultava os recursos ilícitos por meio de operações de câmbio, utilização de apostadores fictícios e empresas laranjas. Segundo o secretário especial da Receita Federal, Robinson Barreirinhas, o Fisco identificou um padrão entre empresas de apostas que operavam irregularmente para acumular recursos e pagar a outorga de R$ 30 milhões, necessária para regularizar suas atividades. “Esse modus operandi perverso se refere a evasão de divisas, lavagem de dinheiro, ocultação da origem de recursos por meio de operações de câmbio, algumas delas com remessas, outras apenas simulando a remessa e utilização de apostadores laranjas”, destacou o secretário. “Esses recursos voltavam do exterior e nós estamos seguros que foram utilizados depois para o próprio pagamento da outorga regular. Nós estamos tratando aqui de uma casa de apostas que é bastante infiltrada no ecossistema do esporte no Brasil, patrocinando diversos clubes, programas de televisão, figuras que se aproximam de figuras da mídia nacional”, afirmou Barreirinhas. De acordo com o chefe do Fisco, a organização criminosa em questão utilizava com frequência empresas laranjas ligadas ao ramo de eventos para ocultar os recursos oriundos da exploração ilegal de bets. “Aquele benefício fiscal do Perse se prestava muito a esse tipo de lavagem de dinheiro, porque as empresas de eventos não pagavam nenhum tributo federal sobre essas receitas”, lembrou Barreirinhas. “Era o instrumento perfeito de lavagem de dinheiro”, acrescentou. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (Franco Dantas, especial para a AE). articles.title: Novo SAC na véspera da Black Friday: o que o varejo precisa ajustar já
articles.titleKo: Novo SAC na véspera da Black Friday: o que o varejo precisa ajustar já
articles.originalSummary: Regra nova às vésperas da data mais movimentada do ano. Você provavelmente tem uma história de SAC para contar. A musiquinha que não termina, o menu que dá voltas e devolve você ao início, a terceira atendente que pede, com toda a educação do mundo, que você explique tudo de novo. Quem trabalha no varejo conhece essa cena dos dois lados do balcão. Desde 2 de novembro, boa parte dessas histórias deixou de ser só irritante e passou a ser descumprimento de norma. Nesse dia entrou em vigor o Decreto nº 13.135/2026, publicado no Diário Oficial em 13 de outubro. O texto revogou o Decreto nº 11.034/2022 e reescreveu as regras do Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor. O mercado continua chamando de “Lei do SAC”. Vou chamar assim também, embora tecnicamente seja um decreto, e esse detalhe tem consequências que comento mais adiante. O calendário não ajudou. Foram 20 dias entre a publicação e a vigência, sem regra de transição, para rever URA, chatbot, escala de atendentes e contrato com call center. E o primeiro grande teste já está marcado: a Black Friday, no dia 27. Afinal, isso vale para o varejo? Essa é a pergunta que mais tenho ouvido, e a resposta honesta é: depende do que a empresa vende e de como vende. O decreto continua mirando, em primeiro lugar, os serviços regulados pelo governo federal, como telefonia, energia, planos de saúde e aviação. A novidade é que agora entram expressamente os serviços financeiros, de pagamento e de crédito oferecidos por meios digitais sob supervisão do Banco Central. Para o varejo, isso não é detalhe. Carteira digital, cartão próprio, conta de pagamento e parcelamento via fintech parceira são, hoje, parte do negócio de muitas redes. Outra mudança: as agências e os órgãos reguladores de cada setor passam a definir os critérios de enquadramento. Ou seja, a fotografia completa de quem está dentro ainda vai se formar nos CDC (Código de Defesa do Consumidor) continua valendo inteiro, e eu não me surpreenderia se Procons e juízes passassem a usar os parâmetros do novo SAC como régua do que é um atendimento razoável. Quem estiver longe demais dela vai ter dificuldade para se explicar. O que muda na prática Gente de verdade, todos os dias. A regra antiga pedia atendimento humano por pelo menos 8 horas diárias. Agora ele é obrigatório das 8h às 20h, inclusive aos sábado, domingo e feriado, tanto no telefone quanto nos canais digitais. Além disso, pelo menos um canal eletrônico precisa funcionar 24 horas . Para quem dimensiona equipe, é aqui que a conta muda. O robô pode ficar, desde que abra a porta. O decreto não proíbe inteligência artificial nem chatbot. Eles podem fazer triagem e até resolver a demanda. A condição é que o consumidor consiga falar com uma pessoa em qualquer etapa, sem ter de informar CPF, número do pedido ou qualquer dado antes disso. Cinco níveis e acabou. Menus eletrônicos e URA não podem passar de cinco níveis. As opções de cancelar e de falar com um atendente têm de aparecer em todos eles, a começar pelo primeiro. Também fica proibido o velho “para isso, acesse nosso aplicativo”: o canal que recebeu a demanda resolve, salvo quando o atendimento presencial for mesmo indispensável. No telefone, quem pede para falar com uma pessoa deve ser atendido em até 20 segundos em pelo menos 80% dos casos, e em até 5 minutos nos demais, ressalvada regra setorial própria. O consumidor tem de ser informado do tempo estimado de espera. Se a ligação cair, a empresa tem 5 minutos para retornar, com o mesmo protocolo e sem começar do zero. Silêncio publicitário. O decreto anterior admitia propaganda na espera, desde que o consumidor consentisse. Isso acabou. Não pode haver publicidade em nenhuma etapa do atendimento, com ou sem consentimento. Em plena temporada de ofertas, convém ouvir de novo cada mensagem gravada. Outra mudança que o consumidor vai sentir logo: a empresa deve acompanhar a demanda até o fim e não pode exigir que o consumidor recomece. Pedir que ele repita o que já disse só é aceito qua

articles.title: Drive-Thru AI Is Freeing Up Crews. What Happens Next?
articles.titleKo: Drive-Thru AI Is Freeing Up Crews. What Happens Next?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Restaurant leaders have spent years training crews on the fundamentals of good service. AI doesn’t change those expectations. One finding in the 2026 QSR Drive-Thru Report caught my attention. In drive-thru visits where AI handled the order, mystery shoppers were 23.9 percentage points less likely to receive a thank-you at the pickup window. Positive assessments of crew demeanor were 15.7 percentage points lower. As someone who builds drive-thru AI, I think those numbers deserve a closer look. The study doesn’t tell us that AI caused those differences. And I don’t think the findings mean AI is inherently less hospitable than a human crew member. In some ways, AI has an advantage. It doesn’t get tired during the lunch rush or lose patience after answering the same question for the hundredth time. It can deliver the same friendly interaction on its five-hundredth order as it does on its first. But the findings do raise a question that restaurant operators and those of us building technology for them need to take seriously. We talk a lot about giving crews more time to focus on hospitality. What does that actually mean for someone juggling a dozen responsibilities during a lunch rush? The conversation doesn’t end at the speaker Before starting my company, I spent weeks standing near drive-thru order posts with a laptop, listening to hundreds of ordering conversations. I wanted to understand what actually happened between a guest pulling up to the speaker and placing an order. What struck me was how much crew members were juggling at once. They might be filling drinks, assembling orders or taking payments, all while taking orders through their headsets. And those orders weren’t always straightforward. Guests changed their minds, asked questions, made substitutions and occasionally ordered things that weren’t on the menu. Crew members had to keep up with every request, accurately enter orders into the point-of-sale system and make adjustments on the fly, all while keeping track of their other responsibilities. That’s where I see a real opportunity for AI. By handling the ordering conversation, AI can take one of those competing demands off a crew member’s plate. Crew members still wear headsets to monitor ordering conversations and step in when needed, but they no longer have to manage every exchange themselves. So, what does that mean for the guest? By the time they reach the pickup window, they may have spoken only to AI, and the crew member greeting them may not have participated in the ordering conversation at all. That doesn’t have to make the interaction less personal. With one less demand competing for their attention, crew members have an opportunity to make that first human exchange count. That could mean taking an extra moment to check that an order is complete, make sure food is packaged properly or explain a delay. Brands can also build a friendly greeting into their pickup-window scripts. And sometimes, it’s as simple as making eye contact, smiling and offering a genuine thank-you instead of hurriedly passing a bag through the window. There’s a benefit for the crew, too. Restaurant jobs are demanding, particularly during peak periods. Having one less conversation to manage while juggling other responsibilities can make a stressful shift a little more manageable. But none of these improvements is guaranteed simply because AI is taking orders. Better hospitality still takes intention Restaurant leaders have spent years training crews on the fundamentals of good service. AI doesn’t change those expectations. It creates an opportunity to help teams meet them more consistently. Making the most of that opportunity requires more than introducing the technology. articles.title: Sweetgreen Launches Agentic Ordering through Claude and ChatGPT
articles.titleKo: Sweetgreen Launches Agentic Ordering through Claude and ChatGPT
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Sweetgreen announced that customers can now order sweetgreen through Claude and ChatGPT. Customers can ask AI assistants for recommendations based on nutrition goals, dietary needs and taste preferences, build an order directly in the conversation, and complete their purchase in the sweetgreen app or website, where their rewards, credits and saved payment methods already live. The launch comes as diners grow more comfortable letting AI handle their orders, with roughly six in ten millennial and Gen Z adults saying they would place an order with an AI-generated bot, according to the National Restaurant Association . For sweetgreen, meeting customers via AI is the next step in its push to make the brand easy to discover, order and enjoy. To power the experience, sweetgreen is making its menu machine-readable, optimizing the data based on how AI assistants respond to customer requests. The goal is to win more occasions by giving agents better context about sweetgreen’s menu so they can recommend the right signature entree to each customer. “We started sweetgreen to connect people to real food, and that mission continues to shape how we innovate. I want sweetgreen to be accessible wherever our customers are, with an experience that feels personal to each of them,” said Jonathan Neman, Co-Founder and CEO of sweetgreen. “Bringing sweetgreen to Claude and ChatGPT gives people a new way to discover meals built around their tastes, dietary preferences and goals. It reflects the culture we’ve built: always looking for better ways to serve our customers and make real food part of their everyday lives.” Built for How People Decide What to Eat Customers increasingly start with a goal rather than a menu, whether that’s hitting a protein target, avoiding an allergen or trying something new. The sweetgreen menu already provides the flexibility and detail that AI assistants need to make useful recommendations, including ingredients, nutrition, allergens, pricing and real-time availability at each restaurant. The AI assistants can now use this information to create meals that fit customers’ goals and specific tastes. “We’re seeing a real shift from searching to delegating. People now hand an AI agent a goal, like a dairy-free dinner or a lunch that fits their training plan, and expect it to come back with the right recommendation,” said Wouleta Ayele, Chief Technology Officer at sweetgreen. “That only works if the agent has ingredient information it can trust. So we’ve made our menu machine-readable, with every ingredient, allergen and price accurate down to the individual restaurant.” How It Works Ordering sweetgreen through an AI assistant takes just a few steps: Turn on the sweetgreen connector in Claude and ChatGPT on desktop or mobile. Ask the AI assistant to help you find menu options that fit your needs – nutrition goals, dietary restrictions, or specific taste profiles. Confirm your local restaurant and browse a visual menu in the conversation, with prices, calories and allergens for every item, plus recommendations tailored to the request. Add items to a bag with a tap. Complete the order in the sweetgreen app or website using saved payments, credits and rewards. This makes checkout secure and consistent, and customers can earn rewards. Sweetgreen is available today through Claude and ChatGPT for pickup and first-party delivery orders at all sweetgreen restaurants. To get started, search for sweetgreen in the Claude and ChatGPT app directories. Learn more at https://www.sweetgreen.com/landing/order-with-ai . articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Smoothie King, whose vision is to make the world a better place by nourishing healthy habits, delivered strong Q3 sales growth and increased guest visits, outperforming several leading restaurant brands as consumers increasingly prioritize health, wellness and nutrition. Same-store sales grew 9% in July and climbed to 11.6% in August. For the third quarter overall, same-store sales increased 8.7%, accelerating from 5.9% in Q2, alongside positive same-store visit growth. We’re continuing to build on this momentum by expanding our menu and investing in our new ways to be relevant, all while staying true to the vision that has guided us for more than 50 years.” MENU INNOVATION THAT GIVES GUESTS MORE REASONS TO VISIT Building on more than 50 years of nutritional expertise, Smoothie King continues to evolve its menu to meet consumers’ growing interest in health and wellness, delivering options that balance nutrition with great taste. The brand’s increase in same-store visits in Q3 reflects continued guest engagement and underscores the opportunity to build on that momentum through menu innovation that aligns with consumers’ changing preferences. Following the introduction of its first nationwide Power Eats food menu in 2025, Smoothie King continues to expand its food platform with protein-forward offerings, including its new protein-packed Chicken Flatbreads, which launched in July. Guests are increasingly pairing smoothies and food as a complete meal, with the brand’s smoothie and food bundle quickly becoming another popular way guests order food, including among its most loyal members. Together, smoothies and food give guests an easy, satisfying meal built around their nutritional goals nourishing their potential throughout the day, while creating additional occasions to visit and opportunities for franchisees to grow sales. TECHNOLOGY DRIVING GROWTH AND FRANCHISEE SUCCESS As Smoothie King continues to grow, technology is playing an increasingly important role in strengthening restaurant operations, improving efficiency and supporting franchisee profitability. articles.title: Bancos fecham nesta sexta-feira; veja como pagar contas no feriado
articles.titleKo: Bancos fecham nesta sexta-feira; veja como pagar contas no feriado
articles.originalSummary: Na próxima sexta-feira, 20, feriado nacional do Dia da Consciência Negra, os bancos de todo o País não terão atendimento presencial. Segundo a Federação Brasileira de Bancos (Febraban), os clientes poderão utilizar aplicativos, internet banking e demais canais digitais para realizar operações bancárias. As salas de autoatendimento poderão estar disponíveis, a critério de cada instituição financeira. O Pix funciona normalmente, 24 horas por dia, inclusive nos feriados e fins de semana. O diretor de Serviços e Segurança da Febraban, Raphael Mielle, lembra que atualmente os clientes conseguem resolver boa parte de suas necessidades bancárias pelo celular ou computador, sem precisar ir a uma agência. “Mesmo nos feriados, os canais digitais continuam disponíveis para consultas, transferências e pagamentos”, diz. Operações que dependem de compensação bancária, como TEDs e cheques, não serão processadas no feriado. Os clientes poderão agendar transferências e pagamentos pelos canais digitais, com processamento no próximo dia útil. Contas de consumo, como água, energia e telefone, e os boletos bancários com vencimento no dia 20 de novembro poderão ser pagos na segunda-feira, 23, sem acréscimos. Já os tributos e impostos com vencimento no feriado devem ser pagos antecipadamente para evitar a incidência de juros e multa. Feriados de novembro movimentam R$ 4 bi em SP Os dois feriados prolongados de novembro devem injetar R$ 4 bilhões nos setores de hospedagem e alimentação fora do lar no Estado de São Paulo , segundo estimativa da Federação de Hotéis, Restaurantes e Bares do Estado de São Paulo (Fhoresp), que representa mais de 550 mil estabelecimentos e 24 sindicatos patronais. Segundo a entidade, o posicionamento dos feriados em uma segunda e uma sexta-feira favorece deslocamentos de curta duração para o litoral paulista, estâncias turísticas, polos de esportes de aventura e destinos do interior do Estado, principalmente a partir da Região Metropolitana de São Paulo e de outros centros urbanos. articles.title: Why Food Safety Culture Must Include Recall Readiness
articles.titleKo: Why Food Safety Culture Must Include Recall Readiness
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ineffective recalls can have serious, long-term, and costly consequences, including increasing public health risks and eroding consumer trust. Food safety culture is one of the industry’s most talked-about priorities, especially in the wake of the recent, large-scale food recalls, including lettuce , jalapeños , meat , eggs , and blueberries . Many restaurant brands have invested heavily in developing strong food safety cultures, with training and education at the forefront of these efforts. At the same time, the recent string of widespread food recalls spotlights something those programs don’t always address: whether the culture extends to recall preparation. After all, your restaurant doesn’t truly have a good food safety culture if you aren’t recall ready. Recall readiness is food safety culture tested under pressure . Consider this: if your restaurant received contaminated lettuce, tainted meat, or other products involved in a recall, would your team know exactly what to do? Even if you have an exceptional food safety culture “on paper,” would this culture drive proper behaviors and decisions in practice, as employees are under extreme pressure? A Recall Gap Puts Guests at Risk Food safety culture with a gap at the recall level isn’t actually a strong food safety culture. Likewise, recall readiness doesn’t hold up without the cultural infrastructure supporting it. Neither initiative stands alone. Think seriously about whether your food safety culture extends to recall readiness. In many companies, recall preparation gets postponed due to its low-frequency nature, with brands earmarking their budgets and resources to daily food safety culture work instead. Unfortunately, recall readiness is a vital part of the culture, at the corporate level down to locations—yet it’s frequently put off until it’s too late. A strong food safety culture requires alignment between your company’s daily food safety protocols and your emergency response protocols. A breakdown during a recall is a systemic failure that can put your consumers, trading partners, and brand at risk. A Recall Gap Undermines Food Safety Culture When a food recall occurs, your company needs a proper, coordinated, and organized response to protect public health, your supply chain, and your brand reputation. Restaurant company leaders must ask themselves: What’s the extent of your food safety culture? Passing safety audits or hanging a certification in your restaurant locations is important, but these things don’t necessarily translate to a safe culture. Sometimes, food businesses mistake this documentation for “proof” of an outstanding food safety culture. Similarly, if a location runs through their checklists—they’ve completed food safety training, they passed a third-party audit, their teams regularly perform safety checks, etc.—they believe they have tangible evidence of an A+ food safety culture. However, food safety culture is actually tested when your team is under extreme pressure during a recall situation. If you’re truly recall ready, your team will be well-prepared and equipped to manage the situation properly: containing the recall, minimizing damages, and protecting public health. If you’re not recall ready, the opposite will be true. Being unprepared to handle a recall puts you and your trading partners at risk for major financial, legal, operational, and reputational damage. Remember: the gap between what your employees are supposed to do and what they actually do can make your guests, business, and trading partners vulnerable in a recall. articles.title: Kura Sushi Wants to Make Sushi a $12 Lunch Option
articles.titleKo: Kura Sushi Wants to Make Sushi a $12 Lunch Option
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Kura Sushi's same-store sales declined 5.7 percent in Q4, including an 11.5 percent traffic drop. Kura Sushi’s conveyor belts give diners plenty of reasons to keep reaching for another plate, but getting them to sit down for a weekday lunch is proving more difficult. With customer visits falling and its average check reaching $29, the revolving sushi chain is testing a less expensive way through the door. An October pilot offered meal combinations at $9.99 and $11.99, giving Kura an opportunity to compete for lunch occasions that its typical ticket may put out of reach. The discounted meals accounted for 5 percent of orders during the three-day test, even though Kura promoted them only to rewards members. As an additional positive, the lower-priced options did not reduce average spending per customer, prompting Kura to expand the test ahead of a planned nationwide rollout in fiscal Q2 (December 1 through February 28). READ MORE : Kura Sushi Welcomes Profit Growth Amid Volatile Environment Kura Sushi Hits its Stride Thanks to Collaborations, Tech Investments Before introducing the meals nationwide, Kura plans to adjust the offerings to ensure the lower prices don’t hurt its profit margins. It is also developing off-premises value bundles and preparing paid advertising to reach customers who have never visited. “So if somebody only has $12, we want Kura to be a great option. But if they can spend more, we want them to come as well,” said CEO Jimmy Uba. The push follows a fiscal fourth quarter in which same-store sales declined 5.7 percent, including an 11.5 percent traffic drop. Price and mix contributed 5.8 percent, with effective pricing of 4.2 percent. Kura traced much of its traffic weakness to weekday lunches after studying customer feedback in August. The pressure stretched across markets, making the challenge less a regional issue than a question of how the chain fits into consumers’ everyday spending. The company believes it is attracting diners accustomed to paying more for sushi, pointing to sustained gains in sales mix. Winning those customers, however, has not compensated for the loss of other visits. For instance, in Q1 thus far, same-store sales have improved to negative 3.1 percent, but Uba said the change has come from mix, with traffic largely tracking its Q4 performance. Kura is responding by holding off on another price increase. A previous 3.5 percent increase rolled off at the beginning of November, and the chain chose not to replace it. Its pricing decisions can change, but the current plan calls for margin improvement without additional menu pricing. Uba said rising sushi prices across the industry create an opportunity to attract a larger audience. Kura’s challenge is making its affordability more visible without weakening customers’ perception of its ingredients. Value combinations add another traffic tool to a business that has relied on pop-culture collaborations, collectible prizes, and limited-time food offerings to bring guests back. Kura plans eight intellectual property collaborations in fiscal 2027, up from seven last year. Its Yoshi campaign runs through November and December, followed by Hatsune Miku in January and Godzilla in February and March. Four additional collaborations will follow. The company is also increasing its Kura Reserve limited-time offerings from nine to 12. Not every fourth-quarter collaboration met expectations. Kura also saw traffic change when the World Cup began and expected visits to recover after the tournament ended. That rebound did not materialize as anticipated. In terms of development, Kura is switching how it measures expansion. After establishing a presence in 25 states and nearing 100 restaurants, the company is changing from a percentage-based growth target to an annual opening count that can increase gradually. O calendário promocional segue até o início de dezembro, com a etapa 12.12 prevista para o período de 4 a 9 de dezembro. As Campanhas PI são uma das principais ferramentas para impulsionar vendas no TikTok Shop. Voltadas a momentos importantes, como a estreia de uma marca na plataforma, lançamentos de produtos e grandes promoções, elas concentram ações de venda com participação de criadores de conteúdo, transmissões ao vivo e entretenimento. Elas são divididas em três formatos: Super Dia da Marca: reúne influenciadores, entretenimento e comércio eletrônico em uma ação de vendas de grande escala. Lançamentos: voltadas à divulgação de novos produtos, com foco em visibilidade e conversão. Inauguração: marca a entrada de grandes marcas na plataforma, com ações para ampliar o alcance desde a estreia. As ativações do “Super Dia da Marca” integram a campanha de Black Friday do TikTok Shop, que reúne 25 marcas dos segmentos de moda, beleza, tecnologia, casa, higiene, eletrodomésticos, limpeza e alimentação. A campanha segue o modelo de discovery commerce do TikTok Shop, em que os usuários descobrem produtos por meio de vídeos, transmissões ao vivo (LIVEs) e conteúdos de criadores e podem concluir a compra sem sair do aplicativo . Estudo realizado pelo TikTok Shop em parceria com a NielsenIQ mostra que 74% dos consumidores que compram on-line aprovam a integração entre entretenimento e compras. Além disso, 91% consideram as LIVEs úteis para esclarecer dúvidas e conhecer produtos, enquanto 82% avaliam que a plataforma oferece entregas rápidas. articles.titleKo: Jack in the Box’s CFO Steps Down Amid Leadership Changes
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Jack in the Box announced that Dawn Hooper will be stepping down as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective April 2, 2027. Hooper will continue to serve as CFO until that time and remain as a consultant as necessary throughout 2027 to support a smooth transition of responsibilities. The company has initiated a search for Hooper’s successor with the assistance of a leading executive search firm. “We thank Dawn for her service and dedication to Jack in the Box throughout her more than 25 years with the company,” said Mark King, Executive Chairman and Interim Chief Executive Officer. “Most recently, as Chief Financial Officer, Dawn has helped lead our efforts to reduce debt and optimize the company’s capital structure. We appreciate her ongoing support during this transition and wish her the best in her next chapter.” Additionally, the company has promoted Shannon McKinney from Senior Vice President, Chief Operating Officer, to Executive Vice President, Chief Operating Officer, effective immediately. In this expanded role, McKinney will oversee the company’s supply chain, in addition to his existing operations responsibilities. The company will continue to evolve its new leadership structure designed to support the company’s next chapter under President Taylor Montgomery, who is expected to succeed Mark King as Chief Executive Officer, as previously announced. “Evolving our leadership structure represents an important step in positioning Jack in the Box for long-term success,” said Montgomery. “Expanding Shannon’s operating responsibilities to include supply chain will help us simplify the organization and strengthen execution. The initiatives we are implementing will improve operational performance and building on these efforts will be critical to driving consistent same-store sales growth, margin expansion, and creating lasting value for our franchisees, employees and shareholders.” The post Jack in the Box’s CFO Steps Down Amid Leadership Changes appeared first on QSR Magazine .

The gains for Steak ‘n Shake continued into Q3, with the brand reporting domestic same-store sales growth of 15.5 percent. Building on a year-ago result of 15.6 percent, the brand is 31.1 percent higher on a two-year stack. Steak ‘n Shake’s makeup has shifted over that time. In Q3 2025, the company had 141 corporate stores, 173 “franchise-partner,” and 96 traditional franchises (the partner model is a $10,000 upfront single-store approach introduced in 2018 and outlined here ). Today, there are 123 company-run restaurants, 186 “franchise-partner,” and 88 traditional franchises. Steak ‘n Shake transitioned seven corporate locations to franchise-partner this past quarter and shuttered a net of one. It also closed a net of six traditional franchises. MORE: Steak ‘n Shake is Getting Political as it Keeps Driving Sales Additionally, as of September 30, eight of 123 company-operated venues were closed. Two were expected to reopen and the remaining six sold or leased. Ultimately, Steak ‘n Shake hopes to transition all corporate restaurants to owner-operators. Regarding that franchise-partner definition, which to the point, is becoming a more prevalent mix of Steak ‘n Shake’s overall footprint—now the largest of its three buckets by more than 60 units—saw Q3 same-store sales results even loftier at 19.1 percent. That’s 33.9 percent over two years. According to the brand’s corporate X account, franchise-partner same-store sales are up more than 19 percent so far in Q4 as well, building off 17 percent from last year. It’s been a hot comps run for Steak ‘n Shake. Same-store sales rose 11.9 percent in Q2 and 14 percent across the first half of the year. It began fiscal 2026 with comps of 10 percent and posted its best calendar run in 2025 since 1992 . Q3 revenue was $74.7 million, up from $69.15 million, year-over-year. Over the first nine months of the year, it’s $210.6 million compared to $200.3 million. Central to the brand’s redirect has been a nod toward higher-quality ingredients. Namely, grass-fed beef and tallow instead of seed oils. That reflected in Q3 results as the cost of food at company-owned units was $15.786 million, or 33.6 percent of net sales versus $14.849 million (31.3 percent of net sales), year-over-year. For a nine-months comparison, the numbers were $43.654 million (32.8 percent) and $41.480 million (30.5 percent), respectively. Steak ‘n Shake said the increase was “primarily because of [the company] materially enhancing the quality of its food ingredients.” This effort began in March 2025 when the brand announced a switch to tallow from seed oils (tots included). Grade A Wisconsin butter, A2 whole milk, cane-sugar bottled soft drinks (August), and the elimination of microwaves (February) followed. In September, Steak ‘n Shake added crinkle-cut fries (also cooked in tallow), allowing customers the opportunity to swap for shoestring. Late August, it claimed to be the first major fast-food chain making buns seed oil-free. Starting October 5, Steak ‘n Shake buns became “unapologetically drenched in pure Grade AA Wisconsin butter,” the company said. In June, Steak ‘n Shake progressed to beef from pasture-raised cattle, stating the product would be 100 percent grass-fed and finished, “making us the only American burger joint serving the healthiest kind of beef.” Steak ‘n Shake previously required suppliers to meet a certain list of standards, such as humane treatment of cattle, no added hormones, and no animal by-products in feed, but didn’t require grass-fed. Carl’s Jr. once had an “All-Natural Burger” in 2014–2015 that was grass-fed, free-range beef and marketed as the first such offering at scale. It was later discontinued. articles.title: Senado aprova R$ 22,6 bilhões em crédito para empresas afetadas pelo tarifaço dos EUA
articles.titleKo: Senado aprova R$ 22,6 bilhões em crédito para empresas afetadas pelo tarifaço dos EUA
articles.originalSummary: O Senado aprovou nesta terça-feira, 17, o projeto resultante da Medida Provisória (MP) 1.379/2026, para criar linhas de crédito no total de R$ 22,6 bilhões, com juros subsidiados, para empresas afetadas pela sobretaxação dos Estados Unidos a produtos brasileiros. O texto segue para sanção. A MP tem validade até a quarta-feira, 18. O texto permite a combinação dos recursos da União com recursos próprios do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES). Pelo previsto, R$ 13,5 bilhões vêm do Tesouro Nacional e R$ 9,1 bilhões, do BNDES . A proposta reforça o Plano Brasil Soberano, criado para apoiar empresas afetadas por barreiras comerciais internacionais, tarifas e instabilidades geopolíticas. A ampliação dos recursos deve beneficiar exportadores de produtos industriais, agropecuários, florestais, pesqueiros, aquícolas e minerais, além de seus fornecedores. Inicialmente, o BNDES previa dispor de R$ 5 bilhões. Em setembro, no entanto, o banco ampliou sua participação no Plano Brasil Soberano 3 para R$ 9,1 bilhões. Com os recursos adicionais, o orçamento final do plano de apoio passou dos R$ 18,5 bilhões estimados inicialmente para R$ 22,6 bilhões. Do total de recursos, R$ 8,8 bilhões serão destinados a exportadores e fornecedores afetados pela aplicação de tarifas comerciais pelos Estados Unidos. Outros R$ 6,8 bilhões serão destinados aos beneficiários exportadores e seus fornecedores que exportam para países do Golfo Pérsico, região afetada pelo conflito no Oriente Médio. Os R$ 7 bilhões restantes serão distribuídos da seguinte forma: R$ 1 bilhão para empresas atuantes em setores industriais relevantes ao comércio exterior brasileiro; R$ 4 bilhões para empresas atuantes em atividades relacionadas à fabricação de adubos e fertilizantes ou de intermediários para fertilizantes; R$ 2 bilhões para empresas atuantes em atividades industriais e tecnológicas na cadeia de minerais críticos e estratégicos. articles.title: Liv Up cria linha de pratos de baixa caloria para usuários de canetas emagrecedoras
articles.titleKo: Liv Up cria linha de pratos de baixa caloria para usuários de canetas emagrecedoras
articles.originalSummary: A Liv Up lançou kits de refeições de baixa caloria voltados a consumidores que utilizam GLP-1, as chamadas canetas emagrecedors. Com pratos de até 390 calorias por R$ 17,99 por unidade, a novidade reúne opções congeladas e prontas para aquecer. O portfólio inclui opções como almôndegas de frango com arroz de sete grãos e mix de legumes, estrogonofe de frango com arroz de sete grãos e brócolis, frango oriental com arroz, brócolis e abóbora e yakisoba de frango com legumes. A composição pode variar conforme a disponibilidade de estoque em cada região. “O que vemos é que esse consumidor não está simplesmente procurando comer menos. Ele passa a prestar mais atenção na qualidade e na composição do que come”, afirma Victor Santos, CEO e cofundador da Liv Up. O lançamento acompanha a expansão do uso de medicamentos à base de GLP-1 no Brasil e as mudanças de hábitos associadas aos tratamentos. Pesquisa do Instituto Locomotiva aponta que 33% dos domicílios brasileiros tinham ao menos um morador que usa ou já usou canetas emagrecedoras em fevereiro de 2026. Como esses medicamentos reduzem o apetite, a composição nutricional dos alimentos e a escolha de refeições equilibradas ganham atenção. Os dados da empresa também mostram o avanço desse comportamento entre seus clientes. Há um ano, 6% dos consumidores da Liv Up declaravam já ter usado medicamentos à base de GLP-1. O percentual subiu para 8% há seis meses e chegou a 14% atualmente, mais que o dobro do registrado em 12 meses. Marca abre dark store em João Pessoa A Liv Up inaugurou uma dark store em João Pessoa (PB), ampliando sua operação no Nordeste. A foodtech prevê abrir novas unidades em Niterói (RJ) e Blumenau (SC) nos próximos meses e tem como meta alcançar faturamento de R$ 450 milhões em 2026. A empresa também prevê a inauguração de mais quatro centros de distribuição na região. Além de chegar a novos municípios, a companhia planeja ampliar o catálogo de produtos no e-commerce, expandir a atuação no varejo e conquistar clientes B2B com a marca “Generosa”. A linha foi criada para fornecer refeições equilibradas a equipes operacionais de redes de alimentação e franquias. Entre as empresas que utilizam os produtos estão Burger King, Subway e Bob’s. A iniciativa marcou a entrada da Liv Up no segmento de foodservice. PepsiCo is expanding DRIPS by Pepsi, its crafted beverage platform, with the launch of a proprietary syrup lineup and concentrated bases. Introducing DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes, the first standalone syrups innovation from PepsiCo designed for scalability and menu versatility, and Concentrated Bases to simplify beverage creation. DRIPS by Pepsi® Signature Mixes offer flavors developed from two years of consumer learning and in-market feedback, along with proven recipes that operators can easily add to their menus. Giving Restaurant Operators More Ways to Create Each DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mix combines multiple flavor notes in a single pump with no added sugar, colors, or artificial preservatives. The syrups are the first to be designed exclusively for the crafted beverage category to help operators bring bold creations to life with less complexity behind the counter, making it easier to move at the speed of culture. The innovative syrups are designed to amplify, not compete with, existing beverage formats and flavor profiles, making it easier to create high-value crafted beverages, from dirty sodas and refreshers to flavor-packed twists on classic favorites. The DRIPS by Pepsi platform is also expanding to include concentrated bases, starting with Lipton® Green Tea flavor, with more to come in 2027. The bases are designed to mix with still or sparkling water, giving operators flexibility to create premium refreshers without expensive, space-consuming equipment. The launches build on the momentum of DRIPS by Pepsi, which since 2024 has tested recipes and met the trend through high-traffic pop-ups, activations, and partnerships across the country. Those real-world learnings helped shape the syrup lineup and the handcrafted beverage recipes behind them. The result is a new way for operators to differentiate their menus, meet consumer demand for a premium product, encourage repeat visits, and stay connected to evolving beverage trends. “The future of beverages isn’t just about what goes into the cup. It’s about creating experiences consumers can’t find everywhere else. DRIPS by Pepsi is an end-to-end platform built on consumer insights, trend forecasting, proprietary recipes, operational resources, and marketing tools that help operators of all size and scale bring crafted beverage programs to life. These syrups are the latest extension of that platform, making it easier for restaurant teams to create customized, handcrafted beverages while staying ahead of emerging consumer trends. Our goal is to simplify innovation so operators can focus on delivering memorable experiences and driving growth,” said Scott Finlow, Chief Marketing Officer, PepsiCo Away From Home. The real fun starts when the Signature Mixes meet PepsiCo’s beverage portfolio Whether paired with PEPSI, MOUNTAIN DEW, STARRY, MUG Root Beer or poppi , the DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes can transform beloved brands into something entirely new. Built for everything from dirty sodas and refreshers to emerging energy-forward beverages, the platform gives operators room to experiment, innovate and create one-of-a-kind experiences for consumers with more than 100+ different recipes to choose from. And with countless combinations still unexplored, the next fan favorite may be just one pour away. Five Distinct DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes. Unlimited Possibilities. The five DRIPS by Pepsi Signature Mixes were developed to help operators unlock more beverage possibilities with fewer ingredients and no added sugar, colors, or artificial preservatives. Each syrup delivers multiple layered flavor notes in a single pump, providing versatile options that make it easier to scale and expand beverage menus without overhauling inventory. articles.title: Donatos Partners with Eulerity to Automate Local Marketing Across Every Restaurant
articles.titleKo: Donatos Partners with Eulerity to Automate Local Marketing Across Every Restaurant
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Donatos Pizza today announced a partnership with Eulerity, the AI-powered marketing automation platform built for multi-location brands, to bring its local digital marketing in-house and automate it across every restaurant. The move extends Donatos decades-long commitment to automation from the kitchen to its marketing, replacing fragmented digital media workflows with one automated system that runs paid media across Search, Social, Display, Video and connected TV (CTV). The partnership was unveiled on the main stage at the Donatos Franchise Conference in Columbus, Ohio, where the team outlined how Donatos will run a unified brand strategy while giving each local market the flexibility to compete in its own neighborhood. Automation from the kitchen to local marketing From its first pepperoni machine to today’s robot-assisted pizza kitchen, Donatos has a long history of putting automation to work where machines do the job best. Eulerity takes the same approach to marketing, freeing corporate marketing teams to focus on strategy while the platform handles the operational tasks better managed by systems. Across hundreds of locations, those tasks add up. Teams manage six to ten advertising platforms, data sits in disconnected systems, and agency workflows can delay campaign changes by one to two weeks. With Eulerity, Donatos sees every dollar, every market and every result in one place, and can adjust campaigns the same day. “We’ve always relied on automation to free up our team for higher-value work, and the most important of that work is the guest experience. Marketing is the next step. With Eulerity, our local marketing runs with omnichannel automation in every market, so our people can spend less time managing ad platforms and more time on strategy and on our guests,” Jodie Conrad, Chief Marketing Officer, Donatos Pizza. Putting Donatos’ own data to work Donatos will use its own first-party data to direct local advertising more precisely through three capabilities: First-Party Audience Engagement : Reconnect with existing Donatos guests through personalized marketing that drives loyalty and repeat visits. Intelligent Retargeting : Re-engage consumers who have interacted with Donatos across digital channels, keeping the brand top of mind. Lookalike Audience Expansion : Identify and reach new local customers who share characteristics with Donatos’ most valuable guests. Eulerity layers these signals with neighborhood-level targeting and geofencing, and its geo-location reporting flags coverage gaps so local media can fill them automatically. One brand standard, more working media Eulerity’s campaign blueprints give Donatos a consistent foundation across every location, while each market tailors its media plan to its own objectives and budget. Applied consistently, those local budgets stop acting like hundreds of small, disconnected buys and start behaving like a single national one, unlocking better optimization, pricing and broader reach. “The strongest restaurant brands own their marketing, their data and their results, and that’s exactly what Donatos is doing. Our job is to make that simple. We give corporate one standard to build on and give every Donatos market the tools to win locally,” said Adam Chandler, COO and Co-Founder of Eulerity. With the holidays upon us, Stoney River is more prepared than ever to deliver unforgettable dining experiences. Today’s diners want every night out to feel like an occasion, and Stoney River – the steakhouse known for its hand-cut steaks, fresh seafood and signature house specialties, bringing a fine-dining experience at an accessible price point – has reimagined every plate to deliver just that. The revamped menu lineup arrives at all locations Nov. 12, giving classic favorites a refined twist and adding starters, surf-and-turf pairings and shareable “For the Table” sides. Before anything changed, the team studied the fine-dining and upscale-casual competitive landscape and tested each dish in four restaurants. Only the improvements that would truly wow guests and keep the experience approachable moved forward. The work began, appropriately, with the star of the show: Prime Beef. Certified Angus Beef Prime must clear USDA Prime marbling requirements plus nine additional specifications, and only Black Angus cattle qualify. Stoney River has long sourced from the Midwest, where cold winters keep herds eating more, and chefs can taste the difference. In fact, Certified Angus Beef Prime represents the top 3% of beef, making it a relatively rare offering in restaurants and an obvious choice for a kitchen determined to stand apart. Filet Mignon stands proudly on its own, whether made with Stoney River’s own coffee-cured blend or served as a Center Cut in petite or regular portions. Then there’s the best of both worlds, where tender Filet Medallions meet their match in a crab cake, broiled lobster or Oscar-style crab for a land-and-sea romance meant to be lingered over. From there, attention moved outward. Shrimp got bigger, the catch got better and even the table settings received an upgrade that feels upscale yet approachable. The fryers switched to beef tallow for potatoes, giving the Parmesan Truffle Fries a crisper edge and a deeper, more savory finish. The comprehensive refresh carries through the rest of the meal: Starters: An expanded appetizer lineup includes the Grilled Seafood Platter, Jumbo Shrimp Cocktail and Crab Stuffed Mushrooms. Soups and salads: Four featured salads, including The Wedge, Steak Salad, House Salad and Classic Caesar Salad, served with house-made dressings, alongside French Onion Soup and New England Lobster Bisque. Prime may lead the way, but the rest of the menu stays deliberately balanced and accessible. Prices range from about $19 for a burger, $30 for a pasta and $50 for a steak, with Steak and Biscuits near $25. articles.title: TikTok Shop já é opção de compra para 22% dos consumidores e entra no top 3 do e-commerce
articles.titleKo: TikTok Shop já é opção de compra para 22% dos consumidores e entra no top 3 do e-commerce
articles.originalSummary: O TikTok Shop aparece como a terceira plataforma mais citada por compradores online às vésperas da Black Friday. Na pesquisa da Worldpanel by Numerator, 22% dos entrevistados afirmaram ter comprado pelo aplicativo nos últimos 30 dias. O índice coloca a rede atrás apenas da Shopee , com 79%, e do Mercado Livre, com 41%. A plataforma supera a Shein, citada por 20% dos compradores, e a Amazon, por 16%. Os resultados refletem apenas as respostas dos participantes da pesquisa e não podem ser generalizados para a população brasileira. A pesquisa mostra ainda que os participantes compram em diferentes plataformas. Em média, cada consumidor on-line citou 2,2 plataformas utilizadas nos últimos 30 dias. “Os participantes relataram compras em mais de uma plataforma, mostrando que diferentes empresas fazem parte da rotina de um mesmo consumidor. Nesse grupo, o TikTok Shop aparece entre as três opções mais citadas, ao lado de plataformas já consolidadas no comércio eletrônico”, analisa Daniel Horai, diretor da Worldpanel by Numerator. Compradores frequentes lideram pedidos online O levantamento também mostra a frequência de compras entre os participantes. Dos 1.804 entrevistados que souberam informar quantas compras on-line fizeram nos últimos 30 dias, a média foi de 3,7 no período. Os consumidores que fizeram cinco compras ou mais representaram 28% desse grupo, mas responderam por 55% do total de compras declaradas. O percentual se refere à quantidade de pedidos, não aos valores gastos, e mostra a participação dos compradores mais frequentes no volume registrado pela pesquisa. articles.title: Chef Melba Wilson to Give Away 1,000 Thanksgiving Turkeys in Harlem

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chef Melba Wilson, celebrated restaurateur, community leader, and owner of Melba’s Restaurant in Harlem, is once again bringing the community together for her annual Thanksgiving Giveaway on Monday, November 23, continuing her longstanding commitment to supporting local children and families during the holiday season. This year’s initiative will provide approximately 1,000 Thanksgiving turkeys to individuals and families. Taking place at Melba’s Restaurant (300 West 114th Street), this year’s initiative will bring together Bank of America, Timberland, recording artist, fashion designer and entrepreneur FERG, God’s Love We Deliver, and Wollman Rink to help make the holiday season a little brighter for the community. Beginning at 5 p.m., Melba’s will host its annual public Thanksgiving Turkey Giveaway, distributing free turkeys to community members and families until 7 p.m. This year’s turkeys have been generously underwritten by Bank of America, helping Melba’s continue its tradition of giving back to the community it serves. Earlier in the day, Melba and her partners will also host a private holiday distribution for select students from PS 161 and the Wadleigh Secondary School for the Performing & Visual Arts, continuing their collective commitment to supporting local children and families. FERG is also expected to participate in the day’s festivities. “Food is not a luxury, it’s a necessity,” said Melba Wilson. “For way too many families, putting a meal on the table is a daily challenge and the holiday season can make those struggles even more difficult. No family should ever have to worry about where their next meal is coming from, especially during a time of year centered on gratitude, family, and togetherness. I feel that it is our responsibility to show up for our communities in meaningful ways. Through our annual Thanksgiving Turkey Giveaway, we are doing a small part to make sure more families can enjoy a wonderful Thanksgiving meal because at the end of the day, taking care of one another, is what community truly is all about.” “Melba has a wonderful way of bringing people together and reminding us what it means to show up for one another, especially during the holidays,” said Connie Verducci, Market Executive, Bank of America New York City. “We’re grateful to have worked alongside her on so many efforts close to her heart, and proud to once again come together to help make Thanksgiving special for local families.” “Timberland was born in New England, but we were raised in New York City—it’s our second home,” said Nina Flood, global brand president for Timberland. “We are honored to partner with Melba’s to support the young people of Harlem as we head into the holiday season. Because nothing is more powerful than coming together to build strong communities.” “Melba’s unwavering dedication to uplifting the community perfectly aligns with our mission to make ice skating at Wollman Rink an accessible, welcoming activity for everyone, and we are honored to support their vital work during this special time of year,” said Stacy Shuster, VP of Business Development and Community Impact at Wollman Rink. “Harlem is the village I come from and it always feels good to be able to help whenever I can,” said FERG. The annual giveaway reflects Melba’s longstanding dedication to community engagement and addressing food insecurity throughout New York City. Through her restaurant and ongoing community initiatives, Wilson has consistently worked to support families, provide meals for children, and create opportunities to give back to the Harlem neighborhood she calls home. articles.title: La Morocha, First U.S. Concept from Chef David Castro Hussong, Opens in L.A.’s Arts District
articles.titleKo: La Morocha, First U.S. Concept from Chef David Castro Hussong, Opens in L.A.’s Arts District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . From the group behind award-winning Los Angeles concepts Mírate and Daisy Margarita Bar as well as the recently opened Gilbert Pérez Bar comes La Morocha, the newest addition to the Arts District, opening Thursday, November 19. A reimagined Los Angeles outpost of the original Ensenada restaurant, La Morocha marks the first U.S. concept from acclaimed Chef David Castro Hussong, whose culinary experience spans celebrated destinations including Blue Hill at Stone Barns, Eleven Madison Park, Cala and Valle de Guadalupe’s Fauna, named Best Restaurant in Mexico and recognized on both Latin America’s and The World’s 50 Best Restaurants lists. It also marks Castro Hussong’s first creative collaboration with restaurateur Matt Egan, a leading force in Los Angeles’ contemporary Mexican dining scene, alongside the group’s key collaborators Randy Evans and Brian Kang. Merging the group’s agave-driven approach and Castro Hussong’s deep Baja roots, the restaurant will serve wood-fired Baja comfort food complemented by Mexican-inspired cocktails and a global wine and spirits program. A TASTE OF ENSENADA IN DTLA On the menu at La Morocha is an assortment of approachable and shareable plates, each inspired by the places where Chef Castro Hussong grew up and the foods he enjoys eating at home. While guests can order popular mainstay dishes from the original Ensenada concept, like its famed Chile Relleno tacos with rockfish, capers, costra de queso, and a flour tortilla, most of the menu is exclusive to Los Angeles and tailored to the local palate. The raw bar draws on the fresh seafood Ensenada is known for, including oysters, ceviches, crudos, and a perfectly spicy Aguachile Rojo made with scallops, chiltepin, jicama, and cucumber. Chef Castro Hussong’s answer to Los Angeles’s fusion pizza conversation is the “Picza,” a playful, Spanish-spelled riff on pizza that lands somewhere between a pie and a tostada, with a golden base and generous toppings. Additional highlights from La Morocha’s list of starters, tacos, and large entrees include: Baja Fish Taco with fried rockfish, salsa verde, chipotle aioli, and corn tortilla Ribeye Taco with grilled steak, salsa toreada, and costra de queso on a flour tortilla Pizca de Cangrejo featuring fresh, sweet crab, beurre blanc, chives and lemon Picza de Flor de Calabaza with squash blossoms, pomodoro, and queso Pescado en Adobo with pasilla mixe adobo, black beans, rice, and flour tortillas Eggplant Milanesa with chile morita, pomodoro, and Monterey cheese Rounding out La Morocha’s menu are desserts thoughtfully developed by celebrated pastry chef Maribel Aldaco Silva, Chef Castro Hussong’s wife and the recipient of Latin America’s Best Pastry Chef award in 2023. The menu features Pixtle Cheesecake; Coffee Churro with coffee ganache, vanilla and coffee ice cream;Mexican Cinnamon Macaroon with chocolate cream, chocolate crisp, and plantain ice cream; and a refreshing Mango and Passion Fruit Sorbet finished with coconut granita and coconut flake. COCKTAILS TO COMPLEMENT Led by Bar Manager Marcos Pulido, who trained under Max Reis at Daisy Margarita Bar, La Morocha’s beverage program celebrates vibrant Mediterranean and Baja flavors, focusing on fresh ingredients, wood-fired aromas, and beach sips. Think ingredients like roasted carrots and pineapple, prickly pear, nixtamal corn, hoja santo, and guava. Standouts include the Zona Centro with watermelon, strawberry, guava, aloe, orange licor and tequila; Reina Querida built on prickly pear, canela y jamaica tea, champagne foam, and mezcal; and La Cura with chile y nogave, ginger, lemon, and reposado tequila. SPOTLIGHT ON MEXICAN WINE Curated by sommelier Felicia Chavez, La Morocha’s wine list centers around the diversity of Mexican winemaking, with a focus on Valle de Guadalupe and other notable regions, alongside classic California selections

articles.title: Nestlé lança espelho com IA que analisa saúde para impulsionar venda de suplementos
articles.titleKo: Nestlé lança espelho com IA que analisa saúde para impulsionar venda de suplementos
articles.originalSummary: A Nestlé lançou o Espelho do Bem-Estar, equipamento que faz leitura facial em 30 segundos para apresentar indicadores de saúde e nutrição. A tecnologia estreia em Fortaleza em parceria com a Pague Menos, enquanto uma versão para iPad chega a farmácias de Salvador e São Paulo. Com a iniciativa, a fabricante projeta dobrar as vendas de suplementos proteicos, vitaminas e minerais nas lojas participantes. Por meio de uma câmera integrada, a tecnologia combina visão computacional e Inteligência Artificial para identificar pequenas variações visuais provocadas pela circulação sanguínea em regiões específicas do rosto. O sistema foi desenvolvido com base na análise de imagens faciais de mais de 60 mil pessoas, sob supervisão de profissionais de saúde. O sistema estima parâmetros como frequências cardíaca e respiratória, nível de estresse, equilíbrio emocional, idade aparente da pele e índices de composição corporal. O processamento é realizado de forma protegida, e os resultados são apresentados de maneira confidencial na tela do celular do usuário. Espelho do Bem-Estar Nas farmácias, estudantes de nutrição acompanham a experiência, explicam os resultados aos consumidores e, com o apoio de profissionais de saúde, identificam necessidades individuais e indicam produtos da Nestlé. O atendimento pode ter continuidade no ambiente digital, por meio da Nina, assistente virtual de Inteligência Artificial desenvolvida pela equipe da Nestlé e treinada por médicos, nutricionistas e outros especialistas, conforme a legislação local. A ferramenta oferece informações sobre hábitos, alimentação e bem-estar, além de orientações sobre soluções nutricionais. O lançamento ocorre em meio à busca dos consumidores por orientação confiável sobre esses produtos. Segundo pesquisa da consultoria McKinsey, 71% esperam experiências personalizadas durante a jornada de compra. A experiência é gratuita e tem finalidade informativa e educativa. Os indicadores são estimativas e não substituem diagnósticos, exames, avaliações clínicas ou acompanhamento médico. Em 2027, a iniciativa deve chegar a todas as regiões do Brasil, primeiro País da América Latina a receber a solução. O projeto incorpora aprendizados da aplicação da tecnologia em outros mercados onde a Nestlé atua, como Europa, Ásia, Estados Unidos e Canadá.
