Pizza Guys, the Sacramento-based pizza franchise known for its handcrafted specialty pizzas, fresh made dough, and premium ingredients, will celebrate the grand opening of its Newport Beach location on Thursday, Nov. 12, at 3601 Jamboree Rd., Suite 3. The restaurant will be owned and operated by Nader Iskander, who is expanding his business after opening his first Pizza Guys location in Brea in May 2024. Before becoming a Pizza Guys franchisee, Iskander spent years working in a very different industry. Born in Egypt, he moved to Burbank at age 25 and spent years running his own general contracting company. With a longtime passion for cooking, Iskander became interested in Pizza Guys after working with the brand on several construction projects. Impressed by its food quality and innovative restaurant designs, he eventually decided to open his own Pizza Guys restaurant in Brea. “Newport Beach is a community that knows good food, and I’m excited to give them a pizza place they can count on,” said Iskander. “Brea taught me that the real work happens in the details, from making dough fresh every morning to remembering a regular’s usual order. That’s the standard my team and I are bringing to Jamboree Road, and we can’t wait to start serving our new neighbors.” A husband and father of three, Iskander places a high value on family and community. When he opened his Brea restaurant, he chose a location close to home and near a school to better serve local families and students. He hopes to bring that same community-focused approach to Newport Beach. “Nader has shown in Brea exactly what it looks like to run a Pizza Guys the right way, with care for the food, the team and the community,” said Shahpour Nejad, CEO and Founder of Pizza Guys. “We’re excited to see him build on that success with a second location and proud to support him as he brings Pizza Guys to Newport Beach.” To learn more about Pizza Guys Newport Beach and to view their full menu, please visit: pizzaguys.com/location/newport-beach/. The updated concept made its U.S. debut at Captain D’s newest restaurant in San Antonio, Texas. Captain D’s, the nation’s leading fast-casual seafood restaurant, is entering its next phase of growth with the unveiling of a new restaurant design that will begin rolling out in new stores across the country. The updated concept made its U.S. debut at Captain D’s newest restaurant in San Antonio, Texas, giving franchisees and guests a first look at the next generation of the iconic seafood brand. The San Antonio restaurant represents more than the brand’s first location in the market. It showcases a new, more contemporary Captain D’s restaurant, designed to support the company’s continued growth and flexibility across a range of real estate opportunities. With development underway and opportunities emerging in markets including Florida, Ohio, Oklahoma, and Maryland, Captain D’s is looking ahead to where the new design can go next. A New Look Built for Growth The design is a fresh evolution of the Captain D’s experience, combining updated materials and modern design elements while preserving the personality and recognizable identity of the 57-year-old brand. The restaurant features new colors and textures, LED accent lighting, stained concrete floors, and updated backlit exterior signage. The result is a more contemporary and polished environment that gives Captain D’s a refreshed look while maintaining the familiar experience guests know. “We wanted to create a fresh, modern look that reflects where Captain D’s is headed while staying true to who we are,” said Brad Reed, Chief Development Officer for Captain D’s. “It’s more polished and contemporary, but when you walk through the doors, you’ll still recognize Captain D’s. This is an evolution of the brand, not a departure from it.” The San Antonio location also demonstrates the flexibility of the new design in a development setting. Built as an end-cap location with a drive-thru, the restaurant showcases how the updated concept can adapt to different site configurations while delivering a consistent brand experience. The restaurant seats 42 guests and is expected to create approximately 30 to 35 local jobs. San Antonio Marks the Beginning Owned and operated by local franchise partners Ruben Cardenas, Brian Clemens and Dave Peters, the San Antonio restaurant marks the beginning of what the ownership group expects to be a larger presence for Captain D’s in the market. They initially plan to develop three Captain D’s restaurants in the San Antonio area, with plans to eventually grow to as many as 10 locations. “San Antonio is growing tremendously, and we see a real opportunity here,” Cardenas said. “There aren’t a lot of fast seafood options, and we think Captain D’s will be a great addition to the community.” Clemens, who grew up in Florida and has been a longtime Captain D’s fan, was surprised to discover San Antonio did not have a location. That personal connection and knowing the popularity of the brand back home helped inspire the ownership group to bring the brand to his adopted hometown. “I grew up in Florida loving Captain D’s, so when I realized there was an opportunity to bring it to San Antonio, it was an easy decision,” said Clemens. “I’ve missed it and I know people in San Antonio will love the high-quality, generous portions of our hand-battered wild-caught fish from Alaska. Where else can you get a fork and knife meal for $5.99?” A Look at What’s Next While San Antonio provides a first look at how Captain D’s plans to evolve its restaurant footprint, the brand is pursuing rapid domestic and international growth. The new design is already serving as a foundation for future restaurants, giving franchisees a modernized concept that can work across a variety of sites and markets. articles.title: Serasa: demanda das empresas por crédito segue em alta, mas dá sinais de desaceleração
articles.titleKo: Serasa: demanda das empresas por crédito segue em alta, mas dá sinais de desaceleração
articles.originalSummary: A demanda das empresas por crédito começa a dar sinais de arrefecimento, após ter exibido resiliência às restrições provocadas pelo alto nível dos juros. A busca das companhias brasileiras por recursos financeiros cresceu 9,9% no acumulado de 12 meses até setembro, mostra levantamento da Serasa Experian. O movimento foi liderado pelos micro e pequenos negócios (MPEs), com alta de 10%, seguidos de grandes empresas (+8,3%) e médias (+5%). No recorte apenas de setembro, o indicador avançou 0,6% ante igual mês do ano passado. O resultado representa uma forte desaceleração após o avanço de 5,3% em agosto e de 17,6% em julho. “O crescimento também ficou menos disseminado, concentrado em serviços e agropecuária, enquanto comércio e indústria recuaram”, afirma a economista-chefe da Serasa Experian, Camila Abdelmalack. “No entanto, como o indicador apresenta volatilidade e ainda acumula alta de 9,9% em 12 meses, é necessário acompanhar os próximos resultados antes de afirmar uma tendência de desaceleração”, pondera. Entre setores, Serviços liderou a expansão nos 12 meses até setembro, com alta de 15,5%, enquanto Agronegócio subiu 15,1%, Indústria aumentou 6,9% e Comércio teve incremento de 5,6%. No confronto mensal, por outro lado, comércio (-1,4%) e indústria (-3,4%) registraram contração. “A procura por crédito reflete as necessidades de gestão financeira das empresas, mas encontra um mercado mais restritivo, no qual os credores reduzem a exposição ao risco e reforçam os critérios de concessão diante da inadimplência elevada”, ressalta Abdelmalack. Com informação do Estadão de Conteúdo (André Marinho). articles.title: IA muda o ritmo do varejo e exige revisão de processos e controles
articles.titleKo: IA muda o ritmo do varejo e exige revisão de processos e controles
articles.originalSummary: A adoção da Inteligência Artificial no varejo não precisa esperar que as empresas concluam grandes projetos de organização de dados. O caminho passa por começar com aplicações de impacto mensurável, não necessariamente em todas as áreas de uma só vez, testar soluções em ambientes controlados e estabelecer mecanismos de segurança proporcionais aos riscos de cada operação. Essas foram algumas das conclusões após mais uma edição do Quando os Líderes se Encontram, realizada na terça-feira, 10, pela Gouvêa Consulting e Gouvêa Experience, com oferecimento da Kyndryl em parceria com a Google Cloud e a SAP. O evento reuniu executivos do varejo, da indústria e de empresas de tecnologia em dois painéis que discutiram como transformar a experimentação com IA em resultados para o negócio e, ao mesmo tempo, evitar que a expansão das aplicações comprometa a segurança, os custos e a confiabilidade das decisões. Como sair da experimentação e gerar resultado No painel “Da experimentação ao impacto: IA, aplicações e a modernização do varejo”, os participantes defenderam que a escolha dos projetos deve partir das necessidades da operação. O debate envolveu aplicações para aumentar vendas, melhorar margens, reduzir rupturas de estoque e acelerar processos, mas também a dificuldade de transformar ganhos individuais de produtividade em resultados para toda a empresa. Para Ricardo Nastri, vice-presidente de Consultoria da Kyndryl Brasil, a adoção da IA pode combinar iniciativas de resultado mais imediato com projetos de transformação de maior alcance. “O projeto de eficiência ajuda, às vezes, a financiar o projeto de transformação”, afirmou. Essa dinâmica também aparece no Estudo de Modernização 2026 da Kyndryl : entre as empresas de varejo, 50% afirmam reinvestir economias obtidas com a otimização dos custos de nuvem em novas iniciativas de inovação, como IA e novas aplicações, e 47% direcionam esses recursos para outros projetos de modernização. Segundo o executivo, as aplicações menores também contribuem para o aprendizado das equipes e para a criação das condições necessárias à expansão da tecnologia. Ellen Bremm, vice-presidente de Varejo da SAP Brasil, destacou a importância de estabelecer critérios para os investimentos. “Os projetos deveriam ser escolhidos ou priorizados de acordo com o KPI que é relevante para o varejo”, afirmou. A revisão dos processos também apareceu como condição para ampliar os resultados. Rafael Sbampato, diretor de Digital e TI da Riachuelo, chamou a atenção para o fato de que acelerar uma tarefa não significa necessariamente acelerar toda a operação. “Se eu fizesse a peça em 30 segundos e esperasse três meses, eu teria esperado três meses”, exemplificou, ao abordar os desafios do desenvolvimento de produtos. Na MBRF, Marcelo Suárez, diretor de Trade Marketing, Vendas Digitais e Experiência do Cliente, defendeu que o potencial da tecnologia deve ser avaliado também pela capacidade de gerar receita. “Eu prefiro que os 3.500 vendedores que a gente tem vendam mais”, disse, ao comentar a utilização de dados para aprimorar as decisões comerciais. O debate contou ainda com Gutemberg Almeida, industry advisor do Google Cloud, que abordou a importância de estruturar os dados, integrar sistemas e estabelecer controles para que as ferramentas possam atuar nos processos corporativos. Como ampliar a IA sem aumentar os riscos O segundo eixo do encontro tratou de um desafio que ganha relevância à medida que as ferramentas deixam de apenas fornecer informações e passam a executar ações dentro das empresas. No painel “Inovar com confiança: como escalar a IA sem ampliar os riscos?”, os participantes discutiram como conciliar a velocidade exigida pelas áreas de negócios com a proteção dos dados, a gestão dos custos e o monitoramento das decisões automatizadas. Roberto Wajnsztok, sócio-diretor da Gouvêa Consulting, destacou a urgência que caracteriza o setor. “O varejista quer aplicar amanhã, porque precisa bater a meta amanhã”, afirmou

articles.title: KFC and Taco Bell Franchisee Tasty Chick’n Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: KFC and Taco Bell Franchisee Tasty Chick’n Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Tasty Chick’n was formed in 2021. Tasty Chick’n, which operates 84 KFC and KFC/Taco Bell restaurants across 10 states, filed for bankruptcy in Houston on Monday. CEO Thomas M. Scott said the company filed to protect the value of its restaurants and to run a court-supervised sale of its assets. It will also look at other ways to restructure on its own, he said. The company runs 75 KFC restaurants and nine KFC/Taco Bell co-branded locations. Florida has the most, with 23, followed by Tennessee with 22. The others are in Virginia, Arkansas, Kentucky, Illinois, Missouri, Alabama, Mississippi and Indiana. Tasty Chick’n was formed in 2021 and built its business through two large purchases. It bought 90 restaurants from Fowler Foods that year and 64 more from JRN, Inc. in 2024. Scott said sales have fallen each year since then. They dropped 11.4 percent in 2024 and 1.4 percent in 2025, and are down another 2.8 percent so far this year, a decline of about 15.6 percent over three years. Meanwhile, food, labor, operating and rent costs rose. The company said its restaurant profit margin shrank from 11.8 percent in 2023 to 4 percent this year, and store-level earnings over the past 12 months fell to about $7.1 million from $12.4 million the year before. As money got tight, Tasty Chick’n began putting off royalty payments to Yum! Brands in mid-2025. It mostly stopped paying them altogether in November 2025. Yum! sent a default notice that December. On September 15, it sent a notice of intent to terminate the franchise agreements, saying Tasty Chick’n owes $15.68 million. Most of that is $7.9 million in advertising contributions and $5.6 million in royalties. Yum! also said the company broke the franchise agreement’s financial reporting rules. Losing the franchise agreements would end the company’s right to use the KFC and Taco Bell names. Scott said that would wipe out the value of the business. It would also put the company in default on its bank loan. That loan is another weight. Tasty Chick’n owes its lenders, led by MidCap Financial Trust, about $67.2 million. It also owes $5 million on a note to JRN. Scott said the company has been talking with both MidCap and Yum! for more than a year but could not get a deal with either, leaving it “caught between” the two. He said the company still hopes for an agreement with both sides. Landlords are also suing. The company faces about 14 real estate lawsuits in Illinois, Florida, Kentucky, Tennessee and Virginia, mostly over unpaid rent, including at stores it has closed or is closing. The suits seek more than $2 million in total. The largest, over a restaurant in Robinson, Illinois, seeks about $1.8 million. Filing for bankruptcy automatically pauses those cases. Nine franchise agreements, tied to closed or closing stores, are being rejected as part of the case, and the company is asking to walk away from the related leases. Another 37 restaurants face remodel or upgrade requirements through 2029, which Scott said add to the company’s costs. The company has hired Guideboat Advisors and Peak Franchise Capital to find buyers. Outreach began in July, and a formal sale process started in October. Tasty Chick’n is marketing the restaurants as one package, market by market, or in combinations, and plans to ask the court to approve bidding rules. Any sale would need court approval and KFC’s consent. Tasty Chick’n employs about 1,646 people. It had about $3.1 million in cash when it filed, and its annual revenue for the year through September was about $194 million. Separate filings show it is asking for a $20 million loan from MidCap to keep operating during the case. articles.title: Durigan defende alíquota da reforma e estima média efetiva de 8,5%
articles.titleKo: Durigan defende alíquota da reforma e estima média efetiva de 8,5%
articles.originalSummary: O ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan , afirmou que a reforma tributária trará ganhos permanentes de responsabilidade fiscal, justiça social e transparência ao sistema tributário brasileiro. Ao defender o modelo aprovado, o ministro reiterou que a alíquota máxima estimada para o novo sistema é de 11,3%, mas que a carga efetiva média deverá ficar em 8,5%, enquanto setores beneficiados por regimes diferenciados e parte da população terão tributação menor ou zerada. As declarações foram feitas nesta terça-feira, 17, durante audiência na Comissão de Assuntos Econômicos (CAE) do Senado destinada a discutir a reforma tributária e a metodologia de cálculo da alíquota dos novos tributos sobre o consumo. Segundo Durigan, um dos principais avanços do novo sistema será tornar mais transparente o custo das renúncias fiscais. Pela sistemática aprovada, a concessão de novos benefícios tributários terá impacto direto na alíquota dos tributos sobre o consumo, permitindo que a sociedade e os agentes públicos conheçam os efeitos de cada decisão. “Quando for pautada uma renúncia fiscal, a conta vai ser apresentada de plano. A decisão vai ser inteira”, disse o ministro. Ele ressaltou que a medida permitirá avaliar de forma mais clara os custos de incentivos tributários e os impactos dessas decisões sobre os demais contribuintes. Caráter social Durigan destacou ainda o caráter social da reforma. Entre as medidas citadas estão a tributação zero da cesta básica, o cashback para famílias inscritas no Cadastro Único, além da redução ou isenção de tributos sobre medicamentos, vacinas, itens de saúde da mulher e outros produtos considerados essenciais. Na avaliação dele, a reforma amplia a progressividade do sistema tributário ao reduzir a carga sobre bens essenciais e devolver parte dos tributos pagos por famílias de menor renda. Alíquota efetiva de 8,5% Ao tratar das estimativas para o novo sistema, o ministro voltou a defender os percentuais divulgados pelo governo e pelo Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU). Ele reiterou que os 11,3% divulgados correspondem à alíquota máxima de referência, aplicável aos contribuintes que não se enquadram em qualquer regime favorecido. Segundo ele, a alíquota efetiva média deverá ficar em 8,5%, em razão das reduções previstas para diversos setores da economia, dos regimes diferenciados e das devoluções de tributos para famílias de baixa renda. “11,3% é a alíquota máxima. Quem tem qualquer regime diferenciado, qualquer redução, vai pagar menos. As pessoas mais pobres vão pagar zero. A alíquota média, é de 8,5%.” Revisão anual O ministro acrescentou que a alíquota será revisada anualmente. Pela sistemática aprovada, a Receita Federal fornecerá os dados ao TCU, responsável por aplicar a metodologia prevista na legislação e subsidiar a definição dos percentuais para os anos seguintes. “Isso vai ter uma revisão todo ano. A alíquota está alta? Ótimo, vamos revisitar.” Segundo o ministro, o mecanismo permitirá ajustar benefícios, regimes diferenciados e outros parâmetros do sistema sempre que houver necessidade de recalibrar a alíquota. Responsabilidade Durigan também afirmou que a reforma exigirá responsabilidade fiscal dos três Poderes. Segundo ele, novas isenções aprovadas pelo Legislativo ou decisões judiciais que ampliem benefícios tributários poderão elevar a alíquota geral do Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (IVA) para compensar a perda de arrecadação. “Não há mágica na economia. Nós vamos ter que ser responsáveis todos, inclusive o Supremo, inclusive o Judiciário, porque a conta vai vir.” Entenda A Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), tributo federal criado na reforma tributária, substituirá o PIS/Pasep e a Cofins a partir de 2027. Ao lado do Imposto sobre Bens e Serviços (IBS), de competência estadual e municipal, formará o novo modelo de Imposto sobre Valor Agregado (IVA) dual do País. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Gyro Project, a fast-fine Greek restaurant bringing authentic street food flavors to a modern setting, will celebrate the opening of its newest New York City location at 107 East 14th Street in Manhattan’s Union Square neighborhood on Thursday, December 3 at 11am with an official Ribbon Cutting Ceremony. The opening marks another milestone in the brand’s continued expansion throughout New York City, bringing its signature Greek flavors and approachable dining experience to one of Manhattan’s busiest shopping, dining and cultural destinations. Located just steps from Union Square, the approximately 600-square-foot restaurant will feature 16 indoor seats and offer The Gyro Project’s signature menu for dine-in, takeout and delivery. Open daily from 10am to 2am, the new location will bring the brand’s fast-fine Greek offerings to the neighborhood throughout the day and late into the night, serving as a convenient destination for nearby residents, students, professionals and late-night diners. The thoughtfully designed interior will blend warm wood finishes with custom-designed wallpaper, neutral wall tiles and woven chairs, creating a welcoming, contemporary atmosphere that balances natural textures with understated design details. The Union Square location will feature a Build-Your-Own Froyo Bar, serving as The Gyro Project’s third location – including Hell’s Kitchen and Garment District – to provide this offering. Guests can also expect The Gyro Project’s lineup of Greek favorites, including classic gyro pita wraps featuring chicken, pork and lamb & beef; hearty platters served with rice, salad and pita; traditional dips such as tzatziki and hummus, soups including traditional Greek avgolemono; loaded Greek fries; fresh salads; and the brand’s signature Greek frozen yogurt. Founded by childhood friends and restaurateurs George Tenedios and Spiro Kokkosis, The Gyro Project was created to fill a void for high-quality Greek cuisine in New York and New Jersey. Since debuting its first location in Fort Lee, New Jersey, in July 2023, the brand has built a loyal following for its signature pita wraps, mixed grill platters, mezedes, specialty fries, rotisserie chicken and Greek froyo – all rooted in authentic recipes and bold Mediterranean flavors. “We’re excited to bring The Gyro Project to Union Square, a neighborhood that has such an incredible mix of energy, culture and community,” said George Tenedios , co-owner of The Gyro Project and recently appointed Archon of the Ecumenical Patriarchate . “As we continue growing throughout New York City, we’re always looking for ways to make each location feel connected to its surroundings. In this lively neighborhood, our extended hours will allow us to serve guests well beyond the traditional lunch and dinner rush.” The Union Square opening follows the brand’s October 15 debut in Hell’s Kitchen at 600 9th Avenue. The opening also builds on The Gyro Project’s growing Manhattan presence, with restaurants serving neighborhoods including the Upper East Side, Upper West Side, Murray Hill, Midtown East, the Garment District and Hudson Yards. Looking ahead, The Gyro Project plans to continue its New York City expansion with an additional location in the Theatre District at 787 8th Avenue, currently anticipated to open in early 2027. With each new restaurant, the brand continues to bring its fast-fine approach to Greek cuisine to some of the city’s most recognizable neighborhoods and commercial districts. The Gyro Project at 107 East 14th Street, New York, NY, will officially celebrate its grand opening on Thursday, December 3 with a Ribbon Cutting Ceremony beginning at 11am. The restaurant will be open daily from 10am to 2am, serving lunch, dinner and late-night fare. The post The Gyro Project Opening in NYC’s Union Square Neighborhood appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.titleKo: Amazon contrata 12 mil temporários para a Black Friday e abre 3.500 vagas permanentes em SP
articles.originalSummary: A Amazon contratou mais de 12 mil trabalhadores temporários no Brasil para atravessar a Black Friday. A varejista chega ao período de maior demanda do ano com 350 centros logísticos, número que inclui mais de 120 unidades abertas desde a edição anterior da data. A média é de duas novas instalações por semana. O objetivo é sustentar a promessa de entrega rápida nos 100% dos municípios do País. “A Black Friday é o momento em que os clientes de todo o Brasil mais contam com a gente, e esses trabalhadores são as pessoas que tornam possível uma entrega rápida e confiável durante o nosso período de maior movimento”, afirma Mireille Schoenardie, líder de Recursos Humanos para Operações da Amazon no Brasil. As vagas temporárias cobrem o salto de pedidos típico da data, mas existe a possibilidade de efetivação. Em 2026, mais de 5 mil pessoas que entraram como temporárias foram efetivadas. Foi o caso de Yorrana Laura, que entrou na Amazon como temporária durante a Black Friday de 2025 e hoje é Assistente de Processos. “Entrei na Amazon como trabalhadora temporária em recebimentos durante a Black Friday. Poucos meses depois, conquistei uma promoção para assistente de processos. O conselho que dou a quem está chegando agora é manter o comprometimento e o foco: crescer aqui é uma possibilidade real para todos”, afirma. Thiago Bittencourt também começou durante uma Black Friday anterior e hoje atua como embaixador, responsável por acolher e treinar novos trabalhadores. “Cheguei muito nervoso e apreensivo no início, mas fui acolhido por toda a equipe. Além de me efetivar e depois me tornar embaixador para treinar os recém-chegados, a experiência transformou o meu lado pessoal “, afirma Thiago. Mais de 3.500 vagas em São Paulo Fora da leva sazonal, a Amazon abre mais de 3.500 vagas efetivas na Grande São Paulo. O pacote inclui convênio médico e odontológico desde o primeiro dia, plano de progressão salarial, bônus, desconto para funcionários e o Programa de Apoio ao Empregado (PAE). Os candidatos devem ter 18 anos ou mais e podem se inscrever no site . articles.title: Outback Cofounder Tim Gannon on Partnerships, and Lessons Learned Along the Way
articles.titleKo: Outback Cofounder Tim Gannon on Partnerships, and Lessons Learned Along the Way
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Food was always central to Outback's early premise. When Tim Gannon moved to Tampa to join his future Outback Steakhouse partners, he arrived with $37 in his pocket. He had sold his polo saddle for gas money and left a job in New Orleans to pursue an opportunity based around who he’d work with , not for . The original plan was relatively modest: open four restaurants. But in the end, Outback grew to 1,300 units and one of the industry’s true icons was born. In a conversation on QSR Uncut (see full episode below), he reflected on the decisions behind the brand’s growth, from the creation of the most-famous appetizer there is in the Bloomin’ Onion to the importance of ownership, hospitality, and getting the word out when you’re just starting. Here are five leadership lessons from the conversation. 1. Choose partners who bring different strengths Before joining Outback, Gannon says his boss offered to pay off his debts, buy him a home, and give him a financial cushion. The offer was worth about $1 million, but it didn’t include equity. Gannon turned it down. He wanted to build something with partners rather than continue working for someone else. “The key was to make money with someone, not for someone,” he said. In Tampa, he found partners who brought different skills to the venture. Gannon focused on food, while Chris Sullivan and Bob Basham developed approaches to incentives, compensation, and operations. He recalls staying with Basham while getting settled in Tampa. Looking back, Gannon considers those relationships central to Outback’s success. “I can’t tell you how important having the right partners is,” he said. The lesson: Look for partners who share your ambition, complement your skills, and are willing to build something together. 2. Create something distinctive by connecting ideas The Bloomin’ Onion began with curiosity about flavor and presentation. While working in New Orleans, Gannon studied how flavors were combined and watched the city’s chefs at work. Along with colleagues, he explored cookbooks for fresh ideas. One Japanese version showed how onions and other vegetables could be cut into flowers. Gannon took inspiration from the presentation, made it edible, and combined it with New Orleans spices. The result became Outback’s signature appetizer. Gannon says the product’s complexity helped make it difficult to duplicate. The seasoning requires a particular blend, and the size of the onion creates operational challenges: Outback built its kitchens with the equipment needed to prepare it at volume. But the idea itself was also memorable. As Gannon phrased it, an item can become attached to a brand in a way that is difficult to transfer elsewhere. The lesson: Originality doesn’t always mean inventing from nothing. It can come from combining influences in a way customers recognize as your own, and building the operation to deliver it consistently. 3. A good product still needs people to discover it When the first Outback opened, business was slow. Gannon recalls a difficult location, little marketing, and customers who didn’t know what to expect from an Australian-themed steakhouse. When Sullivan asked whether he had gotten the food right, Gannon disagreed. The food wasn’t the setback, he believed. People simply didn’t know the restaurant existed. The team began looking for ways to get the product in front of the community. One early effort involved cooking Bloomin’ Onions outside a local radio DJ’s office and bringing them in fresh for him to try on air. Gannon remembers cooking by flashlight early in the morning. The exposure introduced the restaurant to customers. Gannon also recalls overhearing diners at a nearby pizzeria discussing the appetizer and saying they couldn’t wait to tell their neighbors. That conversation gave him hope Outback could make it. The lesson: Don’t assume a strong prod

articles.title: Your Guests Still Love You. So Why Aren’t They Spending?
articles.titleKo: Your Guests Still Love You. So Why Aren’t They Spending?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Consumers today are affected by the largest credit card debt per household ever experienced. Guests might love your restaurant brand more than ever. They might recommend you to their friends, give you glowing reviews, and rank you above every competitor in your category. And yet, they may be visiting half as often. Restaurant leaders know consumers are feeling the financial squeeze. They’re watching transaction counts, average checks, and visit frequency while trying to determine how much of the decline is economic and how much reflects changing brand preference. Yet the loyalty metrics they rely on don’t always make that distinction clear. It creates a serious challenge for operators trying to understand the performance of their brands. It also deserves consideration when evaluating one of the most influential theories in loyalty research. Loyalty Metrics Aren’t Perfect In a 2011 Harvard Business Review article, Timothy Keiningham and his fellow researchers challenged conventional wisdom in how loyalty is measured and evaluated. The research found that popular loyalty measures, including guest satisfaction and Net Promoter Score (NPS), had surprisingly weak relationships with how consumers allocated their spending in reality. Their alternative, named the Wallet Allocation Rule, demonstrated that a brand’s relative ranking among competitors was substantially more predictive of its share of guest spending. The principle is compelling. Here’s how it plays out: A guest might be perfectly satisfied with your restaurant while preferring three competitors. Their satisfaction tells you relatively little about how much of their business you’ll actually capture. Keiningham’s research helped expose the dangerous assumption that satisfied guests are simultaneously commercially loyal guests. However, restaurant leaders should be equally skeptical of treating share of wallet as the definitive measure of loyalty. The research was conducted before a global pandemic dismantled established dining routines. It was conducted before digital ordering became such a dominant force in restaurant transactions, and before years of inflation fundamentally changed how consumers evaluate everyday purchases. The original principle remains valuable, but the conditions under which guests act on their preferences have changed considerably. And it’s complicated efforts to explain declining restaurant spending through competitive preference alone. Guests Aren’t Necessarily Leaving. They’re Spending Less. According to the National Restaurant Association’s third-quarter 2026 consumer research, 50 percent of consumers reported greater difficulty covering their expenses than a year earlier. Forty percent said they were using more discounts and value promotions than usual. And it’s absolutely showing up in purchasing behavior. To compound the issue, McKinsey’s January 2026 restaurant research found that consumers planning to reduce restaurant spending generally preferred cutting back at their favorite restaurants through smaller orders, cheaper items, or promotions rather than abandoning those restaurants for lower-priced competitors. Suffice to say, the game has changed notably. Here’s how that plays out: A guest who previously visited your restaurant weekly may now visit twice a month. They might skip the appetizer or share an entrée with someone else. Their average check declines, their annual spending falls, and their transaction frequency deteriorates. By all conventional commercial measures, that guest looks less loyal. Yet their preference for your brand may be entirely intact. This is where the distinction between brand preference and economic capacity becomes a noticeable and critical factor. articles.title: Franchise Executive Kendall Ware Releases New Book
articles.titleKo: Franchise Executive Kendall Ware Releases New Book
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . At the center of the book is FranShip, Ware's philosophy that blends strong franchise relationships, genuine partnership and authentic friendship. Franchise brands chase unit growth, while the relationships that make that growth sustainable quietly erode. In his new book, “ Built for Franchising: The Advantage Is FranShip ,” franchise executive Kendall Ware, founder and CEO of FranShip Brands, lays out a blueprint for building franchise systems on partnership instead of transaction, with a foreword by 13-time New York Times bestselling author Don Yaeger. Published by Entrepreneur Books and distributed by Simon & Schuster, the book is now available through national and independent book retailers. Ware argues that the strength of the relationship between franchisor and franchisee is the single biggest variable in whether a brand lasts. Strong products, airtight agreements and large ad budgets cannot make up for a network where trust has broken down. When franchisors serve franchisees so franchisees can better serve guests, and both sides commit to the same goal, the payoff shows up in unit profitability, guest loyalty and long-term brand value. “Most franchise problems look like operations problems, but look closer and you’ll find a relationship that stopped working,” Ware said. “When franchisors and franchisees agree on the destination, which is earning the guest’s next visit, a disagreement becomes a conversation instead of a power struggle.” At the center of the book is FranShip ® , Ware’s philosophy that blends strong franchise relationships, genuine partnership and authentic friendship. The FranShip Framework ® brings it to life through a five-level blueprint modeled on building a house: culturally aligned people as the foundation, operational excellence as the four walls, financial optimization as the ceiling, community marketing as the second story and brand amplification as the roof. Each level spells out what franchisors and franchisees each owe the system, and the first five chapters close with fireside conversations with leading operators, including Greg Flynn of Flynn Group and Cinnabon co-founder Greg Komen. Ware pairs the framework with practical tools. The RETAIN Model™ (recruit, engage, train, assimilate, involve and nurture) gives operators a structure for keeping frontline teams in high-turnover businesses. FEES: Franchisees Expect Exceptional Support ® reframes the most common source of franchise friction, and the 777 Rule shows leaders how to communicate important changes seven times, through seven methods, for seven learning styles. He also makes the case for awarding franchises to aligned operators rather than selling them to anyone with a check. Drawing on more than two decades in franchising, Ware writes from both sides of the table. He started busing tables at 16 and, before turning 35, served as CEO, president or COO of seven brands, including Cinnabon, Carvel, Orange Leaf Frozen Yogurt and Walk-On’s Sports Bistreaux. He has also been a franchisee twice. The book draws on that record, from a Walk-On’s training redesign that saved the average franchisee more than $100,000 in pre-opening payroll to an Orange Leaf turnaround in which initiative adoption rose from 40% to 95% after the team invested in its franchisee relationships. Throughout the book, Ware challenges the assumption that signed agreements and unit counts are the measure of a healthy franchise system. He shows how growth that outruns support leads to closures, how cutting labor to protect margins can shrink revenue and how transparency about failed initiatives builds the credibility that makes the next one succeed. articles.title: Hospitality insolvencies fall as operators cling on for Christmas trading
articles.titleKo: Hospitality insolvencies fall as operators cling on for Christmas trading
articles.originalSummary: Hospitality insolvencies fell by 24% in October, with industry figures suggesting operators are holding on through the final months of the year ahead of the Christmas trading period. The latest company insolvency statistics, published today, show that 210 accommodation and food service businesses entered insolvency in October 2026, down from 275 in September and 32% lower than the 307 recorded in October 2025. Saxon Moseley, partner and head of leisure and hospitality at RSM UK, says the fall suggests operators are holding on through the final months of the year to benefit from festive trading.

articles.title: MOOYAH Introduces 6-STAR Combo
articles.titleKo: MOOYAH Introduces 6-STAR Combo
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . MOOYAH Burgers, Fries & Shakes levels up the burger game. Starting Thursday, Nov. 19, MOOYAH serves up the limited-time 6-STAR Combo, available online only through Nov. 29 at participating restaurants. The 6-STAR Combo features MOOYAH’s Double Classic Combo, with two Certified Angus Beef patties, melted American cheese, fresh toppings stacked on a baked-in-house potato bun, plus Personal Hand-Cut Fries and a regular drink. And this time, there’s more than a delicious meal on the line. Every MOOYAH Rewards member who orders the 6-STAR Combo online while logged in earns a sweepstakes entry for a chance to win a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition console and a digital code for Grand Theft Auto VI. Limit one entry per person per day, regardless of how you enter. “A big game night is basically a holiday for gamers, and nobody should play hungry,” said Stacy Fields, Vice President of Marketing at MOOYAH Burgers, Fries & Shakes. “The 6-STAR Combo fuels those big gaming nights, and one lucky Rewards member walks away with a PlayStation 5 and the most anticipated game of the year. Big burgers, bigger rewards. That’s how we like to celebrate.” Big Burgers. Bigger Rewards. MOOYAH built the 6-STAR Combo for burger lovers and gamers alike, pairing a seriously good burger with a shot at an epic prize. Getting in the game takes three moves. Log in to a MOOYAH Rewards account on the MOOYAH app or at mooyah.com. Order the 6-STAR Combo online from a participating MOOYAH. Score a sweepstakes entry, up to one per person per day. Not a MOOYAH Rewards member yet? Download the MOOYAH app and create an account. Your Next Mission Starts at MOOYAH The 6-STAR Combo is available starting November 19 and runs for just 11 days, making it a limited-time opportunity to satisfy your burger cravings and take a shot at an exciting gaming giveaway. Guests can order online through MOOYAH.com or the MOOYAH Rewards app. The post MOOYAH Introduces 6-STAR Combo appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Burger King is Rebuilding its Restaurants. It Wants Customers to Help Decide Where
articles.titleKo: Burger King is Rebuilding its Restaurants. It Wants Customers to Help Decide Where
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Burger King president Tom Curtis received 120,000 calls and voicemails after posting his phone number in mid-February . Feedback typically unfolded a couple of ways (in addition to a few marriage proposals): Somebody suggested what the chain needed to do. Or, they mentioned the location itself. Curtis found that latter loop difficult to visualize. So, starting in June, he hit the road and asked customers, once again, to be honest about Burger King. Curtis didn’t pick rundown or tired locations off a predetermined map; he randomly walked in and got customers to open up. By now, he had a lot of experience, to put it lightly, in doing so. “A lot of times they would tell you, ‘It doesn’t make me feel good about my community to come here,’” Curtis says in an interview with QSR magazine . “It doesn’t make me feel good about my community to even drive by here. And I just wish that the commitment that you guys had to your menu and your food and your Whopper was matched by your commitment to my community’s sentiment.” “That,” Curtis heard, “would move me the most.” Burger King rolled the tape on Curtis’ road trip and captured experiences for a new campaign launched Tuesday that will place customer responses at the center. In addition to Curtis fielding replies on-site, the brand debuted a “ ReBuildMyBK.com ” website where guests can offer thoughts on their local restaurant and help Burger King pinpoint stores in need of TLC. Burger King president Tom Curtis is taking feedback once again. This time, it’s around the brand’s store assets. And as far as Burger King has come since launching “Reclaim the Flame” in September 2021, this is one corner of its turnaround with whitespace. The brand is about 60 percent into a modern re-image. As of September 30, parent company Restaurant Brands International funded $198 million out of up to $550 million set aside for “Royal Reset” improvements, which include remodels, relocations, restaurant technology kitchen equipment, and building enhancements. Burger King in 2023 unveiled a “Sizzle” design and later developed a catalogue for operators to expand the implementation of the unit’s elements. It’s no grand mystery why Burger King wants to accelerate. Of updated restaurants disclosed via its 2026 FDD, 964 underwent a full remodel and 67 scrape and rebuilds. The average sales uplift was double-digits for each, but north of 25 percent for demolished restaurants. Full remodels appreciated an 11.9 percent average sales uplift, while scrape and rebuilds were at 26 percent. Stores that underwent a conversion to a double drive-thru observed average sales hikes of 16.8 percent (10.6 percent without). And restaurants that fixed from legacy to “modern image” posted average sales growth of 13.8 percent. Units from Burger King’s “20/20 Light” to a new look achieved 10.2 percent. With Sizzle, those garnered upticks of 14.9 percent. Here’s a deeper breakdown . But to Curtis’ point, sentiment can’t always be number crunched. You have to ask people how they feel. Curtis says he heard “good, bad, and otherwise” as he traveled. He witnessed old units. New ones. Sizzles. Upgraded, but not Sizzles. And, naturally, some “really rough” Burger Kings. The campaign chronicled Curtis’ trips to five markets—Columbus, Georgia; Cleveland; Chicago; Phoenix; and Las Vegas. He observed everything, and Curtis was a seasoned listening pro at this point. When Burger King opened Curtis’ hotline last winter, he sat with director of communications Kristen Viersen on the porch of his house and prepared. It was key, he says, to ensure he wouldn’t overpromise and underdeliver. It can be easier to agree with critics than host an open dialogue on what to improve. McDonald’s Brings Home Alone to Life With New Holiday Meal. Whether it’s a spontaneous fry run or the pure joy of scoring a must-have collectible, at McDonald’s, the rules of adulthood take a backseat. It’s the same energy Kevin McCallister embraced when accidentally left behind in 20th Century Studios’ Home Alone . This holiday season, McDonald’s is calling on fans to channel Kevin’s playful nature through the Home Alone Meal featuring limited-time menu items and collectible socks, along with IRL and digital experiences for fans to make the holiday moment their own – available at participating restaurants nationwide starting Dec. 1, while supplies last. THERE’S A LITTLE KEVIN IN ALL OF US The Home Alone Meal turns Kevin’s most memorable movie moments into something fans can taste, collect and make their own. With every specialty meal, fans can unwrap one of four limited-edition, festive collectible socks for a chance to literally walk in Kevin’s footsteps. Featuring designs inspired by iconic characters, scenes and quotes from the film, the collectible socks bring the world of Home Alone to life in a way that’s uniquely McDonald’s. They’re perfect for jumping on beds or keeping cozy during your next holiday feast. And just like Kevin, you make the rules for this meal for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Choose your entree for the Home Alone Meal – from an A.M. Sausage Egg and Cheese McGriddles to a Big Mac. For lunch and dinner, the meal will include limited-time menu items inspired by Kevin’s cravings: Medium Little Nero’s Pizza McShaker Fries: Transform our World Famous Fries® into Kevin’s go-to pizza – plain cheese – with McShaker seasoning featuring notes of tangy tomato, savory garlic, Italian herbs and rich cheese. Simply drop the fries into the McShaker bag, add the seasoning and shake. Lovely Cheese Pizza Dipping Sauce: Drench your meal in this creamy sauce blending rich tomato flavor, warm aged Parmesan cheese, garden herbs and a whisper of garlic. Get it on the side with your Chicken McNuggets or McCrispy Strips or order it a la carte to add extra cheesy goodness to your entree of choice. And in true Kevin fashion, no meal is complete without an over-the-top treat. Introducing: the Everything Sundae McFlurry. Available a la carte, the limited-time McFlurry takes our signature creamy vanilla soft serve and swirls in hot fudge, crunchy pieces of Oreo cookies and colorful M&M’s for an indulgent treat you’ll want all for yourself. “The best McDonald’s moments are the ones our fans make their own,” said Morgan Flatley, Global Chief Marketing Officer and Head of New Business Ventures at McDonald’s and interim U.S. Chief Creative Officer. “Bringing together two icons people already love, McDonald’s and Home Alone , we’re giving fans across the globe a holiday moment to share and celebrate, through nostalgic flavors, collectible keepsakes and the kind of playful experience only McDonald’s can deliver.” DON’T LEAVE THE HOLIDAY FUN BEHIND The Home Alone fun does not stop with the meal. articles.title: GEN Korean BBQ Prepares for Layoffs as it Transitions to CPG Business
articles.titleKo: GEN Korean BBQ Prepares for Layoffs as it Transitions to CPG Business
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . A definitive asset purchase agreement has not been signed, and the final terms are still being negotiated. GEN Korean BBQ plans to dismantle much of the infrastructure it built to support years of restaurant expansion, targeting a 75 percent reduction in corporate overhead. Layoffs are set to begin in the fourth quarter. The sweeping restructuring comes as the company works to sell most of its restaurants and transform itself into a CPG business. The brand eyes a much smaller organization focused on getting Korean barbecue products into grocery stores and American homes. “GEN today carries the corporate structure of a company that was opening 10 restaurants a year. The company we are becoming needs a fraction of that,” chairman and CEO David Kim said during the company’s Q3 earnings call earlier this month. Kim did not specify how many corporate employees would lose their jobs. Some restaurant-support functions are expected to transfer with the locations being sold, and GEN is renegotiating or terminating office leases, systems, and other contracts that will no longer be necessary. “Every role in the new GEN must earn its place by growing CPG or keeping us compliant,” Kim said. The cost-cutting initiative is tied to GEN’s previously announced agreement to sell 47 U.S. restaurants to Chubby Cattle Group for up to $100 million. The companies signed a binding letter of intent in October, outlining a transaction that would transfer restaurant operations and lease obligations to Chubby Cattle over time. A definitive asset purchase agreement has not been signed, and the final terms are still being negotiated. GEN would continue operating each restaurant until its transfer is completed. Under the proposed deal, GEN would retain ownership of its brand, its CPG business, and its restaurant in Cerritos, California, which would support training and product development. The company would also keep its existing 49 percent ownership interest in five Chubby Group restaurants through a separate joint venture. The potential sale represents a dramatic reversal for a chain that previously envisioned an aggressive national expansion. In early 2025, GEN was targeting 75 restaurants by the end of 2026. Its priorities have since shifted as restaurant sales weakened, operating losses mounted, and its retail business gained traction. The financial pressure continued in Q3. Revenue declined 3.3 percent to $48.7 million from $50.4 million a year earlier. Operating losses widened to $6 million from $3.7 million, and the company’s net loss increased to $5.5 million from $3.6 million. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of approximately $600,000, compared with a loss of $200,000 in the prior-year period. GEN also faces a growing debt burden. Total outstanding debt reached $26.8 million at the end of September, up from $14.6 million at the end of 2025. Cash and cash equivalents stood at $2.9 million. The company expects proceeds from the proposed restaurant transaction to help reduce debt. The restructuring would leave GEN with a business that requires significantly less investment in real estate, construction, and restaurant staffing. Its retail products are manufactured through partners in several U.S. states and South Korea, allowing the company to expand production without building its own facilities. GEN is targeting a $40 million annualized CPG revenue run rate by the end of 2027, with Kim suggesting that figure could rise as the company secures additional retail partnerships. The brand’s frozen Korean barbecue meats are already available through retailers including Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Stater Bros., Smart & Final, Save Mart, Bristol Farms, and select Costco regions. articles.title: Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse Unveils Major Expansion
articles.titleKo: Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse Unveils Major Expansion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Family-owned and operated Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse has completed a 5,394-square-foot expansion, bringing its restaurant to nearly 12,000 square feet with redesigned dining areas and event spaces for celebrations, corporate entertaining and social gatherings. Designed to enhance both everyday dining and private events, the expansion allows Galpão Gaucho to welcome more guests, accommodate larger parties and host multiple gatherings simultaneously while preserving the attentive service and warm Southern Brazilian hospitality guests have come to appreciate. The transformation reflects Galpão Gaucho’s continued commitment to the Bay Area and coincides with the brand’s 10th anniversary Year of Celebration, honoring a decade of authentic Southern Brazilian churrasco traditions and memorable experiences shared around the table. “Churrasco has always been about bringing people together,” said Jovani Gava, founder and director of operations at Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse. “In Southern Brazil, meals are social occasions where family and friends gather, conversations flow and hospitality takes center stage. As we celebrate 10 years of Galpão Gaucho, these enhancements allow us to bring even more people together, with spaces that feel just as personal for an intimate dinner as they do for a gathering of a hundred.” Throughout the restaurant, rich wood-paneled walls, statement chandeliers and warm finishes create an inviting atmosphere. Near the piano, signature white leather seating provides a comfortable setting to enjoy dinner, cocktails and live music. The new private and semi-private dining areas feature sleek upholstered chairs in contrasting shades of brown and black, offering added comfort for business meetings, corporate events and celebrations. The restaurant now offers five private dining and event spaces accommodating groups of 10 to 100 guests. Glass partitions, floor-to-ceiling curtains and flexible room configurations allow for gatherings of varying sizes, including one space that converts from two private rooms into a single venue. Long banquet-style tables, complimentary audiovisual capabilities and large-screen TVs support everything from executive meetings and presentations to rehearsal dinners and holiday parties. At the heart of the expansion remains Galpão Gaucho’s signature rodizio experience, where gaucho chefs continuously carve 17 selections from the grill tableside. Guests also enjoy a gourmet salad bar featuring more than 45 offerings, Brazilian-inspired specialties, signature side dishes, handcrafted desserts and a curated wine program. For private events, hosts can tailor beverage service to their gathering by preselecting wine bottles or wines by the glass, limiting selections to signature cocktails or standard-tier drinks – or setting a designated number of drinks per guest. Through December 31, 2026, qualifying private dining and event reservations are eligible for exclusive Year of Celebration rewards for both organizers and attendees. Details and eligibility requirements are available on the Year of Celebration page. For more information or to reserve a private dining experience, corporate event or celebration, visit GalpaoGauchoUSA.com. articles.titleKo: Latest opening: Tattu Canary Wharf
articles.originalSummary: Permanently Unique Group has brought its Tattu restaurant to Canary Wharf, marking the brand’s second London opening with a new waterfront location. The top line: Tattu, part of Permanently Unique Group, has opened its new Canary Wharf restaurant, joining its original London site in Soho. The restaurant is led by global executive chef Eugene Papadimitriou, who trained at Le Cordon Bleu before progressing through the ranks at Tattu.
